3.47.m:
A king is not defiled, nor is wind defiled, O best of the twice-born, nor indeed are flies; / and that which is unseen is declared undefiled, as are the rays of light that are seen.
3.232 / Haṃsa said: / Ritual impurity due to death is prescribed for ten days among sapiṇḍas / for a brahmin, O best of the twice-born; twelve days for a king [kṣatriya];
a fortnight is prescribed for a vaiśya, and a month for a śūdra, / both at birth and at death, for those desiring purity according to rule.
At the end of the first [period], complete purity is attained for an equal, O best of the twice-born; / and at the end of the second, it is always known to be for an unequal.
If within the ten days one hears of a death or a birth, / one remains impure only for whatever is left of the ten nights.
If the ten nights have passed, but within a year, / purification is ordained after three nights; but beyond that, upon merely bathing.
In the case of a miscarriage, purification takes as many nights as the months [of pregnancy]. / Up to the appearance of teeth, it is immediate; up to tonsure, it is one day and night;

three nights until the investiture of vows; beyond that, ten nights. / For girls, marriage is declared to take the place of the vows.
When they are married, no ritual impurity is prescribed on the father’s side. / For a maternal grandfather it is three nights; and for wives who have gone to another,
and for remarried women belonging to oneself, and for sons gone to another [caste or adopted], / and when a teacher has died, or the king of one's dwelling-land,
for the teacher’s wife and sons, for a pupil, and for fellow students, / ritual impurity lasts one night, and likewise when one who provides food has died.
For suicides killed by falling from a cliff, fire, starvation, or water, / and for outcasts, there is no ritual impurity; nor for those struck down by lightning or weapons.
Artisans, vow-keepers, students, the king’s treasury officials, and consecrated sacrificers / are declared not subject to ritual impurity, as are those executing the king’s command.
For an expired śūdra, after one year, purification is held [to take] five days; / purification takes twelve days when three years have elapsed;
when six years have passed, it is declared to take a month. / On following a corpse, bathing and consuming clarified butter bring purification.

3.47.m:
Through the ten days of birth and death, there is no rite of purity, nor food to be offered to brahmins; / nor is there any fault in acceptance of gifts when the sacrificial fees consist of bipeds, quadrupeds, or grain.
3.233 / Haṃsa said: / The sacred part for the gods is considered to be at the tips of the fingers; that for the ancestors is at the base of the forefinger; / that for Brahmā is at the base of the thumb; and that for men is at the little finger.
One should sip water using the Brahmā part, gratify the gods with the divine part, / gratify the ancestors with the ancestral part, O knower of dharma, and likewise drink with the human part.
During the unalterable silent prayer, and likewise during sacrificing for oneself and officiating for others, / and during teaching and studying, a man must not be distracted in mind.
In these very duties and in the presence of teachers, / one should uncover the right hand and should not wear sandals.
The fire rite, the rite to the gods, ritual sipping, / dining, and the ancestral rite one should not perform with knees exposed.
One should never pronounce the name of an initiated person here, O sages; / nor should the teacher's name alone ever be uttered.

yācamānaṃ yathāśaktyā na kuryādvimukhaṃ kvacit ..
daivaṃ pūrvāhṇikaṃ kāryaṃ tvaparāhṇe tu paitṛkam .. 7 ..
atithīnāṃ tathā pūjā sarvakālaṃ vidhīyate ..
yadviśiṣṭatamaṃ loke yaccāsti dayitaṃ gṛhe .. 8 ..
tattadguṇavate deyaṃ tadevākṣayamicchatā ..
priyāṇi labhate loke priyadaḥ priyakṛttathā .. 9 ..
pratiśrutaṃ prayatnena dātavyamṛṣisattamāḥ ..
aprayacchaṃstadāpnoti mūrtīṣṭakṛtasaṃśayam .. 3.233.10 ..
narakaṃ mahadāpnoti śṛgālaścaiva jāyate ..
mātā pitā guruścaiva jyeṣṭho bhrātā tathā svasā .. 11 ..
pitṛvyo mātulaścaiva tathā mātṛṣvasā dvijāḥ ..
pitṛṣvasā tathā śvaśrūrgurubhāryā tathaiva ca.. .. 12 ..
mātāmahaśca śvaśuraḥ pūjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ ..
pratyutthānaśca kartavyaṃ teṣāṃ pūrvābhivādanam .. 13 ..
3.47.d:
याचमानं यथाशक्त्या न कुर्याद्विमुखं क्वचित् ॥
दैवं पूर्वाह्णिकं कार्यं त्वपराह्णे तु पैतृकम् ॥ 7 ॥
अतिथीनां तथा पूजा सर्वकालं विधीयते ॥
यद्विशिष्टतमं लोके यच्चास्ति दयितं गृहे ॥ 8 ॥
तत्तद्गुणवते देयं तदेवाक्षयमिच्छता ॥
प्रियाणि लभते लोके प्रियदः प्रियकृत्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
प्रतिश्रुतं प्रयत्नेन दातव्यमृषिसत्तमाः ॥
अप्रयच्छंस्तदाप्नोति मूर्तीष्टकृतसंशयम् ॥ 3.233.10 ॥
नरकं महदाप्नोति शृगालश्चैव जायते ॥
माता पिता गुरुश्चैव ज्येष्ठो भ्राता तथा स्वसा ॥ 11 ॥
पितृव्यो मातुलश्चैव तथा मातृष्वसा द्विजाः ॥
पितृष्वसा तथा श्वश्रूर्गुरुभार्या तथैव च॥ ॥ 12 ॥
मातामहश्च श्वशुरः पूजनीयाः प्रयत्नतः ॥
प्रत्युत्थानश्च कर्तव्यं तेषां पूर्वाभिवादनम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.47.m:
One should never turn away a petitioner according to one's capacity; / the rite for gods belongs to the morning, but that for ancestors to the afternoon.
Likewise, the honoring of guests is prescribed at all times; / whatever is most excellent in the world and whatever is cherished in the home,
all that should be given to the virtuous by one desiring it to be inexhaustible; / one who gives pleasant things and does pleasant things obtains pleasant things in this world.
What has been promised must be given with effort, O best of sages; / not giving it, he incurs uncertainty regarding what was offered to the deities;
he goes to a terrible hell and is reborn as a jackal. / Mother, father, teacher, elder brother, and sister,
paternal uncle, maternal uncle, and maternal aunt, O twice-born, / paternal aunt, mother-in-law, and teacher's wife likewise,
maternal grandfather, and father-in-law should be honored with effort; / one must rise up to greet them and offer obeisance first.

3.47.s:
mātulaśca pitṛvyaśca yadā syātāṃ kanī yasau ..
nābhivādyāstu te pūrvaṃ pratyutthānaṃ tu kārayet .. 14 ..
ucchiṣṭo na spṛśecchīrṣaṃ sarve prāṇāstadāśrayāḥ ..
pūrvāṃ sandhyāṃ japaṃstiṣṭhedāsīnaścaiva paścimām .. 15 ..
3.47.d:
मातुलश्च पितृव्यश्च यदा स्यातां कनी यसौ ॥
नाभिवाद्यास्तु ते पूर्वं प्रत्युत्थानं तु कारयेत् ॥ 14 ॥
उच्छिष्टो न स्पृशेच्छीर्षं सर्वे प्राणास्तदाश्रयाः ॥
पूर्वां सन्ध्यां जपंस्तिष्ठेदासीनश्चैव पश्चिमाम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.47.m:
When a maternal uncle and a paternal uncle are younger, / they should not be saluted first, but one should rise up to greet them.
One who is impure with food residue should not touch his head, for all the vital breaths reside there; / one should remain standing while reciting the morning twilight devotion, and seated during the evening one.

3.47.s:
madhyandine niśākāle tvardharātre viśeṣataḥ ..
catuṣpathaṃ na seveta upasandhye tathaiva ca .. 16 ..
3.47.d:
मध्यन्दिने निशाकाले त्वर्धरात्रे विशेषतः ॥
चतुष्पथं न सेवेत उपसन्ध्ये तथैव च ॥ 16 ॥
3.47.m: At midday, at night, and especially at midnight, / and likewise at the two twilights, one should not resort to a crossroads.

3.47.s:
nāstikyaṃ vedanindāñca devatānāñca kutsanam ..
dveṣastambhātimānau ca taikṣṇyaṃ caiva vivarjayeta .. 17 ..
3.47.d:
नास्तिक्यं वेदनिन्दाञ्च देवतानाञ्च कुत्सनम् ॥
द्वेषस्तम्भातिमानौ च तैक्ष्ण्यं चैव विवर्जयेत ॥ 17 ॥
3.47.m: Atheism, abuse of the Vedas, reviling the deities, / malice, obstinacy, excessive pride, and harshness one must avoid.

3.47.s:
parasya daṇḍaṃ nodyacchetkruddho nainaṃ nipātayet ..
anyatra putrācchiṣyādvā śiṣṭyarthaṃ tāḍanaṃ smṛtam .. 18 ..
3.47.d:
परस्य दण्डं नोद्यच्छेत्क्रुद्धो नैनं निपातयेत् ॥
अन्यत्र पुत्राच्छिष्याद्वा शिष्ट्यर्थं ताडनं स्मृतम् ॥ 18 ॥
3.47.m: One should not raise a staff against another, nor let it fall in anger; / except in the case of a son or a pupil, striking is taught for instruction alone.

3.47.s:
na brāhmaṇaṃ parivadennakṣatrāṇi na nirdiśet ..
tithiṃ pakṣasya na brūyāttathāsyāyurna riṣyate .. 19 ..
3.47.d:
न ब्राह्मणं परिवदेन्नक्षत्राणि न निर्दिशेत् ॥
तिथिं पक्षस्य न ब्रूयात्तथास्यायुर्न रिष्यते ॥ 19 ॥
3.47.m: One should not revile a brahmin, nor point out the lunar mansions; / one should not announce the lunar day of a fortnight; thus one's life is not impaired.

3.47.s:
prāgastaśāyī na bhavenna cābhyudayaśāyikaḥ ..
avalokyo na cādarśo malino buddhimattaraiḥ .. 3.233.20 ..
3.47.d:
प्रागस्तशायी न भवेन्न चाभ्युदयशायिकः ॥
अवलोक्यो न चादर्शो मलिनो बुद्धिमत्तरैः ॥ 3.233.20 ॥
3.47.m: One should not be asleep before sunset nor asleep at sunrise; / and a dirty mirror should not be looked into by the truly wise.

3.47.s:
akṛtvā devatāpūjāṃ nānyaṃ gacchetkadācana ..
anyatra tu guruṃ vṛddhaṃ dhārmikaṃ vā vicakṣaṇam..21..
3.47.d:
अकृत्वा देवतापूजां नान्यं गच्छेत्कदाचन ॥
अन्यत्र तु गुरुं वृद्धं धार्मिकं वा विचक्षणम्॥21॥
3.47.m: Without having performed worship of the deities, one should never visit another; / except indeed a teacher, an elder, a righteous man, or a sage.

3.47.s:
varjayecca tathā prājñāścāsanākarṣaṇaṃ sadā ..
snātvā tu nāvamājeta gātrāṇi tu vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 22..
3.47.d:
वर्जयेच्च तथा प्राज्ञाश्चासनाकर्षणं सदा ॥
स्नात्वा तु नावमाजेत गात्राणि तु विचक्षणः ॥ 22॥
3.47.m: The wise should always avoid dragging a seat; / having bathed, a discerning person should not wipe his limbs.

3.47.s:
viparyayaṃ na kurvīta vāsaso buddhimānnaraḥ ..
tathā nānyadhṛtaṃ dhāryaṃ na cāpadaśameva ca .. 23 ..
3.47.d:
विपर्ययं न कुर्वीत वाससो बुद्धिमान्नरः ॥
तथा नान्यधृतं धार्यं न चापदशमेव च ॥ 23 ॥
3.47.m: A wise man should not reverse his garments; / nor should one wear clothes worn by another, nor one without a hem.

3.47.s:
anyadeva bhavedvāsaḥ śayanīye dvijottamāḥ ..
anyadrathyāsu devānāṃ tvarcāyāmanyadeva tu .. 24 ..
3.47.d:
अन्यदेव भवेद्वासः शयनीये द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
अन्यद्रथ्यासु देवानां त्वर्चायामन्यदेव तु ॥ 24 ॥
3.47.m: One garment should be worn for sleeping, O best of twice-born, / another on the streets, and yet another during worship of the gods.

3.47.s:
upavāsaṃ tu kurvīta snātaḥ śuciralaṃkṛtaḥ ..
parvakāleṣu sarveṣu brahmacārī tathā bhavet .. 25 ..
3.47.d:
उपवासं तु कुर्वीत स्नातः शुचिरलंकृतः ॥
पर्वकालेषु सर्वेषु ब्रह्मचारी तथा भवेत् ॥ 25 ॥
3.47.m: Having bathed, being pure and adorned, one should observe a fast; / during all junction times one should likewise remain celibate.

3.47.s:
pippalaṃ ca vaṭañcaiva śaṇaśākaṃ tathaiva ca ..
udumbaraṃ na khādeta bhavyārthī puruṣaḥ sadā ..26 ..
3.47.d:
पिप्पलं च वटञ्चैव शणशाकं तथैव च ॥
उदुम्बरं न खादेत भव्यार्थी पुरुषः सदा ॥26 ॥
3.47.m: A man seeking prosperity should never eat / pippala, vaṭa, hemp-greens, and udumbara.

3.47.s:
putramāṃsopamaṃ māṃsaṃ pṛṣṭhamāṃsaṃ ca varjayet ..
pāṇau ca lavaṇaṃ rātrau dadhisaktūṃstathaiva ca .. 27 ..
3.47.d:
पुत्रमांसोपमं मांसं पृष्ठमांसं च वर्जयेत् ॥
पाणौ च लवणं रात्रौ दधिसक्तूंस्तथैव च ॥ 27 ॥
3.47.m: Meat akin to one's son's flesh and meat from the back [of an animal] one should avoid; / and salt held in the hand, and at night, yogurt and roasted barley flour.

3.47.s:
sāyaṃ prātaśca bhuñjīta nāntarāle kadācana ..
sāyaṃ prātarmanuṣyāṇāmaśanaṃ devanirmitam .. 28 ..
3.47.d:
सायं प्रातश्च भुञ्जीत नान्तराले कदाचन ॥
सायं प्रातर्मनुष्याणामशनं देवनिर्मितम् ॥ 28 ॥
3.47.m: One should eat in the evening and in the morning, and never in between; / morning and evening meals were established by the gods for men.

3.47.s:
bhūmau sadaiva cāśnīyānna cāsīno ca śabdavat ..
toyapūrṇaṃ yadā pānamatithibhyo dvijottamāḥ .. 29 ..
3.47.d:
भूमौ सदैव चाश्नीयान्न चासीनो च शब्दवत् ॥
तोयपूर्णं यदा पानमतिथिभ्यो द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 29 ॥
3.47.m: One should always eat on the ground, not seated [haphazardly], and without making noise; / when drink filled with water [is served] to guests, O best of twice-born,

3.47.s:
paścādbhuñjīta medhāvī na cāpyanyamanā naraḥ ..
na dhāvedvarṣamāṇe tu nadīṃ mattāṃ na laṅghayet ..3.233.30..
3.47.d:
पश्चाद्भुञ्जीत मेधावी न चाप्यन्यमना नरः ॥
न धावेद्वर्षमाणे तु नदीं मत्तां न लङ्घयेत् ॥3.233.30॥
3.47.m: the wise man should eat afterwards, without being distracted; / one should not run while it is raining, nor cross a raging river.

3.47.s:
gāṃ carantīṃ pibantañca vatsakaṃ na niṣedhayeta ..
samānamekapaṅktyāṃ tu deyamannaṃ tathā bhavet..31..
3.47.d:
गां चरन्तीं पिबन्तञ्च वत्सकं न निषेधयेत ॥
समानमेकपङ्क्त्यां तु देयमन्नं तथा भवेत्॥31॥
3.47.m: One should not prevent a cow while grazing or a calf while drinking; / in a single row [of diners], equal food should be given.

3.47.s:
paṅktyāntu viṣamaṃ dattvā narakaṃ pratipadyate ..
viṣaṃ hālāhalaṃ bhuṅkte yo pradāya suhṛjjane .. 32 ..
3.47.d:
पङ्क्त्यान्तु विषमं दत्त्वा नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
विषं हालाहलं भुङ्क्ते यो प्रदाय सुहृज्जने ॥ 32 ॥
3.47.m: By giving unequally in a row [of diners], one falls into hell; / he who [eats] without giving to his friends eats deadly hālāhala poison.

3.47.s:
loṣṭhamardī tṛṇacchedī nakhakhādī ca yo naraḥ ..
nityocchiṣṭo bhavedyaḥ sa nehāyurvindate mahat .. 33 ..
3.47.d:
लोष्ठमर्दी तृणच्छेदी नखखादी च यो नरः ॥
नित्योच्छिष्टो भवेद्यः स नेहायुर्विन्दते महत् ॥ 33 ॥
3.47.m: A man who crushes clods of earth, cuts grass, or bites his nails, / and who is constantly impure with food residue, does not attain a long life here.

3.47.s:
paraṃ jñeyamanāyuṣyaṃ paradārābhimarśanam ..
udakyāgamanaṃ jñeyamalaṃghyaṃ paramaṃ sukham .. 34 ..
3.47.d:
परं ज्ञेयमनायुष्यं परदाराभिमर्शनम् ॥
उदक्यागमनं ज्ञेयमलंघ्यं परमं सुखम् ॥ 34 ॥
3.47.m: Touching another man's wife is to be known as utterly shortening life; / intercourse with a menstruating woman is to be known [as forbidden]; [righteous conduct] is an unassailable supreme happiness.

3.47.s:
purīṣamūtre nodīkṣennādhitiṣṭhetkadācana ..
udakyayā tu saṃbhāṣāṃ na tu kurvīta karhicit .. 35 ..
3.47.d:
पुरीषमूत्रे नोदीक्षेन्नाधितिष्ठेत्कदाचन ॥
उदक्यया तु संभाषां न तु कुर्वीत कर्हिचित् ॥ 35 ॥
3.47.m: One should not look at feces and urine, nor ever stand upon them; / and one should never converse with a menstruating woman.

3.47.s:
nādhitiṣṭhettuṣaṃ jātu keśabhasmakapālikāḥ ..
anyasya cāpyupasthānaṃ dūrataḥ parivarjayet .. 36 ..
3.47.d:
नाधितिष्ठेत्तुषं जातु केशभस्मकपालिकाः ॥
अन्यस्य चाप्युपस्थानं दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 36 ॥
3.47.m: One should never step upon chaff, hair, ashes, or potsherds; / and one should avoid from afar the toilet of another.

3.47.s:
trīṇi tejāṃsi nocchiṣṭo nālabheta kadācana ..
agniṃ gāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ caiva tathā hyāyurna riṣyate .. 37 ..
3.47.d:
त्रीणि तेजांसि नोच्छिष्टो नालभेत कदाचन ॥
अग्निं गां ब्राह्मणं चैव तथा ह्यायुर्न रिष्यते ॥ 37 ॥
3.47.m: Impure with food residue, one should never touch three splendors: / fire, a cow, and a brahmin; thus indeed life is not impaired.

3.47.s:
trīṇi tejāṃsi cocchiṣṭo nodīkṣeta kadācana ..
sūryācandramasau caiva nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvaśaḥ .. 38 ..
3.47.d:
त्रीणि तेजांसि चोच्छिष्टो नोदीक्षेत कदाचन ॥
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ चैव नक्षत्राणि च सर्वशः ॥ 38 ॥
3.47.m: Impure with food residue, one should never look upon three splendors: / the sun and the moon, and all the lunar mansions.

3.47.s:
nāvamanyeta dharmajña trīṇi tejāṃsi paṇḍitaḥ ..
agniṃ ca kulaputraṃ ca brāhmaṇañca dvijottamāḥ .. 39 ..
3.47.d:
नावमन्येत धर्मज्ञ त्रीणि तेजांसि पण्डितः ॥
अग्निं च कुलपुत्रं च ब्राह्मणञ्च द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 39 ॥
3.47.m: O knower of dharma, a wise man should not show disrespect to three splendors: / fire, a man of noble family, and a brahmin, O best of twice-born.

3.47.s:
trīnkṛśānnāvajānīyāddīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ ..
brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ sarpaṃ sarve hyāśīviṣāstrayaḥ .. 3.233.40 ..
3.47.d:
त्रीन्कृशान्नावजानीयाद्दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः ॥
ब्राह्मणं क्षत्रियं सर्पं सर्वे ह्याशीविषास्त्रयः ॥ 3.233.40 ॥
3.47.m: One who desires to live a long life should not despise three [even when] weak: / a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a serpent; for all three possess virulent venom.

3.47.s:
nādhyāpayedathocchiṣṭo nādhīyīta kadācana ..
sarvaṃ ca tilasaṃbaddhannādyādastamite ravau .. 41 ..
3.47.d:
नाध्यापयेदथोच्छिष्टो नाधीयीत कदाचन ॥
सर्वं च तिलसंबद्धन्नाद्यादस्तमिते रवौ ॥ 41 ॥
3.47.m: Impure with food residue, one should not teach nor ever study; / and one should not eat anything mixed with sesame when the sun has set.

3.47.s:
ūrdhvaprāṇā hyutkramanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati ..
pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastānpratipadyate .. 42 ..
3.47.d:
ऊर्ध्वप्राणा ह्युत्क्रमन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति ॥
प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान्प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 42 ॥
3.47.m: The vital breaths of a youth rise upward when an elder arrives; / through rising up and greeting respectfully, he regains them.

3.47.s:
abhivādayeta vṛddhāṃśca āsanaṃ caiva dāpayet ..
kṛtāñjalirupāsīta gacchataḥ pṛṣṭhato'nviyāt .. 43 ..
3.47.d:
अभिवादयेत वृद्धांश्च आसनं चैव दापयेत् ॥
कृताञ्जलिरुपासीत गच्छतः पृष्ठतोऽन्वियात् ॥ 43 ॥
3.47.m: One should salute elders and offer them a seat; / with folded hands one should attend them, and follow behind when they walk.

3.47.s:
nāsīta cāsane bhinne bhinnaṃ kāsyaṃ ca varjayet ..
naikavastreṇa bhoktavyaṃ na nagnaḥ snānamarhati .. 44 ..
3.47.d:
नासीत चासने भिन्ने भिन्नं कास्यं च वर्जयेत् ॥
नैकवस्त्रेण भोक्तव्यं न नग्नः स्नानमर्हति ॥ 44 ॥
3.47.m: One should not sit on a broken seat, and one should avoid broken bell-metal; / one should not dine in a single garment, nor ought one to bathe naked.

3.47.s:
guruṇā vairanirbandho na karttavyaḥ kadācana ..
anumānyaḥ prasādyaśca guruḥ kruddho vijānatā .. 45 ..
3.47.d:
गुरुणा वैरनिर्बन्धो न कर्त्तव्यः कदाचन ॥
अनुमान्यः प्रसाद्यश्च गुरुः क्रुद्धो विजानता ॥ 45 ॥
3.47.m: One should never persist in enmity toward a teacher; / an angry teacher should be conciliated and propitiated by one who understands.

3.47.s:
dūrādāvasathānmūtraṃ dūrādātmāvasecanam ..
ucchiṣṭonmārjanaṃ caiva dūrātkāryaṃ vijānatā .. 46 ..
3.47.d:
दूरादावसथान्मूत्रं दूरादात्मावसेचनम् ॥
उच्छिष्टोन्मार्जनं चैव दूरात्कार्यं विजानता ॥ 46 ॥
3.47.m: Urinating far from the dwelling, washing oneself far off, / and clearing food residue far away should be done by one who understands.

3.47.s:
upānaho ca vastraṃ ca dhṛtamanyairna dhārayet ..
pādaṃ pādena nākrāmenna kaṇḍūyena śaucayet .. 47 ..
3.47.d:
उपानहो च वस्त्रं च धृतमन्यैर्न धारयेत् ॥
पादं पादेन नाक्रामेन्न कण्डूयेन शौचयेत् ॥ 47 ॥
3.47.m: One should not wear shoes or clothing worn by others; / one should not step on one foot with the other, nor scratch it, nor wash it [with the other foot].

3.47.s:
hīnāṅgānatiriktāṅgānvidyāhīnānvigarhitān ..
rūpadraviṇahīnāṃśca sattvahīnāṃśca nākṣipet .. 48 ..
3.47.d:
हीनाङ्गानतिरिक्ताङ्गान्विद्याहीनान्विगर्हितान् ॥
रूपद्रविणहीनांश्च सत्त्वहीनांश्च नाक्षिपेत् ॥ 48 ॥
3.47.m: One should not insult those who lack limbs or have extra limbs, those devoid of learning, those who are censured, / those who lack beauty and wealth, or those who lack strength.

3.47.s:
bhuñjāno brāhmaṇaśreṣṭho naiva śaṅkāṃ samācaret ..
dadhi cāpyanupānaṃ ca na karttavyaṃ bhavārthinā .. 49 ..
3.47.d:
भुञ्जानो ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठो नैव शङ्कां समाचरेत् ॥
दधि चाप्यनुपानं च न कर्त्तव्यं भवार्थिना ॥ 49 ॥
3.47.m: While eating, an excellent brahmin should never harbor doubt; / nor should one who desires prosperity consume curds as a drink after eating.

3.47.s:
ācamya caiva hastena parisrāvyaṃ tathodakam ..
aṅguṣṭhacaraṇasyāgre dakṣiṇasya tathopari .. 3.233.50 ..
3.47.d:
आचम्य चैव हस्तेन परिस्राव्यं तथोदकम् ॥
अङ्गुष्ठचरणस्याग्रे दक्षिणस्य तथोपरि ॥ 3.233.50 ॥
3.47.m: And after sipping water, water should be poured with the hand / upon the tip of the big toe of the right foot.

3.47.s:
parāpavādaṃ na brūyānnāpriyaśca kadācana ..
na manyuḥ kasyacitkāryaḥ kadācidapi vai dvijaḥ .. 51 ..
3.47.d:
परापवादं न ब्रूयान्नाप्रियश्च कदाचन ॥
न मन्युः कस्यचित्कार्यः कदाचिदपि वै द्विजः ॥ 51 ॥
3.47.m: One should never speak censure of another, nor what is unpleasant; / indeed, twice-born, anger should never be directed against anyone.

3.47.s:
homaścānudite sūrye dātavyo dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
tāvadbhavati vahnistho yāvannodeti bhāskaraḥ .. 52 ..
3.47.d:
होमश्चानुदिते सूर्ये दातव्यो द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
तावद्भवति वह्निस्थो यावन्नोदेति भास्करः ॥ 52 ॥
3.47.m: And the fire offering must be offered before the sun has risen, O best of the twice-born; / it remains within fire as long as the sun does not rise.

3.47.s:
parīpsitaṃ ca vahnisthaḥ samyagdattāmathāhutim ..
tadā bhāsayate sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 53 ..
3.47.d:
परीप्सितं च वह्निस्थः सम्यग्दत्तामथाहुतिम् ॥
तदा भासयते सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 53 ॥
3.47.m: Remaining in the fire, having received the properly offered oblation, / it then illuminates all the three worlds together with the moving and unmoving.

3.47.s:
patitaistu kathāṃ neccheddarśanaṃ cāpi varjayet ..
saṃsargaṃ na ca gacchettu tathāsyāyurna riṣyate .. 54 ..
3.47.d:
पतितैस्तु कथां नेच्छेद्दर्शनं चापि वर्जयेत् ॥
संसर्गं न च गच्छेत्तु तथास्यायुर्न रिष्यते ॥ 54 ॥
3.47.m: One should not desire conversation with fallen persons, and one should avoid even seeing them; / one should not associate [with them]—thus one's lifespan is not harmed.

3.47.s:
vṛddho jñātistathā mitraṃ daridraṃ ca kulodgatam ..
gṛhe vāsayitavyāni dhanyāni munisattamāḥ .. 55 ..
3.47.d:
वृद्धो ज्ञातिस्तथा मित्रं दरिद्रं च कुलोद्गतम् ॥
गृहे वासयितव्यानि धन्यानि मुनिसत्तमाः ॥ 55 ॥
3.47.m: An elder, a kinsman, a friend, and an impoverished man of noble birth— / these fortunate persons should be sheltered in the home, O best of sages.

3.47.s:
brāhmaṇasya padābhyāṃ tu vasetpūjitamālayam ...
sandhyāsvadhyayanaṃ varjyaṃ bhojanaṃ svapanakriyā .. 56 ..
3.47.d:
ब्राह्मणस्य पदाभ्यां तु वसेत्पूजितमालयम् ॥।
सन्ध्यास्वध्ययनं वर्ज्यं भोजनं स्वपनक्रिया ॥ 56 ॥
3.47.m: A dwelling honored by the feet of a brahmin should be inhabited. / At the twilights, study, eating, and sleeping are to be avoided.

3.47.s:
naktaṃ na kuryātpitryāṇi bhuktvā caiva prasādhanam ..
pānīyasya kriyā naktaṃ na kāryā bhūtimicchatā .. 57 ..
3.47.d:
नक्तं न कुर्यात्पित्र्याणि भुक्त्वा चैव प्रसाधनम् ॥
पानीयस्य क्रिया नक्तं न कार्या भूतिमिच्छता ॥ 57 ॥
3.47.m: One should not perform ancestral rites at night, nor adorn oneself after eating; / an action with water at night should not be performed by one desiring prosperity.

3.47.s: animantrito na gacchettu yajñaṃ gacchettu darśakaḥ .. 58..
3.47.d: अनिमन्त्रितो न गच्छेत्तु यज्ञं गच्छेत्तु दर्शकः ॥ 58॥
3.47.m: Uninvited, one should not go to a sacrifice; but one may go as a spectator.

3.47.s:
caritāni purāṇānāṃ śrotavyāni punaḥpunaḥ ..
śrutismṛtyuditaṃ dharmaṃ tvanutiṣṭhettathā sadā .. 59 ..
3.47.d:
चरितानि पुराणानां श्रोतव्यानि पुनःपुनः ॥
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितं धर्मं त्वनुतिष्ठेत्तथा सदा ॥ 59 ॥
3.47.m: The deeds of the Purāṇas should be heard again and again; / and one should always follow the dharma spoken of in the Śruti and the Smṛti.

3.47.s: sukhī syāttatprasaktastu iha loke paratra ca .. 3.233.60 ..
3.47.d: सुखी स्यात्तत्प्रसक्तस्तु इह लोके परत्र च ॥ 3.233.60 ॥
3.47.m: One devoted to that will be happy both in this world and in the next.

3.47.s:
śrutistu vedo vijñeyo dharmaśāstraṃ tathā smṛtiḥ .
te sarvārtheṣu mīmāṃsye tābhyāṃ dharmo hi nirbabhau .. 61 ..
3.47.d:
श्रुतिस्तु वेदो विज्ञेयो धर्मशास्त्रं तथा स्मृतिः ।
ते सर्वार्थेषु मीमांस्ये ताभ्यां धर्मो हि निर्बभौ ॥ 61 ॥
3.47.m: Śruti is known as the Veda, and Smṛti as the Dharmaśāstra; / they must be examined in all matters, for from them dharma shone forth.

3.47.s:
yo'vamanyeta bhūtebhyo hetuśāstrāśrayāddvijāḥ ..
sādhubhiḥ sa bahiṣkāryo narakāgnestu bhājanam .. 62..
3.47.d:
योऽवमन्येत भूतेभ्यो हेतुशास्त्राश्रयाद्द्विजाः ॥
साधुभिः स बहिष्कार्यो नरकाग्नेस्तु भाजनम् ॥ 62॥
3.47.m: He who would disrespect [them] among living beings by relying on dialectical scriptures, O twice-born, / should be cast out by the virtuous, a receptacle for the fire of hell.

3.47.s:
vedaḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāraḥ svasya ca priyamātmanaḥ ..
etaccaturvidhaṃ prāhuḥ sādhūnāṃ dharmalakṣaṇam ..63..
3.47.d:
वेदः स्मृतिः सदाचारः स्वस्य च प्रियमात्मनः ॥
एतच्चतुर्विधं प्राहुः साधूनां धर्मलक्षणम् ॥63॥
3.47.m: The Veda, the Smṛti, the conduct of the virtuous, and what is pleasing to oneself— / they declare this to be the fourfold definition of dharma for the good.

3.47.s:
cāturvarṇyavyavasthānaṃ yasmindeśe na vidyate ..
sa mlecchaviṣayo jñeya āryāvarttamataḥ param ..64..
3.47.d:
चातुर्वर्ण्यव्यवस्थानं यस्मिन्देशे न विद्यते ॥
स म्लेच्छविषयो ज्ञेय आर्यावर्त्तमतः परम् ॥64॥
3.47.m: The country in which the order of the four classes does not exist / is to be known as the land of barbarians; beyond that is Āryāvarta.

3.47.s:
sarasvatīdṛṣadvatyordevanadyoryadantaram ..
taṃ devavihitaṃ deśaṃ brahmāvartaṃ pracakṣate .. 65 ..
3.47.d:
सरस्वतीदृषद्वत्योर्देवनद्योर्यदन्तरम् ॥
तं देवविहितं देशं ब्रह्मावर्तं प्रचक्षते ॥ 65 ॥
3.47.m: The land between the two divine rivers, the Sarasvatī and the Dṛṣadvatī, / established by the gods, they call Brahmāvarta.

3.47.s:
yasmindeśe ya ācāraḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ ..
varṇānāṃ sāntarālānāṃ sa sadācāra ucyate .. 66 ..
3.47.d:
यस्मिन्देशे य आचारः पारम्पर्यक्रमागतः ॥
वर्णानां सान्तरालानां स सदाचार उच्यते ॥ 66 ॥
3.47.m: The custom that has descended in succession from antiquity in that country / among the classes and the intermediate ones is called the conduct of the virtuous.

3.47.s:
vaidikaiḥ karmabhiḥ puṇyairniṣekādirdvijanmanām ..
kāryāḥ śarīrasaṃskārāḥ pāvanāḥ pretya ceha ca..67..
3.47.d:
वैदिकैः कर्मभिः पुण्यैर्निषेकादिर्द्विजन्मनाम् ॥
कार्याः शरीरसंस्काराः पावनाः प्रेत्य चेह च॥67॥
3.47.m: By means of meritorious Vedic rites beginning with the rite of impregnation, / bodily sacraments are to be performed for the twice-born, purifying both in the next world and in this one.

3.47.s:
gārbhaiḥ kṛtyairjātakarmacaulamauñjīnibaṃdhanaiḥ ..
vaijikaṃ gārbhikaṃ caino dvijānāmapahanyate .. 68 ..
3.47.d:
गार्भैः कृत्यैर्जातकर्मचौलमौञ्जीनिबंधनैः ॥
वैजिकं गार्भिकं चैनो द्विजानामपहन्यते ॥ 68 ॥
3.47.m: Through rites of the womb, the birth rite, tonsure, and the tying of the muñja girdle, / the sin derived from seed and womb is destroyed for the twice-born.

3.47.s:
svādhyāyena vrataihoṃmaistraividyenejyayā sutaiḥ ..
mahāyajñaiśca yajñaiśca brāhmīyaṃ kriyate tanuḥ..69..
3.47.d:
स्वाध्यायेन व्रतैहोंमैस्त्रैविद्येनेज्यया सुतैः ॥
महायज्ञैश्च यज्ञैश्च ब्राह्मीयं क्रियते तनुः॥69॥
3.47.m: By study of the Veda, by vows, by fire offerings, by knowledge of the three Vedas, by sacrifice, by sons, / and by the great sacrifices and sacrifices, this body is made divine.

3.47.s:
garbhāṣṭamebde kurvīta brāhmaṇasyopanāyanam ..
garbhādekadaśe rājño garbhāttu dvādaśe viśaḥ..3.233.70..
3.47.d:
गर्भाष्टमेब्दे कुर्वीत ब्राह्मणस्योपनायनम् ॥
गर्भादेकदशे राज्ञो गर्भात्तु द्वादशे विशः॥3.233.70॥
3.47.m: One should perform the initiation of a brahmin in the eighth year from conception, / of a king in the eleventh from conception, and of a vaiśya in the twelfth from conception.

3.47.s:
āṣoḍaśādbrāhmaṇasya sāvitrī nātivartate..
ādvāviṃśātkṣattrabandhorācaturvijaterviśaḥ..71..
3.47.d:
आषोडशाद्ब्राह्मणस्य सावित्री नातिवर्तते॥
आद्वाविंशात्क्षत्त्रबन्धोराचतुर्विजतेर्विशः॥71॥
3.47.m: For a brahmin the Sāvitrī does not expire until the sixteenth year; / for a kṣatriya until the twenty-second; for a vaiśya until the twenty-fourth.

3.47.s:
ata ūrdhvaṃ trayopyete yathākālamasaṃskṛtāḥ..
sāvitrīpatitā vrātyā bhavanti ca vigarhitāḥ..72..
3.47.d:
अत ऊर्ध्वं त्रयोप्येते यथाकालमसंस्कृताः॥
सावित्रीपतिता व्रात्या भवन्ति च विगर्हिताः॥72॥
3.47.m: Beyond that, all three, if uninitiated at the proper time, / become fallen from the Sāvitrī, outcasts, and censured.

3.47.s:
brahmaṇaḥ praṇavaṃ kuryādādāvante ca sarvadā..
sravatyanoṃkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ parastācca viśīryate .. 73 ..
3.47.d:
ब्रह्मणः प्रणवं कुर्यादादावन्ते च सर्वदा॥
स्रवत्यनोंकृतं पूर्वं परस्ताच्च विशीर्यते ॥ 73 ॥
3.47.m: One should always utter the syllable Oṃ at the beginning and at the end of the Veda; / that which is not preceded by Oṃ trickles away, and that not followed by it disintegrates.

3.47.s:
indriyāṇāṃ vicaratāṃ viṣayeṣvapahāriṣu ..
saṃśaye yatnamātiṣṭhedvidvānyanteva vājinām .. 74 ..
3.47.d:
इन्द्रियाणां विचरतां विषयेष्वपहारिषु ॥
संशये यत्नमातिष्ठेद्विद्वान्यन्तेव वाजिनाम् ॥ 74 ॥
3.47.m: Regarding the senses wandering among enticing sensory objects, / a wise man should make an effort to control them, like a charioteer [controlling] horses.

3.47.s:
vaśīkṛtvendriyagrāmaṃ saṃyamya ca manastathā ...
sarvānsaṃsādhayatyarthānakṣiṇvanyogatastanum .. 75 ..
3.47.d:
वशीकृत्वेन्द्रियग्रामं संयम्य च मनस्तथा ॥।
सर्वान्संसाधयत्यर्थानक्षिण्वन्योगतस्तनुम् ॥ 75 ॥
3.47.m: Having brought the collection of senses under control and having restrained the mind, / one achieves all aims without injuring the body through yoga.

3.47.s:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati ..
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate ..76..
3.47.d:
न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति ॥
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ॥76॥
3.47.m: Desire is never extinguished by the enjoyment of desires; / it only increases even more, like fire fed with clarified butter.

3.47.s:
yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryati jīryataḥ ..
yāsau prāṇāntiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham ..77..
3.47.d:
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः ॥
यासौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् ॥77॥
3.47.m: That which is hard to abandon by the foolish, which does not age as one ages, / which is a fatal disease—there is happiness for one who abandons that craving.

3.47.s:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ..
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet .. 78 ..
3.47.d:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः॥
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥ 78 ॥
3.47.m: Threefold is this gate of hell, destructive of the self: / desire, anger, and greed; therefore one should abandon these three.

3.47.s:
indriyāṇāṃ prasaṅgena doṣamanvetyasaṃśayam ..
saṃniyamya tu tānyeva tataḥ siddhiṃ sa gacchati .. 79 ..
3.47.d:
इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन दोषमन्वेत्यसंशयम् ॥
संनियम्य तु तान्येव ततः सिद्धिं स गच्छति ॥ 79 ॥
3.47.m: By attachment to the senses, one undoubtedly incurs fault; / but having restrained them, one then attains perfection.

3.47.s:
abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ ..
catvāri saṃpravardhante hyāyurmedhā yaśo balam .. 3.233.80 ..
3.47.d:
अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोपसेविनः ॥
चत्वारि संप्रवर्धन्ते ह्यायुर्मेधा यशो बलम् ॥ 3.233.80 ॥
3.47.m: For one who is disposed to saluting respectfully and who constantly serves the elderly, / four things truly increase: lifespan, intellect, fame, and strength.

3.47.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ kuśalaṃ pṛcchetkṣattrabandhumanāmayam ..
vaiśyaṃ kṣemaṃ samāgamya śūdraṃ tvārogyameva ca .. 81 ..
3.47.d:
ब्राह्मणं कुशलं पृच्छेत्क्षत्त्रबन्धुमनामयम् ॥
वैश्यं क्षेमं समागम्य शूद्रं त्वारोग्यमेव च ॥ 81 ॥
3.47.m: One should ask a brahmin about his well-being, a kṣatriya about his freedom from harm, / a vaiśya about his prosperity upon meeting, and a śūdra about his health.

3.47.s:
vittaṃ bandhurvayaḥ karma vidyā bhavati pañcamī ..
etāni mānyasthānāni garīyo yadyaduttaram .. 82 ..
3.47.d:
वित्तं बन्धुर्वयः कर्म विद्या भवति पञ्चमी ॥
एतानि मान्यस्थानानि गरीयो यद्यदुत्तरम् ॥ 82 ॥
3.47.m: Wealth, kin, age, ritual action, and learning is the fifth; / these are grounds for respect, each subsequent one being weightier.

3.47.s:
na hāyanairna palitairna vittena na bandhubhiḥ ..
ṛṣayaścakrire dharmaṃ yo'nūcānaḥ sa no mahān .. 83 ..
3.47.d:
न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः ॥
ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्मं योऽनूचानः स नो महान् ॥ 83 ॥
3.47.m: Not by years, nor by grey hair, nor by wealth, nor by relatives [is greatness judged]; / the sages made this dharma: 'He who has studied the Veda with its limbs is great to us.'

3.47.s:
viprāṇāṃ jñānato jyaiṣṭhyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca vīryataḥ ..
vaiśyānāṃ dhānyadhanataḥ śūdrāṇāmeva janmataḥ .. 84 ..
3.47.d:
विप्राणां ज्ञानतो ज्यैष्ठ्यं क्षत्रियाणां च वीर्यतः ॥
वैश्यानां धान्यधनतः शूद्राणामेव जन्मतः ॥ 84 ॥
3.47.m: The seniority of brahmins is from knowledge, of kṣatriyas from valor, / of vaiśyas from grain and wealth, and of śūdras merely from age.

3.47.s:
ahiṃsayaiva bhūtānāṃ kāryaṃ śreyo'nupālanam ..
vāk caiva madhurā hyasyāḥ prayojyā dharmakāṃkṣiṇā .. 85 ..
3.47.d:
अहिंसयैव भूतानां कार्यं श्रेयोऽनुपालनम् ॥
वाक् चैव मधुरा ह्यस्याः प्रयोज्या धर्मकांक्षिणा ॥ 85 ॥
3.47.m: The pursuit of the highest good must be done only by non-violence toward living beings; / and speech that is sweet should be employed by one who desires dharma.

3.47.s:
yasya vā'ṅmanasī śuddhe samyaggupte ca sarvadā ..
sa vai sarvamavāpnoti vedāntagamanātphalam ..86..
3.47.d:
यस्य वाऽङ्मनसी शुद्धे सम्यग्गुप्ते च सर्वदा ॥
स वै सर्वमवाप्नोति वेदान्तगमनात्फलम् ॥86॥
3.47.m: He whose speech and mind are pure and always well guarded / indeed attains all the fruit that comes from mastering the Vedānta.

3.47.s:
vedameva sadābhyasyettapastaptuṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
vedābhyāso hi viprasya tapaḥ paramihocyate .. 87 ..
3.47.d:
वेदमेव सदाभ्यस्येत्तपस्तप्तुं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
वेदाभ्यासो हि विप्रस्य तपः परमिहोच्यते ॥ 87 ॥
3.47.m: To practice asceticism, one should constantly study the Veda, O best of the twice-born; / for the study of the Veda is declared to be the highest asceticism for a brahmin in this world.

3.47.s:
yo'nadhītya dvijo vedānanyatra kurute śramam ..
sa jīvanneva śūdratvamāśu gacchati sānvayaḥ .. 88 ..
3.47.d:
योऽनधीत्य द्विजो वेदानन्यत्र कुरुते श्रमम् ॥
स जीवन्नेव शूद्रत्वमाशु गच्छति सान्वयः ॥ 88 ॥
3.47.m: A twice-born man who, without having studied the Vedas, expends effort elsewhere / quickly descends into the status of a śūdra even while living, along with his family.

3.47.s:
māturagre'dhijananaṃ dvitīyaṃ mauñjibandhanam ..
tṛtīyaṃ yajñadīkṣāyāṃ dvijasya śruticodanāt .. 89 ..
3.47.d:
मातुरग्रेऽधिजननं द्वितीयं मौञ्जिबन्धनम् ॥
तृतीयं यज्ञदीक्षायां द्विजस्य श्रुतिचोदनात् ॥ 89 ॥
3.47.m: The first birth is from the mother, the second at the tying of the muñja girdle, / and the third at the sacrificial consecration, in accordance with the injunction of Śruti for the twice-born.

3.47.s:
na hyasminsajjate karma kiñcidāmauñjibandhanāta ..
nābhivyāhārayedbrahma svadhāniyamanādṛte ... 3.233.90 ..
3.47.d:
न ह्यस्मिन्सज्जते कर्म किञ्चिदामौञ्जिबन्धनात ॥
नाभिव्याहारयेद्ब्रह्म स्वधानियमनादृते ॥। 3.233.90 ॥
3.47.m: For no ritual action applies to him until the tying of the muñja girdle; / he should not pronounce Vedic texts, except for the regulation of ancestral food.

3.47.s:
śūdreṇa hi samastāvadyāvadvedaṃ na jānate ..
kṛtopanayanasyāsya vratādeśanamiṣyate .. 91 ..
3.47.d:
शूद्रेण हि समस्तावद्यावद्वेदं न जानते ॥
कृतोपनयनस्यास्य व्रतादेशनमिष्यते ॥ 91 ॥
3.47.m: For he is equal to a śūdra as long as he does not know the Veda; / for him whose initiation has been performed, the instruction of vows is prescribed.

3.47.s:
guroryatra parīvādo nindā cāpi pravartate ..
karṇau tatra pidhātavyau gantavyaṃ vā tato'nyataḥ ..92..
3.47.d:
गुरोर्यत्र परीवादो निन्दा चापि प्रवर्तते ॥
कर्णौ तत्र पिधातव्यौ गन्तव्यं वा ततोऽन्यतः ॥92॥
3.47.m: Where gossip and censure of the teacher takes place, / there one should cover one's ears or go elsewhere from that place.

3.47.s:
kharo bhavetparīvādī śvā vai bhavati nindakaḥ ..
paribhoktā krimirbhavati kīṭo bhavati matsarī ..93..
3.47.d:
खरो भवेत्परीवादी श्वा वै भवति निन्दकः ॥
परिभोक्ता क्रिमिर्भवति कीटो भवति मत्सरी ॥93॥
3.47.m: One who slanders becomes a donkey; a reviler indeed becomes a dog; / one who consumes [his teacher's property] becomes a worm; one who is envious becomes an insect.

3.47.s:
dūrastho nārcayedenaṃ na kruddho nāntike striyāḥ ..
ekāsanastho na bhavedāpanno'pi kadācana.. 94..
3.47.d:
दूरस्थो नार्चयेदेनं न क्रुद्धो नान्तिके स्त्रियाः ॥
एकासनस्थो न भवेदापन्नोऽपि कदाचन॥ 94॥
3.47.m: Standing at a distance he should not honour him, nor when angry, nor near a woman; / he should never share a single seat with him, even when in distress.

3.47.s:
gośvoṣṭrayānaprāsādasvastareṣu kaṭeṣu ca ..
nāsīta guruṇā sārdhaṃ śilāphalakanauṣu ca .. 95 ..
3.47.d:
गोश्वोष्ट्रयानप्रासादस्वस्तरेषु कटेषु च ॥
नासीत गुरुणा सार्धं शिलाफलकनौषु च ॥ 95 ॥
3.47.m: In a vehicle [drawn by] cattle, horses, or camels, on a mansion terrace, on mats of grass, / on woven mats, on stone slabs, wooden planks, or in boats, he should not sit together with his guru.

3.47.s:
gurorgurau sannihite guruvadvṛttimācaret ..
adhyāpayangurusuto guruvanmānamarhati .. 96 ..
3.47.d:
गुरोर्गुरौ सन्निहिते गुरुवद्वृत्तिमाचरेत् ॥
अध्यापयन्गुरुसुतो गुरुवन्मानमर्हति ॥ 96 ॥
3.47.m: When the guru's guru is present, he should behave as towards his guru; / if the guru's son is teaching, he deserves respect like the guru.

3.47.s:
na kuryādguruputrasya pādayoścāvanejanama ..
guruvatpratipūjyāstu savarṇā guruyoṣitaḥ..97..
3.47.d:
न कुर्याद्गुरुपुत्रस्य पादयोश्चावनेजनम ॥
गुरुवत्प्रतिपूज्यास्तु सवर्णा गुरुयोषितः॥97॥
3.47.m: He should not wash the feet of the guru's son; / but the wives of the guru belonging to the same caste are to be worshipped just like the guru.

3.47.s:
asavarṇāstu sampūjyāḥ pratyutthānābhivādanaiḥ ..
abhyañjanaṃ sthāpanaṃ ca gātrotsādanameva ca..98..
3.47.d:
असवर्णास्तु सम्पूज्याः प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादनैः ॥
अभ्यञ्जनं स्थापनं च गात्रोत्सादनमेव च॥98॥
3.47.m: Those of a different caste, however, are to be honoured by rising and saluting; / anointing, bathing, massaging of the body,

3.47.s:
gurupatnyā na kāryāṇi keśānāṃ ca prasādhanam..
gurupatnī ca yuvatirnābhivādyeha pādayoḥ..99..
3.47.d:
गुरुपत्न्या न कार्याणि केशानां च प्रसाधनम्॥
गुरुपत्नी च युवतिर्नाभिवाद्येह पादयोः॥99॥
3.47.m: and dressing of the hair are not to be done for a wife of the guru; / nor should a youthful wife of the guru be saluted here at her feet

3.47.s:
pūrṇā viṃśativarṣeṇa guṇadoṣau vijānatā..
mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā na viviktāsano bhavet..3.233.100..
3.47.d:
पूर्णा विंशतिवर्षेण गुणदोषौ विजानता॥
मात्रा स्वस्रा दुहित्रा वा न विविक्तासनो भवेत्॥3.233.100॥
3.47.m: by one who has reached twenty years of age and knows right and wrong. / One should not sit in a secluded seat with one's mother, sister, or daughter.

3.47.s:
balavānindriyagrāmo vidvāṃsamapi karṣati ..
viproṣya pādagrahaṇaṃ tvanvahañcābhivādanam ..101..
3.47.d:
बलवानिन्द्रियग्रामो विद्वांसमपि कर्षति ॥
विप्रोष्य पादग्रहणं त्वन्वहञ्चाभिवादनम् ॥101॥
3.47.m: The realm of the senses is powerful: it draws away even a wise man. / Having returned from a journey, he should touch [their] feet, but salute [them] daily;

3.47.s:
gurudāreṣu kurvīta satāṃ dharmamanusmaran ..
striyo ratnānyatho vidyā dharmassatyaṃ subhāṣitam..102..
3.47.d:
गुरुदारेषु कुर्वीत सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन् ॥
स्त्रियो रत्नान्यथो विद्या धर्मस्सत्यं सुभाषितम्॥102॥
3.47.m: he should act towards the wives of the guru mindful of the dharma of the virtuous. / Women, gems, knowledge, dharma, truth, eloquent speech,

3.47.s:
śilpāni cāpyaduṣṭāni samādeyāni sarvataḥ..
abrāhmaṇādadhyayanaṃ cāpatkāle vidhīyate..103..
3.47.d:
शिल्पानि चाप्यदुष्टानि समादेयानि सर्वतः॥
अब्राह्मणादध्ययनं चापत्काले विधीयते॥103॥
3.47.m: and unblemished crafts are to be acquired from everywhere. / Study from a non-brahmin is prescribed in times of distress;

3.47.s:
anuvrajyā ca śuśrūṣā yāvadadhyayanaṃ gurau ..
nābrāhmaṇagurau śiṣyo vāsamātyantikaṃ vaset .. 104 ..
3.47.d:
अनुव्रज्या च शुश्रूषा यावदध्ययनं गुरौ ॥
नाब्राह्मणगुरौ शिष्यो वासमात्यन्तिकं वसेत् ॥ 104 ॥
3.47.m: following after and serving [him] should last only as long as the study with the teacher; / a disciple should not make his permanent residence with a non-brahmin teacher,

3.47.s:
brāhmaṇe vānanūcāne kāṅkṣangatimanuttamāt ..
pitṛbhirmātṛbhirnāryaḥ patibhirdevaraistathā..105..
3.47.d:
ब्राह्मणे वाननूचाने काङ्क्षन्गतिमनुत्तमात् ॥
पितृभिर्मातृभिर्नार्यः पतिभिर्देवरैस्तथा॥105॥
3.47.m: nor with a brahmin who is unlearned in the Vedas, if he desires the highest state. / By fathers, mothers, husbands, and likewise by brothers-in-law,

3.47.s:
bhūṣyā bhūṣayitavyāśca bahukalyāṇamīpsubhiḥ..
yatra nāryastu pūjyante ramante tatra devatāḥ .. 106 ..
3.47.d:
भूष्या भूषयितव्याश्च बहुकल्याणमीप्सुभिः॥
यत्र नार्यस्तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः ॥ 106 ॥
3.47.m: women must be adorned and treated with respect by those seeking great prosperity. / Where women are honoured, there the gods rejoice;

3.47.s:
yatraitāstu na pūjyante sarvāstatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ ..
santuṣṭo bhāryayā bhartā bhāryā bhartrā tathaiva ca .. 107 ..
3.47.d:
यत्रैतास्तु न पूज्यन्ते सर्वास्तत्राफलाः क्रियाः ॥
सन्तुष्टो भार्यया भर्ता भार्या भर्त्रा तथैव च ॥ 107 ॥
3.47.m: where they are not honoured, there all rites are fruitless. / A husband satisfied with his wife, and a wife likewise with her husband,

3.47.s:
yasminnetatkule nityaṃ kalyāṇaṃ tatra vai dhuvam ..
kuvivāhaiḥ kriyālopairvedānadhyayanena ca .. 108 ..
3.47.d:
यस्मिन्नेतत्कुले नित्यं कल्याणं तत्र वै धुवम् ॥
कुविवाहैः क्रियालोपैर्वेदानध्ययनेन च ॥ 108 ॥
3.47.m: in whichever family this is constant, prosperity there is indeed certain. / Through bad marriages, through omission of rites, and through non-study of the Vedas,

3.47.s:
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca ..
śilpena vyavahāreṇa śūdrāputraiśca kevalaiḥ ..109 ..
3.47.d:
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥
शिल्पेन व्यवहारेण शूद्रापुत्रैश्च केवलैः ॥109 ॥
3.47.m: families fall into degradation, as well as by transgressing against brahmins, / by crafts, trade, and by sons born only of a śūdra woman,

3.47.s:
gobhiraśvaiśca yānaiśca kṛṣyā rājopasevayā ..
ayājya yājanāccaiva nāstikyena ca karmaṇā .. 3.233.110
3.47.d:
गोभिरश्वैश्च यानैश्च कृष्या राजोपसेवया ॥
अयाज्य याजनाच्चैव नास्तिक्येन च कर्मणा ॥ 3.233.110
3.47.m: by [dealing in] cattle, horses, and vehicles, by agriculture, by serving a king, / by sacrificing for those unfit to be sacrificed for, and by deeds of unbelief.

3.47.s:
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti yāni hīnāni mantrataḥ ..
mantratastu samṛddhāni kulānyalpadhanānyapi .. .. 111 ..
3.47.d:
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति यानि हीनानि मन्त्रतः ॥
मन्त्रतस्तु समृद्धानि कुलान्यल्पधनान्यपि ॥ ॥ 111 ॥
3.47.m: Families devoid of mantras fall into degradation; / but families rich in mantras, even if poor in wealth,

3.47.s:
kulasaṃkhyāntu gacchanti karṣanti ca mahadyaśaḥ ..
ṛṣayaḥ pitaro devā bhūtānyatithayastathā .. 112 ..
3.47.d:
कुलसंख्यान्तु गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च महद्यशः ॥
ऋषयः पितरो देवा भूतान्यतिथयस्तथा ॥ 112 ॥
3.47.m: attain the status of noble families and attract great renown. / The seers, the ancestors, the gods, all beings, and guests

3.47.s:
āśāsate kuṭumbibhyastebhyaḥ kāryaṃ vijānatā ..
svādhyāyenārcayetarṣīnhomairdevānyathāvidhi .. 113 ..
3.47.d:
आशासते कुटुम्बिभ्यस्तेभ्यः कार्यं विजानता ॥
स्वाध्यायेनार्चयेतर्षीन्होमैर्देवान्यथाविधि ॥ 113 ॥
3.47.m: expect [offerings] from householders; by one who knows, [this duty] must be performed for them. / One should worship the seers with Vedic recitation, and the gods with oblations according to rule;

3.47.s:
pitṝñchrāddhena nṝnannairbhūtāni balikarmaṇā ..
dadyādaharahaḥ śrāddhamannādyenodakena ca .. 114 ..
3.47.d:
पितॄञ्छ्राद्धेन नॄनन्नैर्भूतानि बलिकर्मणा ॥
दद्यादहरहः श्राद्धमन्नाद्येनोदकेन च ॥ 114 ॥
3.47.m: the ancestors with a śrāddha, men with food, and living beings with a bali offering. / Day after day he should offer a śrāddha with food and water,

3.47.s:
payomūlaphalairvāpi pitṛbhyaḥ prītimāharan ..
ekamapyāśayedvipra pitrarthe pāñcayajñike .. 115 ..
3.47.d:
पयोमूलफलैर्वापि पितृभ्यः प्रीतिमाहरन् ॥
एकमप्याशयेद्विप्र पित्रर्थे पाञ्चयज्ञिके ॥ 115 ॥
3.47.m: or with milk, roots, and fruits, bringing satisfaction to the ancestors. / He should feed even a single brahmin for the sake of the ancestors in the rite of the five sacrifices;

3.47.s:
na caivātrāśāyetkañcidvaiśvadevaṃ prati dvijam ..
vaiśvadevasya siddhasya gṛhye'gnau vidhipūrvakam .. 116 ..
3.47.d:
न चैवात्राशायेत्कञ्चिद्वैश्वदेवं प्रति द्विजम् ॥
वैश्वदेवस्य सिद्धस्य गृह्येऽग्नौ विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ 116 ॥
3.47.m: and he should not feed any twice-born man here for the vaiśvadeva [offering]. / When the vaiśvadeva is prepared in the domestic fire according to rule,

3.47.s:
svasūtravihitaṃ kuryādvaiśvadevamatandritaḥ ..
praṇīte vāprāṇīte vā hutotsṛṣṭe jale'pi vā .. 117 ..
3.47.d:
स्वसूत्रविहितं कुर्याद्वैश्वदेवमतन्द्रितः ॥
प्रणीते वाप्राणीते वा हुतोत्सृष्टे जलेऽपि वा ॥ 117 ॥
3.47.m: he should perform the vaiśvadeva prescribed by his own aphorisms, without indolence. / In water [into which fire] has been brought or not brought, or which has been cast out after oblation,

3.47.s:
vaiśvadevaṃ dhruvaṃ kāryaṃ brāhmaṇena vipaścitā ..
paraṃ sthānamavāpnoti kṛtvaivaṃ satataṃ gṛhī ..
bhojayedatithiṃ paścādbhikṣāṃ dadyācca bhikṣave .. 118 ..
3.47.d:
वैश्वदेवं ध्रुवं कार्यं ब्राह्मणेन विपश्चिता ॥
परं स्थानमवाप्नोति कृत्वैवं सततं गृही ॥
भोजयेदतिथिं पश्चाद्भिक्षां दद्याच्च भिक्षवे ॥ 118 ॥
3.47.m: the vaiśvadeva must certainly be performed by a wise brahmin. / Having done this constantly, the householder attains the highest realm; / afterwards he should feed a guest and give alms to a mendicant.

3.47.s:
yatpuṇyaphalamāpnoti gāṃ dattvā vidhivadgurau ..
tatpuṇyaphalamāpnoti bhikṣāṃ dattvā yathārcitām .. 119 ..
3.47.d:
यत्पुण्यफलमाप्नोति गां दत्त्वा विधिवद्गुरौ ॥
तत्पुण्यफलमाप्नोति भिक्षां दत्त्वा यथार्चिताम् ॥ 119 ॥
3.47.m: Whatever fruit of merit one obtains by giving a cow to a guru according to rule, / that fruit of merit one obtains by giving alms that have been properly honoured.

3.47.s:
vidyātapaḥsamṛddheṣu hutaṃ vipramukhāgniṣu ..
nistārayati durgeṣu bhavatyakṣayameva ca .. 3.233.120 ..
3.47.d:
विद्यातपःसमृद्धेषु हुतं विप्रमुखाग्निषु ॥
निस्तारयति दुर्गेषु भवत्यक्षयमेव च ॥ 3.233.120 ॥
3.47.m: That which is offered into the fires that are the mouths of brahmins rich in learning and austerity / delivers from difficulties and becomes inexhaustible.

3.47.s:
saṃprāptāya tvatithaye pradadyādāsanodakam ..
annaṃ caiva yathāśakti satkṛtya vidhipūrvakam .. 121 ..
3.47.d:
संप्राप्ताय त्वतिथये प्रदद्यादासनोदकम् ॥
अन्नं चैव यथाशक्ति सत्कृत्य विधिपूर्वकम् ॥ 121 ॥
3.47.m: To an arrived guest he should give a seat and water, / and food according to his ability, honouring him according to rule.

3.47.s:
śilānyapyuñchato nityaṃ pañcāgnīnapi juhvataḥ ..
sarvaṃ sukṛtamādatte brāhmaṇo'narcito vasan .. 122 ..
3.47.d:
शिलान्यप्युञ्छतो नित्यं पञ्चाग्नीनपि जुह्वतः ॥
सर्वं सुकृतमादत्ते ब्राह्मणोऽनर्चितो वसन् ॥ 122 ॥
3.47.m: Even if one always gathers ears of grain and offers oblations into the five fires, / an unhonoured brahmin, dwelling [in the house], takes away all one's merit.

3.47.s:
tṛṇāni bhūmirudakaṃ vāk caturthī ca sūnṛtā ..
etānyapi satāṃ gehe nocchidyaṃte kadācana .. 123 ..
3.47.d:
तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक् चतुर्थी च सूनृता ॥
एतान्यपि सतां गेहे नोच्छिद्यंते कदाचन ॥ 123 ॥
3.47.m: Grass, ground, water, and fourthly, gentle speech— / these are never lacking in the house of the virtuous.

3.47.s:
ekarātrantu nivasannatithirbrāhmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
naikagrāmīṇamatithiṃ vipraṃ sāṅgatikaṃ tathā..124..
3.47.d:
एकरात्रन्तु निवसन्नतिथिर्ब्राह्मणः स्मृतः ॥
नैकग्रामीणमतिथिं विप्रं साङ्गतिकं तथा॥124॥
3.47.m: A brahmin staying for one night only is called a guest; / one should not [regard as] a guest a brahmin who is a fellow villager or an associate.

3.47.s:
upāsate ye gṛhasthāḥ parapākamabuddhayaḥ ..
tena te pretya paśutāṃ vrajantyannādyadāyinām ....29..
3.47.d:
उपासते ये गृहस्थाः परपाकमबुद्धयः ॥
तेन ते प्रेत्य पशुतां व्रजन्त्यन्नाद्यदायिनाम् ॥॥29॥
3.47.m: Those senseless householders who seek after the cooked food of others, / because of that, after death, become cattle of those who give them food.

3.47.s:
aprīṇanyotithiḥ sāyaṃ sūryānte gṛhamedhinā ..
kāle prāptastvakāle vā nāsyānaśnangṛhe vaseta .. 126 ..
3.47.d:
अप्रीणन्योतिथिः सायं सूर्यान्ते गृहमेधिना ॥
काले प्राप्तस्त्वकाले वा नास्यानश्नन्गृहे वसेत ॥ 126 ॥
3.47.m: A guest arriving at evening after sunset should not be left ungratified by the householder; / arriving in time or out of time, he should not dwell in his house without eating.

3.47.s:
na vai svayaṃ tadaśnīyādatithiṃ yanna bhojayet ..
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ svargyañcātithipūjanam ..127 ..
3.47.d:
न वै स्वयं तदश्नीयादतिथिं यन्न भोजयेत् ॥
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं स्वर्ग्यञ्चातिथिपूजनम् ॥127 ॥
3.47.m: He himself should not eat that which he does not feed to a guest; / honouring a guest brings wealth, fame, long life, and heaven.

3.47.s:
vaiśvadeve tu nirvṛtte yadyanyo'tithirāvrajet ..
tathā cānnaṃ yathāśakti pradadyācca baliṃ haret .. 128 ..
3.47.d:
वैश्वदेवे तु निर्वृत्ते यद्यन्योऽतिथिराव्रजेत् ॥
तथा चान्नं यथाशक्ति प्रदद्याच्च बलिं हरेत् ॥ 128 ॥
3.47.m: If another guest should arrive when the vaiśvadeva is finished, / he should give him food according to his ability and offer a bali portion.

3.47.s:
na bhojanārthe sve vipraḥ kulagotre nivedayet ..
bhojanārthe tu śaṃsanvā vāntāśītyucyate budhaiḥ .. 129 ..
3.47.d:
न भोजनार्थे स्वे विप्रः कुलगोत्रे निवेदयेत् ॥
भोजनार्थे तु शंसन्वा वान्ताशीत्युच्यते बुधैः ॥ 129 ॥
3.47.m: A brahmin should not declare his family and lineage for the sake of a meal; / one who praises [his lineage] for the sake of a meal is called by the wise an eater of vomit.

3.47.s:
yadi tvatithidharmeṇa kṣattriyo gṛhamāvrajet ..
bhuktavatsu ca vipreṣu kāmaṃ tamapi pūjayet ..3.233.130..
3.47.d:
यदि त्वतिथिधर्मेण क्षत्त्रियो गृहमाव्रजेत् ॥
भुक्तवत्सु च विप्रेषु कामं तमपि पूजयेत् ॥3.233.130॥
3.47.m: If, however, a kṣatriya should arrive at the house as a guest, / he may gladly feed him too after the brahmins have eaten.

3.47.s:
vaiśyaśūdrāvapi prāptau kuṭumbe 'tithidharmiṇau ..
bhojayetsaha bhṛtyaistānānṛśaṃsyaṃ prayojayan ..131..
3.47.d:
वैश्यशूद्रावपि प्राप्तौ कुटुम्बे ऽतिथिधर्मिणौ ॥
भोजयेत्सह भृत्यैस्तानानृशंस्यं प्रयोजयन् ॥131॥
3.47.m: If a vaiśya and a śūdra also arrive at the household in the role of guests, / he should feed them along with his servants, exercising compassion.

3.47.s:
sakhyādīnbhāryayā sārdhaṃ bhojayedgṛhamāgatān ..
patitaśvapacebhyastu śvabhyastu bhuvi nirvapet .. 132 ..
3.47.d:
सख्यादीन्भार्यया सार्धं भोजयेद्गृहमागतान् ॥
पतितश्वपचेभ्यस्तु श्वभ्यस्तु भुवि निर्वपेत् ॥ 132 ॥
3.47.m: He should feed friends and other [kinsmen] who have come to the house along with his wife; / but for the fallen, outcasts, and dogs, he should scatter [food] on the ground.

3.47.s:
suvāsinīḥ kumārāṃśca rogiṇo garbhiṇīstathā ..
atithibhyo'gra evainānbhojayedavicārayan .. 133 ..
3.47.d:
सुवासिनीः कुमारांश्च रोगिणो गर्भिणीस्तथा ॥
अतिथिभ्योऽग्र एवैनान्भोजयेदविचारयन् ॥ 133 ॥
3.47.m: Newly married daughters, maidens, the sick, and pregnant women— / he should feed these even before the guests, without hesitation.

3.47.s:
adattvā tu ya etebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ bhuṃkte vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
sa bhuñjāno na jānāti śvagṛddhairjagdhamātmanaḥ .. 134..
3.47.d:
अदत्त्वा तु य एतेभ्यः पूर्वं भुंक्ते विचक्षणः ॥
स भुञ्जानो न जानाति श्वगृद्धैर्जग्धमात्मनः ॥ 134॥
3.47.m: A wise man who eats beforehand without having given to these, / while eating, does not know that he is being devoured by dogs and vultures.

3.47.s:
bhuktavatsu tu vipreṣu sveṣu bhṛtyeṣu caiva hi ..
bhuñjīyātāṃ tataḥ paścādavaśiṣṭaṃ tu dampatī .. 135..
3.47.d:
भुक्तवत्सु तु विप्रेषु स्वेषु भृत्येषु चैव हि ॥
भुञ्जीयातां ततः पश्चादवशिष्टं तु दम्पती ॥ 135॥
3.47.m: When the brahmins and his own servants have eaten, / the husband and wife should then afterwards eat what remains.

3.47.s:
gṛhasthairdhāryate viprāstairlokyaṃ sacarācaram ..
pākaḥ kāryo gṛhasthena bhūtoddharaṇakāmyayā .. 136 ..
3.47.d:
गृहस्थैर्धार्यते विप्रास्तैर्लोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
पाकः कार्यो गृहस्थेन भूतोद्धरणकाम्यया ॥ 136 ॥
3.47.m: The three worlds with what is moving and unmoving are sustained by householders, O brahmins; / cooking should be done by the householder with the desire to sustain all beings.

3.47.s:
aghaṃ sa kevalaṃ bhuṃkte yaḥ pacatyātmakāraṇāt..
vighasāśī bhavennityaṃ nityaṃ cāmṛtabhojanaḥ ..137..
3.47.d:
अघं स केवलं भुंक्ते यः पचत्यात्मकारणात्॥
विघसाशी भवेन्नित्यं नित्यं चामृतभोजनः ॥137॥
3.47.m:
He eats pure sin who cooks for his own sake.
He should constantly eat remains (vighasa), and constantly eat nectar (amṛta).

3.47.s:
vighasaṃ bhuktaśeṣaṃ tu yajñaśeṣaṃ tathāmṛtam ..
rājarṣisnātakācāryapriyaśvaśuramātulān ..138..
3.47.d:
विघसं भुक्तशेषं तु यज्ञशेषं तथामृतम् ॥
राजर्षिस्नातकाचार्यप्रियश्वशुरमातुलान् ॥138॥
3.47.m:
Remains (vighasa) is the leftover of food eaten [by guests], and nectar is the leftover of a sacrifice.
Royal sages, snātakas, teachers, dear ones, fathers-in-law, and maternal uncles,

3.47.s:
arhayenmadhuparkeṇa parisaṃvatsaroṣitān ..
dvau kālau gṛhiṇaḥ pāko vaiśvadevaśca kīrtyate .. 139 ..
3.47.d:
अर्हयेन्मधुपर्केण परिसंवत्सरोषितान् ॥
द्वौ कालौ गृहिणः पाको वैश्वदेवश्च कीर्त्यते ॥ 139 ॥
3.47.m:
he should honor with honey-mixture (madhuparka) when they have stayed away for a full year.
For a householder, cooking and the Vaiśvadeva offering are prescribed at two times [daily].

3.47.s:
vedoditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryādataṃdritaḥ ..
sarvānsamutsṛjedarthāsvāndhyāyasya virodhinaḥ ..3.233.140..
3.47.d:
वेदोदितं स्वकं कर्म नित्यं कुर्यादतंद्रितः ॥
सर्वान्समुत्सृजेदर्थास्वान्ध्यायस्य विरोधिनः ॥3.233.140॥
3.47.m:
Unwearied, he should constantly perform his own duty enjoined by the Veda.
He should abandon all pursuits that conflict with Vedic recitation (svādhyāya).

3.47.s:
buddhivṛddhikarāṇyāśu dhanyāni ca hitāni ca ..
nityaṃ śāstrāṇyavekṣeta nigamāṃścaiva vaidikān ..141..
3.47.d:
बुद्धिवृद्धिकराण्याशु धन्यानि च हितानि च ॥
नित्यं शास्त्राण्यवेक्षेत निगमांश्चैव वैदिकान् ॥141॥
3.47.m:
He should constantly study the treatises that quickly increase intelligence,
bestow prosperity, and are beneficial, as well as the Vedic scriptures.

3.47.s:
ṛṣiyajñaṃ devayajñaṃ bhūtayajñaṃ tathaiva ca ..
nṛyajñaṃ pitṛyajñaṃ ca pañcayajñānna hāpayet ..142..
3.47.d:
ऋषियज्ञं देवयज्ञं भूतयज्ञं तथैव च ॥
नृयज्ञं पितृयज्ञं च पञ्चयज्ञान्न हापयेत् ॥142॥
3.47.m:
The sacrifice to sages, the sacrifice to gods, and likewise the sacrifice to beings,
the sacrifice to humans, and the sacrifice to ancestors—he must not neglect the five sacrifices.

3.47.s:
agnihotraṃ ca juhuyādādyaṃte dyuniśoḥ sadā ..
darśena cārdhamāsāṃte paurṇamāse tathaiva ca ..143..
3.47.d:
अग्निहोत्रं च जुहुयादाद्यंते द्युनिशोः सदा ॥
दर्शेन चार्धमासांते पौर्णमासे तथैव च ॥143॥
3.47.m:
He should always offer the Agnihotra at the beginning and end of day and night,
and likewise on the new moon at the end of the half-month, and on the full moon.

3.47.s:
tayoḥ kālaḥ smṛtaḥ kṣīṇe pūrṇe ca śaśalakṣaṇe ..
paśunāpyāyanānte ca māsānte saumikairmakhaiḥ..144..
3.47.d:
तयोः कालः स्मृतः क्षीणे पूर्णे च शशलक्षणे ॥
पशुनाप्यायनान्ते च मासान्ते सौमिकैर्मखैः॥144॥
3.47.m:
Their time is taught when the hare-marked moon is waned and full.
At the end of an animal sacrifice, at the end of the half-year (ayana), and at the end of the year with Soma sacrifices.

3.47.s:
nāniṣṭvā navasasyeṣṭyā paśunā vāgnimāndvijaḥ..
navānnamadyānmāsaṃ vā dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ..145..
3.47.d:
नानिष्ट्वा नवसस्येष्ट्या पशुना वाग्निमान्द्विजः॥
नवान्नमद्यान्मासं वा दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः॥145॥
3.47.m:
A twice-born who maintains the fire should not eat fresh grain or meat,
desiring to live a long life, without having first offered the sacrifice of fresh crops (navasasyeṣṭi) or an animal sacrifice.

3.47.s:
navenānarcito hyasya paśuhavyena cāgnayaḥ..
prāṇānevāttumicchanti navānnāmiṣagarddhinaḥ..146..
3.47.d:
नवेनानर्चितो ह्यस्य पशुहव्येन चाग्नयः॥
प्राणानेवात्तुमिच्छन्ति नवान्नामिषगर्द्धिनः॥146॥
3.47.m:
For his fires, unhonored with the new [grain] and with an animal offering,
desiring fresh grain and meat, wish to consume his very vital breaths.

3.47.s:
āsanāśanaśayyābhiradbhirmūlaphalena vā..
nāsya kaścidvasedgehe śaktito 'narcito'tithiḥ..147..
3.47.d:
आसनाशनशय्याभिरद्भिर्मूलफलेन वा॥
नास्य कश्चिद्वसेद्गेहे शक्तितो ऽनर्चितोऽतिथिः॥147॥
3.47.m:
No guest should dwell in his house unhonored according to his capacity
with a seat, food, a bed, water, or roots and fruits.

3.47.s:
pāṣaṇḍino vikarmasthānvaiḍālavratikāñśaṭhān..
haitukānbakavṛttīṃśca vāṅmātreṇāpi nārcayet..148..
3.47.d:
पाषण्डिनो विकर्मस्थान्वैडालव्रतिकाञ्शठान्॥
हैतुकान्बकवृत्तींश्च वाङ्मात्रेणापि नार्चयेत्॥148॥
3.47.m:
Heretics, those engaged in improper deeds, those who behave like cats, rogues,
rationalists, and those who act like herons, he should not honor even with speech alone.

3.47.s:
na dānaṃ yaśase dadyānno bhayānnopakāriṇe ..
na nṛttagītaśīlebhyo hāsakebhyaśca dhārmikaḥ .. 149 ..
3.47.d:
न दानं यशसे दद्यान्नो भयान्नोपकारिणे ॥
न नृत्तगीतशीलेभ्यो हासकेभ्यश्च धार्मिकः ॥ 149 ॥
3.47.m:
A righteous man should not give gifts for fame, nor out of fear, nor to a benefactor,
nor to those devoted to dancing and singing, nor to buffoons.

3.47.s:
vedavidyāvratasnātāñśrotriyāngṛhamedhinaḥ ..
pūjayeddhavyakavyeṣu viparītām̐stu varjayet .. 3.233.150 ..
3.47.d:
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नाताञ्श्रोत्रियान्गृहमेधिनः ॥
पूजयेद्धव्यकव्येषु विपरीताम्̐स्तु वर्जयेत् ॥ 3.233.150 ॥
3.47.m:
He should honor in offerings to gods and ancestors those householders
who have completed their bath after vows and Vedic learning, and who are learned in the Veda; but he should avoid those of opposite character.

3.47.s:
śaktito yajamānasya dātavyo gṛhamedhinaḥ ..
saṃvibhāgaśca bhūtebhyaḥ kartavyo'nuparodhataḥ .. 151 ..
3.47.d:
शक्तितो यजमानस्य दातव्यो गृहमेधिनः ॥
संविभागश्च भूतेभ्यः कर्तव्योऽनुपरोधतः ॥ 151 ॥
3.47.m:
A gift should be made according to the capacity of the sacrificer who is a householder;
and a sharing should be made for all creatures without causing deprivation.

3.47.s:
rājato dhanamanvicchetsaṃsīdansnātakaḥ kṣudhā ..
yājyāntevāsino vāpi na tvanyata iti sthitiḥ .. 192 ..
3.47.d:
राजतो धनमन्विच्छेत्संसीदन्स्नातकः क्षुधा ॥
याज्यान्तेवासिनो वापि न त्वन्यत इति स्थितिः ॥ 192 ॥
3.47.m:
A snātaka sinking from hunger should seek wealth from a king,
or from one for whom he sacrifices, or from a pupil, but not from anyone else: such is the rule.

3.47.s:
na jīrṇamalavadvāsā bhavecca vibhave sati ..
svādhyāye nityayuktaḥ syānnityamātmahiteṣu ca..153..
3.47.d:
न जीर्णमलवद्वासा भवेच्च विभवे सति ॥
स्वाध्याये नित्ययुक्तः स्यान्नित्यमात्महितेषु च॥153॥
3.47.m:
When wealth is available, he should not wear ragged or dirty clothes.
He should be constantly engaged in Vedic recitation and constantly in what is beneficial for himself.

3.47.s:
vaiṇavīṃ dhārayedyaṣṭiṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum ..
yajñopavītaṃ vedaṃ ca śubhe raukme ca kuṇḍale .. 154 ..
3.47.d:
वैणवीं धारयेद्यष्टिं सोदकं च कमण्डलुम् ॥
यज्ञोपवीतं वेदं च शुभे रौक्मे च कुण्डले ॥ 154 ॥
3.47.m:
He should carry a bamboo staff, a water-pot with water,
a sacred thread, a Veda, and auspicious gold earrings.

3.47.s:
śuklavāsā bhavennityaṃ parimṛṣṭaparicchadaḥ ..
na caiva pralikhedbhūmiṃ nātmanopaharetsrajam .. 155 ..
3.47.d:
शुक्लवासा भवेन्नित्यं परिमृष्टपरिच्छदः ॥
न चैव प्रलिखेद्भूमिं नात्मनोपहरेत्स्रजम् ॥ 155 ॥
3.47.m:
He should always wear white garments and have well-cleaned possessions.
He should never scratch the ground, nor should he put a garland on himself.

3.47.s:
nāpsu mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā ṣṭhīvanaṃ vā samutsṛjet ..
amedhyaliptamanyadvā lohitaṃ vā viṣāṇi vā .. 156 ..
3.47.d:
नाप्सु मूत्रं पुरीषं वा ष्ठीवनं वा समुत्सृजेत् ॥
अमेध्यलिप्तमन्यद्वा लोहितं वा विषाणि वा ॥ 156 ॥
3.47.m:
He must not discharge urine, feces, or saliva into water,
nor anything smeared with impurities, nor blood, nor poisons.

3.47.s:
etānyeva tathā vahnau nikṣipennaiva ca dvijaḥ ..
naikaḥ śūnyagṛhe svapyācchayānaṃ naiva bodhayet .. 157 ..
3.47.d:
एतान्येव तथा वह्नौ निक्षिपेन्नैव च द्विजः ॥
नैकः शून्यगृहे स्वप्याच्छयानं नैव बोधयेत् ॥ 157 ॥
3.47.m:
A twice-born should never throw these very things into the fire.
He should not sleep alone in an empty house, nor should he awaken someone who is sleeping.

3.47.s:
na divīndrāyudhaṃ dṛṣṭvā kasyaciddarśayedbudhaḥ ..
na śūdrarājye nivasennādhārmikajanāvṛte .. 158..
3.47.d:
न दिवीन्द्रायुधं दृष्ट्वा कस्यचिद्दर्शयेद्बुधः ॥
न शूद्रराज्ये निवसेन्नाधार्मिकजनावृते ॥ 158॥
3.47.m:
A wise man, having seen a rainbow in the sky, should not point it out to anyone.
He should not live in a realm ruled by a śūdra, nor in one surrounded by unrighteous people,

3.47.s:
na pāṣaṇḍijanākīrṇe nopasṛṣṭe na parvate ..
vaidyasāṃvatsarairhīne tathā prabalanāyake .. 159 ..
3.47.d:
न पाषण्डिजनाकीर्णे नोपसृष्टे न पर्वते ॥
वैद्यसांवत्सरैर्हीने तथा प्रबलनायके ॥ 159 ॥
3.47.m:
nor in one crowded with heretics, nor in one afflicted by disease, nor on a mountain,
nor in one lacking physicians and astrologers, nor where there is a tyrannical ruler.

3.47.s:
na kurvīta vṛthā ceṣṭāṃ na vāryañjalinā pibet ..
notsaṅge bhakṣayedbhakṣyānna jātu syātkutūhalī .. 3.233.160 ..
3.47.d:
न कुर्वीत वृथा चेष्टां न वार्यञ्जलिना पिबेत् ॥
नोत्सङ्गे भक्षयेद्भक्ष्यान्न जातु स्यात्कुतूहली ॥ 3.233.160 ॥
3.47.m:
He should not make futile efforts, nor drink water with his hollowed hands.
He should not eat food from his lap, and he should never be inquisitive without reason.

3.47.s:
na nṛtyedatha vā gāyedvāditrāṇi na vādayet ..
nāsphoṭayenna ca kṣveḍenna ca raktāṃ virāgayet..161..
3.47.d:
न नृत्येदथ वा गायेद्वादित्राणि न वादयेत् ॥
नास्फोटयेन्न च क्ष्वेडेन्न च रक्तां विरागयेत्॥161॥
3.47.m:
He should not dance, nor sing, nor play musical instruments.
He should not clap his hands, nor groan, nor alienate a woman who loves him.

3.47.s:
na pādau dhāvayetkāṃsye na ca pādau pratāpayet ..
na cchindyānnakharomāṇi dantairnotpāṭayennakhān .. 162 ..
3.47.d:
न पादौ धावयेत्कांस्ये न च पादौ प्रतापयेत् ॥
न च्छिन्द्यान्नखरोमाणि दन्तैर्नोत्पाटयेन्नखान् ॥ 162 ॥
3.47.m:
He should not wash his feet in a bronze vessel, nor warm his feet.
He should not cut his nails or hair, nor tear his nails with his teeth.

3.47.s:
pādayornaiva kurvīta darbheṣu parimārjanam ..
pālāśamāsanaṃ varjyaṃ pāduke dantadhāvanam .. 163 ..
3.47.d:
पादयोर्नैव कुर्वीत दर्भेषु परिमार्जनम् ॥
पालाशमासनं वर्ज्यं पादुके दन्तधावनम् ॥ 163 ॥
3.47.m:
He should not wipe his feet upon darbha grass.
A seat of palāśa wood is to be avoided, as are shoes and a tooth-stick [made of it].

3.47.s:
na karmaviphalaṃ kuryādāyatyāṃ vā sukhodayam ..
na vigarhyakathāḥ kuryādbahirmālyaṃ na dhārayet..164..
3.47.d:
न कर्मविफलं कुर्यादायत्यां वा सुखोदयम् ॥
न विगर्ह्यकथाः कुर्याद्बहिर्माल्यं न धारयेत्॥164॥
3.47.m:
He should not perform an action that is fruitless, or whose outcome brings happiness only later [at the cost of dharma].
He should not engage in censurable talk, nor wear a garland outwardly.

3.47.s:
advāreṇa na cātīyādgrāmaṃ vā veśma caiva vā..
rātrau ca vṛkṣamūlāni dūrataḥ parivarjayet ..169..
3.47.d:
अद्वारेण न चातीयाद्ग्रामं वा वेश्म चैव वा॥
रात्रौ च वृक्षमूलानि दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥169॥
3.47.m:
He should not enter a village or a house except by the door.
And at night, he should avoid the roots of trees from afar.

3.47.s:
ārdrapādastu bhuñjīta nārdrapādastu saṃvi śeta ..
na śūdrāya matiṃ dadyānnocchiṣṭaṃ na haviṣkṛtam ..166..
3.47.d:
आर्द्रपादस्तु भुञ्जीत नार्द्रपादस्तु संवि शेत ॥
न शूद्राय मतिं दद्यान्नोच्छिष्टं न हविष्कृतम् ॥166॥
3.47.m:
He should eat with wet feet, but he should not go to sleep with wet feet.
He should not give advice to a śūdra, nor leftovers, nor sacrificial food.

3.47.s:
na cāsyopadiśeddharmaṃ na cāsya vratamādiśet ..
na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇīyāllubdhasyocchāstravartinaḥ..167..
3.47.d:
न चास्योपदिशेद्धर्मं न चास्य व्रतमादिशेत् ॥
न राज्ञः प्रतिगृह्णीयाल्लुब्धस्योच्छास्त्रवर्तिनः॥167॥
3.47.m:
He should not instruct him in dharma, nor prescribe a vow for him.
He should not accept gifts from a king who is greedy and acts contrary to the scriptures.

3.47.s:
narakāṇi ca sarvāṇi dadyādrājapratigrahaḥ ..
daśasūnāsamaścakrī daśacakrasamo dhvajī..168..
3.47.d:
नरकाणि च सर्वाणि दद्याद्राजप्रतिग्रहः ॥
दशसूनासमश्चक्री दशचक्रसमो ध्वजी॥168॥
3.47.m:
Accepting gifts from a king brings all the hells.
An oil-presser equals ten slaughterhouses; a tavern-keeper equals ten oil-presses;

3.47.s:
daśadhvajasamā veśyā daśaveśyāsamo nṛpaḥ ..
etadvijñāya vai rājñāṃ na pragṛhṇanti sādhavaḥ .. 169 ..
3.47.d:
दशध्वजसमा वेश्या दशवेश्यासमो नृपः ॥
एतद्विज्ञाय वै राज्ञां न प्रगृह्णन्ति साधवः ॥ 169 ॥
3.47.m:
a prostitute equals ten tavern-keepers; and a king equals ten prostitutes.
Knowing this, good men do not accept gifts from kings.

3.47.s:
upākarmaṇi cotsarge trirātraṃ na paṭhed dvijaḥ ..
vedāṅgāni paṭhetkṛṣṇe śukle vedamatandritaḥ .. .. 3.233.170 ..
3.47.d:
उपाकर्मणि चोत्सर्गे त्रिरात्रं न पठेद् द्विजः ॥
वेदाङ्गानि पठेत्कृष्णे शुक्ले वेदमतन्द्रितः ॥ ॥ 3.233.170 ॥
3.47.m:
At the beginning and conclusion of the Vedic study term, a twice-born should not recite for three nights.
He should study the Vedic ancillary sciences during the dark fortnight, and the Veda during the bright fortnight, unwearied.

3.47.s:
nāvispaṣṭamadhīyīta na śūdrajanasannidhau..
na niśānte pariśrānto brahmādhītya punaḥ svapet..171..
3.47.d:
नाविस्पष्टमधीयीत न शूद्रजनसन्निधौ॥
न निशान्ते परिश्रान्तो ब्रह्माधीत्य पुनः स्वपेत्॥171॥
3.47.m:
He should not recite indistinctly, nor in the presence of śūdras.
Exhausted at the end of the night, having studied the Veda, he should not go back to sleep.

3.47.s:
sāyaṃ niśīthe nādhyayanaṃ vāditre na ca vādyati..
atithiñcānanujñāpya mārute vāti vā bhṛśam..172..
3.47.d:
सायं निशीथे नाध्ययनं वादित्रे न च वाद्यति॥
अतिथिञ्चाननुज्ञाप्य मारुते वाति वा भृशम्॥172॥
3.47.m:
There is no Vedic recitation in the evening or at midnight, nor while musical instruments are playing,
nor without taking leave of a guest, nor when the wind blows violently,

3.47.s:
paśumaṇḍūkamārjāraśvasarpanakulādibhiḥ..
kṛte'ntarālagamane rudhire ca tathā srute..173..
3.47.d:
पशुमण्डूकमार्जारश्वसर्पनकुलादिभिः॥
कृतेऽन्तरालगमने रुधिरे च तथा स्रुते॥173॥
3.47.m:
nor when a beast, frog, cat, dog, snake, mongoose, or the like
has crossed between [teacher and student], nor when blood has flowed.

3.47.s:
dvāvetau varjayennityamanadhyāyau dvijottamaḥ ..
svādhyāyabhūmiṃ cāśuddhāṃ cātmānamaśuciṃ dvijāḥ ..174..
3.47.d:
द्वावेतौ वर्जयेन्नित्यमनध्यायौ द्विजोत्तमः ॥
स्वाध्यायभूमिं चाशुद्धां चात्मानमशुचिं द्विजाः ॥174॥
3.47.m:
A foremost twice-born should always avoid these two occasions of non-recitation,
and twice-borns [should avoid] an impure ground for recitation and an impure self.

3.47.s:
devatānāṃ guro rājñaḥ snātakācāryayostathā..
nākrametkāmataśchāyāṃ babhruṇo dīkṣitasya ca..175..
3.47.d:
देवतानां गुरो राज्ञः स्नातकाचार्ययोस्तथा॥
नाक्रमेत्कामतश्छायां बभ्रुणो दीक्षितस्य च॥175॥
3.47.m:
He should not intentionally step on the shadow of deities, of a guru, of a king,
of a snātaka, of a teacher, of a brown cow, or of an initiated sacrificer.

3.47.s:
nātmānamavamanyeta pūrvābhirasamṛddhibhiḥ..
āmṛtyoḥ śriyamanvicchenna tāṃ manyeta durlabhām..176..
3.47.d:
नात्मानमवमन्येत पूर्वाभिरसमृद्धिभिः॥
आमृत्योः श्रियमन्विच्छेन्न तां मन्येत दुर्लभाम्॥176॥
3.47.m:
He should not despise himself on account of former lack of prosperity.
He should pursue fortune until death; he should not consider it unattainable.

3.47.s:
satyaṃ brūyātpriyaṃ brūyānna brūyātsatyamapriyam ..
priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyādeṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 177 ..
3.47.d:
सत्यं ब्रूयात्प्रियं ब्रूयान्न ब्रूयात्सत्यमप्रियम् ॥
प्रियं च नानृतं ब्रूयादेष धर्मः सनातनः ॥ 177 ॥
3.47.m:
He should speak the truth, he should speak what is pleasant; he should not speak an unpleasant truth,
nor should he speak a pleasant untruth: this is eternal dharma.

3.47.s:
bhadraṃ bhadramiti brūyādbhadramityeva vā vadet ..
śuṣkavairaṃ vivādaṃ ca na kuryātkenacitsaha .. 178 ..
3.47.d:
भद्रं भद्रमिति ब्रूयाद्भद्रमित्येव वा वदेत् ॥
शुष्कवैरं विवादं च न कुर्यात्केनचित्सह ॥ 178 ॥
3.47.m:
He should say, 'Auspicious, auspicious,' or he should simply say, 'Auspicious.'
He should not engage in futile enmity or dispute with anyone.

3.47.s:
anāturaḥ svāni khāni na spṛśedanimittataḥ ..
gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca sūtakānnaṃ ca varjayet ..
sarvaṃ paravaśaṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvamātmavaśaṃ sukham ..179..
3.47.d:
अनातुरः स्वानि खानि न स्पृशेदनिमित्ततः ॥
गणान्नं गणिकान्नं च सूतकान्नं च वर्जयेत् ॥
सर्वं परवशं दुःखं सर्वमात्मवशं सुखम् ॥179॥
3.47.m:
When not ailing, he should not touch his bodily orifices without a reason.
He should avoid food offered by a group, food of a courtesan, and food tainted by child-birth.
Everything subject to another is suffering; everything subject to oneself is happiness.

3.47.s:
sāvitraśāntihomāṃśca kuryātsarvatra nityaśaḥ ..
pitṛṃścaivāṣṭakāsvarcennityamanvaṣṭakāsu ca .. 3.233.180 ..
3.47.d:
सावित्रशान्तिहोमांश्च कुर्यात्सर्वत्र नित्यशः ॥
पितृंश्चैवाष्टकास्वर्चेन्नित्यमन्वष्टकासु च ॥ 3.233.180 ॥
3.47.m:
He should constantly perform Sāvitra and propitiatory oblations everywhere.
And he should constantly honor the ancestors on the Aṣṭakā and Anvaṣṭakā days.

3.47.s:
maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ nityañca prayatātmanām ..
japatāṃ juhvatāṃ caiva vinipāto na vidyate .. 181 ..
3.47.d:
मङ्गलाचारयुक्तानां नित्यञ्च प्रयतात्मनाम् ॥
जपतां जुह्वतां चैव विनिपातो न विद्यते ॥ 181 ॥
3.47.m: For those who are devoted to auspicious conduct, whose minds are always restrained, / and who recite sacred texts and offer oblations into the fire, ruin does not occur.

3.47.s:
na pādapāṇicapalo na netracapalo dvijaḥ ..
na syādvākca palaścaiva na paradrohakarmadhīḥ .. 182 ..
3.47.d:
न पादपाणिचपलो न नेत्रचपलो द्विजः ॥
न स्याद्वाक्च पलश्चैव न परद्रोहकर्मधीः ॥ 182 ॥
3.47.m: A twice-born should not be fickle with feet or hands, nor fickle with his eyes; / he should not be fickle in speech, nor should his mind be set on injuring others.

3.47.s:
yenāsya pitaro yātā yena yātāḥ pitāmahāḥ ..
tena yāyātsatāṃ mārgaṃ tena gacchanna riṣyate .. 183 ..
3.47.d:
येनास्य पितरो याता येन याताः पितामहाः ॥
तेन यायात्सतां मार्गं तेन गच्छन्न रिष्यते ॥ 183 ॥
3.47.m: By the way his fathers went, by which his grandfathers went, / by that let him tread the path of the good; walking by that, he is not harmed.

3.47.s:
ṛtvikpurohitācāryamātulātithisaṃśritaiḥ ..
bālavṛddhāturairvaidyairjñātisambandhibāndhavaiḥ .. 184 ..
3.47.d:
ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यमातुलातिथिसंश्रितैः ॥
बालवृद्धातुरैर्वैद्यैर्ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिबान्धवैः ॥ 184 ॥
3.47.m: With officiating priests, the family priest, teachers, maternal uncles, guests, and dependents, / with children, the elderly, the sick, physicians, kinsmen, relations by marriage, and relatives,

3.47.s:
mātāpitṛbhyāṃ jāmībhirbhrātrā putreṇa bhāryayā ..
duhitrā dāsavargeṇa vivādaṃ na samācaret .. 185 ..
3.47.d:
मातापितृभ्यां जामीभिर्भ्रात्रा पुत्रेण भार्यया ॥
दुहित्रा दासवर्गेण विवादं न समाचरेत् ॥ 185 ॥
3.47.m: With mother and father, female relations, a brother, a son, a wife, / a daughter, and the circle of servants, he should not engage in dispute.

3.47.s:
etairvivādaṃ santyajya sarvāṃllokāñjayed gṛhī ..
tasmādetairadhikṣiptaḥ sahetāsaṃjvaraṃ sadā .. 186 ..
3.47.d:
एतैर्विवादं सन्त्यज्य सर्वांल्लोकाञ्जयेद् गृही ॥
तस्मादेतैरधिक्षिप्तः सहेतासंज्वरं सदा ॥ 186 ॥
3.47.m: Abandoning dispute with these, a householder conquers all worlds; / therefore, reviled by them, he should always endure it without agitation.

3.47.s:
pratigrahaṇasamartho'pi prasaṃgaṃ tatra varjayet ..
pratigraheṇa viprāṇāṃ brāhmaṃ tejo vinaśyati .. 187 ..
3.47.d:
प्रतिग्रहणसमर्थोऽपि प्रसंगं तत्र वर्जयेत् ॥
प्रतिग्रहेण विप्राणां ब्राह्मं तेजो विनश्यति ॥ 187 ॥
3.47.m: Even if he is capable of accepting gifts, he should avoid indulgence in it; / by accepting gifts, the brahmic radiance of brahmins perishes.

3.47.s:
na ca dravyamavijñāya vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ pratigrahe ..
prājñaḥ pratigrahaṃ kuryādavasīdannapi kṣudhā .. 188..
3.47.d:
न च द्रव्यमविज्ञाय विधिं धर्म्यं प्रतिग्रहे ॥
प्राज्ञः प्रतिग्रहं कुर्यादवसीदन्नपि क्षुधा ॥ 188॥
3.47.m: Without knowing the property and the lawful rule regarding acceptance of gifts, / a wise man should not accept a gift, even though perishing of hunger.

3.47.s:
atapāstvanadhīyānaḥ pratigraharucirdvijaḥ ..
ambhasya saṃplavenaiva saha tainaiva majjati .. 189 ..
3.47.d:
अतपास्त्वनधीयानः प्रतिग्रहरुचिर्द्विजः ॥
अम्भस्य संप्लवेनैव सह तैनैव मज्जति ॥ 189 ॥
3.47.m: A twice-born who performs no austerities, does not study, and delights in accepting gifts, / sinks down into the water together with that [giver], like [one riding] a float of stone.

3.47.s:
tasmānna vidvāngṛhṇīyādyasmāttasmātpratigraham ..
alpakenāpyavidvāṃstu paṅke gauriva sīdati .. 3.233.190 ..
3.47.d:
तस्मान्न विद्वान्गृह्णीयाद्यस्मात्तस्मात्प्रतिग्रहम् ॥
अल्पकेनाप्यविद्वांस्तु पङ्के गौरिव सीदति ॥ 3.233.190 ॥
3.47.m: Therefore, a wise man should not accept a gift from anyone whatsoever; / an unlearned man, even through a small [gift], sinks down like a cow in the mud.

3.47.s:
pratigrahasamartho'pi nādatte yaḥ pratigraham ..
ye lokā dānaśīlānāṃ sa tānāpnoti śāśvatān .. 191 ..
3.47.d:
प्रतिग्रहसमर्थोऽपि नादत्ते यः प्रतिग्रहम् ॥
ये लोका दानशीलानां स तानाप्नोति शाश्वतान् ॥ 191 ॥
3.47.m: He who, though capable of accepting gifts, does not take a gift, / attains those eternal worlds that belong to the generous.

3.47.s:
gurūnbhṛtyānujjihīṣurarciṣyandevatātithīn ..
sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyānna tu tṛpyetsvayaṃ tataḥ .. 192 ..
3.47.d:
गुरून्भृत्यानुज्जिहीषुरर्चिष्यन्देवतातिथीन् ॥
सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न तु तृप्येत्स्वयं ततः ॥ 192 ॥
3.47.m: Wishing to support his elders and servants, or wishing to worship gods and guests, / he may accept [gifts] from anyone, but he should not himself enjoy satisfaction from it.

3.47.s:
guruṣvabhyavatīteṣu vinā vātairgṛhe vasan ..
ātmano vṛttimanvicchangṛhṇīyātsādhutaḥ sadā .. 193 ..
3.47.d:
गुरुष्वभ्यवतीतेषु विना वातैर्गृहे वसन् ॥
आत्मनो वृत्तिमन्विच्छन्गृह्णीयात्साधुतः सदा ॥ 193 ॥
3.47.m: When his elders have passed away, or living in the house without them, / seeking a livelihood for himself, he should always accept [gifts only] from a virtuous man.

3.47.s:
dharmadhvajo'tha vā lubdhaśchadmastho lokanindakaḥ ..
vaiḍālavratiko jñeyo hiṃsraḥ sarvātisādhakaḥ .. 194 ..
3.47.d:
धर्मध्वजोऽथ वा लुब्धश्छद्मस्थो लोकनिन्दकः ॥
वैडालव्रतिको ज्ञेयो हिंस्रः सर्वातिसाधकः ॥ 194 ॥
3.47.m: One who hoists the flag of righteousness, or is greedy, acts deceitfully, censures people, / is injurious, and makes all into tools [for his ends], is to be known as one who acts like a cat.

3.47.s:
adhodṛṣṭirnaikṛtikaḥ svārthasādhanatatparaḥ ..
śaṭho mithyāvinītaśca bakavratacaro dvijaḥ .. 195 ..
3.47.d:
अधोदृष्टिर्नैकृतिकः स्वार्थसाधनतत्परः ॥
शठो मिथ्याविनीतश्च बकव्रतचरो द्विजः ॥ 195 ॥
3.47.m: With eyes cast down, deceitful, intent on accomplishing his own purpose, / treacherous, and falsely humble, such a twice-born is one who behaves like a crane.

3.47.s:
ye bakavratino viprā ye ca mārjāraliṅginaḥ ..
te patantyandhatāmisraṃ saha pāpena karmaṇā .. 196 ..
3.47.d:
ये बकव्रतिनो विप्रा ये च मार्जारलिङ्गिनः ॥
ते पतन्त्यन्धतामिस्रं सह पापेन कर्मणा ॥ 196 ॥
3.47.m: Those brahmins who act like cranes, and those who bear the marks of cats, / fall into the blind darkness along with their evil deed.

3.47.s:
na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret ..
vratena pāpaṃ pracchādya kurvanstrīśūdradambhanama ..
pretyeha tādṛśo vipro gṛhyate brahmavādibhiḥ .. 197 ..
3.47.d:
न धर्मस्यापदेशेन पापं कृत्वा व्रतं चरेत् ॥
व्रतेन पापं प्रच्छाद्य कुर्वन्स्त्रीशूद्रदम्भनम ॥
प्रेत्येह तादृशो विप्रो गृह्यते ब्रह्मवादिभिः ॥ 197 ॥
3.47.m: One should not undertake a vow under the pretext of dharma after committing a sin, / concealing the sin by the vow and practicing deceit toward women and śūdras. / Having died, such a brahmin is censured here by the expounders of the Veda.

3.47.s:
chadmanā caritaṃ tacca vrataṃ rakṣāṃsi gacchati ..
aliṅgo liṅgiveśena yo vṛttimupajīvati .. 198 ..
3.47.d:
छद्मना चरितं तच्च व्रतं रक्षांसि गच्छति ॥
अलिङ्गो लिङ्गिवेशेन यो वृत्तिमुपजीवति ॥ 198 ॥
3.47.m: And that vow performed under false pretense goes to the Rākṣasas. / He who, lacking religious marks, maintains his livelihood by wearing the garb of one who has them,

3.47.s:
sa liṅgināṃ haratyenastiryagyonau ca jāyate ..
parakīyanipāneṣu na snāyāddhi kadācana ..
nipānakartuḥ snātvā tu duṣkṛtāṃśena lipyate .. 199 ..
3.47.d:
स लिङ्गिनां हरत्येनस्तिर्यग्योनौ च जायते ॥
परकीयनिपानेषु न स्नायाद्धि कदाचन ॥
निपानकर्तुः स्नात्वा तु दुष्कृतांशेन लिप्यते ॥ 199 ॥
3.47.m: Takes away the sin of those who possess the marks and is born in an animal womb. / One should never bathe in water reservoirs belonging to another; / for having bathed [there], one becomes tainted by a portion of the misdeed of the maker of the reservoir.

3.47.s:
yānaṃ śayyāsanaṃ vastraṃ kūpodyānagṛhāṇi tu..
adattānyupabhuñjāno hyenasaḥ syātturīyabhāk ..3.233.200..
3.47.d:
यानं शय्यासनं वस्त्रं कूपोद्यानगृहाणि तु॥
अदत्तान्युपभुञ्जानो ह्येनसः स्यात्तुरीयभाक् ॥3.233.200॥
3.47.m: A vehicle, a bed, a seat, clothing, or wells, gardens, and houses— / one who enjoys them when not given indeed partakes of a fourth of the sin.

3.47.s:
yamānseveta satataṃ na nityaṃ niyamānbudhaḥ ..
yamānsaṃtyajya kurvāṇo niyamānkevalānbhajan ..201..
3.47.d:
यमान्सेवेत सततं न नित्यं नियमान्बुधः ॥
यमान्संत्यज्य कुर्वाणो नियमान्केवलान्भजन् ॥201॥
3.47.m: A wise man should constantly cultivate the restraints, not always the observances; / he who, having abandoned the restraints, acts practicing only the observances [falls].

3.47.s:
śaucamijyā tapo dānaṃ svādhyāyopasthanigrahaḥ ..
vratopavāso maunaṃ ca snānaṃ ca niyamā daśa ..202 ..
3.47.d:
शौचमिज्या तपो दानं स्वाध्यायोपस्थनिग्रहः ॥
व्रतोपवासो मौनं च स्नानं च नियमा दश ॥202 ॥
3.47.m: Purity, sacrifice, austerity, giving, recitation of the Veda, restraint of the sexual organ, / vows, fasting, silence, and bathing: these are the ten observances.

3.47.s:
ānṛśaṃsyaṃ kṣamā satyamahiṃsā ca damaḥ spṛhā ..
dhyānaṃ prasādo mādhuryaṃ cārjavaṃ ca yamā daśa ..203..
3.47.d:
आनृशंस्यं क्षमा सत्यमहिंसा च दमः स्पृहा ॥
ध्यानं प्रसादो माधुर्यं चार्जवं च यमा दश ॥203॥
3.47.m: Absence of cruelty, patience, truth, non-injury, self-control, freedom from longing, / meditation, serenity, gentleness, and straightforwardness: these are the ten restraints.

3.47.s:
nāśrotriyatate yajñe grāmayājihute tathā ..
striyā klībena ca hute bhuñjīyādbrāhmaṇaḥ kvacit ..204..
3.47.d:
नाश्रोत्रियतते यज्ञे ग्रामयाजिहुते तथा ॥
स्त्रिया क्लीबेन च हुते भुञ्जीयाद्ब्राह्मणः क्वचित् ॥204॥
3.47.m: A brahmin should never eat at a sacrifice performed by one not learned in the Veda, nor at one offered by a village priest, / nor at one offered by a woman or an impotent person.

3.47.s: yajño'nṛtena kṣarati tapaḥ kṣarati vismayāt ..205..
3.47.d: यज्ञोऽनृतेन क्षरति तपः क्षरति विस्मयात् ॥205॥
3.47.m: A sacrifice trickles away through falsehood; austerity trickles away through arrogance.

3.47.s:
āyurviprāpavādena dānaṃ ca parikīrttanāt ..
dharmaṃ śanaiḥ sañcinuyādvalmīkamiva puttikāḥ .. 206 ..
3.47.d:
आयुर्विप्रापवादेन दानं च परिकीर्त्तनात् ॥
धर्मं शनैः सञ्चिनुयाद्वल्मीकमिव पुत्तिकाः ॥ 206 ॥
3.47.m: Lifespan [trickles away] by speaking ill of brahmins, and giving by boasting of it. / One should slowly accumulate dharma, as termites [build] an anthill,

3.47.s:
paralokasahāyārthaṃ parapīḍāṃ vivarjayet ..
uttamairuttamairni'tyaṃ sambandhānācaretsaha ..207 ..
3.47.d:
परलोकसहायार्थं परपीडां विवर्जयेत् ॥
उत्तमैरुत्तमैर्निऽत्यं सम्बन्धानाचरेत्सह ॥207 ॥
3.47.m: For the sake of assistance in the other world, avoiding injury to others. / One should constantly form alliances with the best and highest,

3.47.s:
ninīṣuḥ kulamutkarṣamadhamānadhamām̐styajet ..
edhodakaṃ mūlaphalamannamabhyuddhṛtaṃ ca yat .. 208 ..
3.47.d:
निनीषुः कुलमुत्कर्षमधमानधमाम्̐स्त्यजेत् ॥
एधोदकं मूलफलमन्नमभ्युद्धृतं च यत् ॥ 208 ॥
3.47.m: Wishing to lead one's family to preeminence, and should abandon the lowest of the low. / Firewood, water, roots, fruits, and food that has been offered,

3.47.s:
sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyānmadhvathābhayadakṣiṇām ..
āhṛtyābhyudyatāṃ bhikṣāṃ gṛhṇīyādapracoditām ..
anyatra kulaṭāṣaṇḍhapatitastenavidviṣaḥ .. 209 ..
3.47.d:
सर्वतः प्रतिगृह्णीयान्मध्वथाभयदक्षिणाम् ॥
आहृत्याभ्युद्यतां भिक्षां गृह्णीयादप्रचोदिताम् ॥
अन्यत्र कुलटाषण्ढपतितस्तेनविद्विषः ॥ 209 ॥
3.47.m: Honey, and security as a sacrificial fee, he may accept from everywhere. / Having brought it, one should accept alms that are held out unasked, / except from an unchaste woman, a eunuch, a fallen person, a thief, or an enemy.

3.47.s:
śayyāṃ gṛhāñśubhāngandhānāpaḥ puṣpamaṇīrdadhi ..
dhānā matsyāḥ payo māṃsaṃ śākaṃ caiva tu nirṇudeta .. 3.233.210 ..
3.47.d:
शय्यां गृहाञ्शुभान्गन्धानापः पुष्पमणीर्दधि ॥
धाना मत्स्याः पयो मांसं शाकं चैव तु निर्णुदेत ॥ 3.233.210 ॥
3.47.m: A bed, houses, auspicious fragrances, water, flowers, jewels, curds, / parched grain, fish, milk, meat, and vegetables: one should not reject these.

3.47.s:
yo'nyathāsantamātmānamanyathā satsu bhāṣate ..
kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ caureṇātmāpahāriṇā .. 211 ..
3.47.d:
योऽन्यथासन्तमात्मानमन्यथा सत्सु भाषते ॥
किं तेन न कृतं पापं चौरेणात्मापहारिणा ॥ 211 ॥
3.47.m: He who describes himself to good people as being other than he really is— / what sin has not been committed by that thief who robs himself?

3.47.s:
vācyarthā niyatāssarve vāṅmūlā vāgvinissṛtāḥ ..
tāṃ tu yaḥ stenayedvācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛnnaraḥ .. .. 212 ..
3.47.d:
वाच्यर्था नियतास्सर्वे वाङ्मूला वाग्विनिस्सृताः ॥
तां तु यः स्तेनयेद्वाचं स सर्वस्तेयकृन्नरः ॥ ॥ 212 ॥
