3.47.m: All objects of thought are determined by speech; they have speech as their root and issue forth from speech. / But that man who would steal that speech is one who commits theft of everything.

3.47.s:
santānikaṃ yakṣyamāṇamadhvagaṃ sarvavedagam ..
gurvarthaṃ pitṛmātrarthaṃ svādhyāyārthamatāpinaḥ .. 213 ..
3.47.d:
सन्तानिकं यक्ष्यमाणमध्वगं सर्ववेदगम् ॥
गुर्वर्थं पितृमात्रर्थं स्वाध्यायार्थमतापिनः ॥ 213 ॥
3.47.m: [For] one wishing to marry for the sake of offspring, one about to perform a sacrifice, a traveller, one who has studied all the Vedas, / one [begging] for the sake of his teacher, for the sake of his father and mother, or for the sake of his Vedic study, these being without affliction,

3.47.s:
na caitānsnātakānvindyādbrāhmaṇāndharmabhaikṣukān ..
niḥsvebhyo deyametebhyo dānaṃ vidyā viśeṣataḥ .. 214 ..
3.47.d:
न चैतान्स्नातकान्विन्द्याद्ब्राह्मणान्धर्मभैक्षुकान् ॥
निःस्वेभ्यो देयमेतेभ्यो दानं विद्या विशेषतः ॥ 214 ॥
3.47.m: And one should not consider these graduated students and brahmins as beggars of dharma. / To these who are destitute, a gift of learning in particular is to be given.

3.47.s:
etebhyo hi dvijāgrebhyo deyamannaṃ sadakṣiṇam ..
itarebhyo bahirvedyāṃ kṛtānnaṃ deyamucyate .. 215 ..
3.47.d:
एतेभ्यो हि द्विजाग्रेभ्यो देयमन्नं सदक्षिणम् ॥
इतरेभ्यो बहिर्वेद्यां कृतान्नं देयमुच्यते ॥ 215 ॥
3.47.m: For to these foremost of twice-born, food accompanied by a sacrificial fee should be given; / to others, cooked food is said to be given outside the sacrificial altar.

3.47.s:
kṛtadāro'parāndārānbhikṣitvā yo'dhigacchati ..
ratimātraṃ phalaṃ tasya dravyadātustu santatiḥ .. 216 ..
3.47.d:
कृतदारोऽपरान्दारान्भिक्षित्वा योऽधिगच्छति ॥
रतिमात्रं फलं तस्य द्रव्यदातुस्तु सन्ततिः ॥ 216 ॥
3.47.m: He who, having already taken a wife, obtains another wife by begging [for funds], / his reward is mere sexual pleasure, while the offspring belongs to the giver of the wealth.

3.47.s:
yasya traivārṣikaṃ bhaktaṃ paryāptaṃ bhṛtyavṛttaye ..
adhikaṃ vāpi vidyeta sa somaṃ pātumarhati .. 217 ..
3.47.d:
यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यवृत्तये ॥
अधिकं वापि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति ॥ 217 ॥
3.47.m: He who has food provisions for three years, sufficient for the maintenance of his dependents, / or even more, is entitled to drink soma.

3.47.s:
ataḥ svalpīyasi dravye yaḥ somaṃ pibati dvijaḥ ..
sa pītasomapūrvo'pi tasya nāpnoti tatphalam .. 218 ..
3.47.d:
अतः स्वल्पीयसि द्रव्ये यः सोमं पिबति द्विजः ॥
स पीतसोमपूर्वोऽपि तस्य नाप्नोति तत्फलम् ॥ 218 ॥
3.47.m: A twice-born who drinks soma when possessing less wealth than this, / even though having previously drunk soma, does not attain its fruit.

3.47.s:
saktaḥ parajane dātā svajane duḥkhajīvini ..
madhvāpītau viṣāsvādaḥ sa dharmapratirūpakaḥ.. 219 ..
3.47.d:
सक्तः परजने दाता स्वजने दुःखजीविनि ॥
मध्वापीतौ विषास्वादः स धर्मप्रतिरूपकः॥ 219 ॥
3.47.m: A giver who is generous to strangers while his own people live in misery, / is drinking honey tasting of poison; he is an imitation of righteousness.

3.47.s:
bhṛtyānāmuparodhena yaḥ karotyaurdhvadaihikam ..
tadbhavatyamukhodarkaṃ jīvato'sya mṛtasya vā .. 3.233.220 ..
3.47.d:
भृत्यानामुपरोधेन यः करोत्यौर्ध्वदैहिकम् ॥
तद्भवत्यमुखोदर्कं जीवतोऽस्य मृतस्य वा ॥ 3.233.220 ॥
3.47.m: He who performs rites for the dead to the detriment of his dependents, / that results in grief for him, whether living or dead.

3.47.s:
na yajñārthe dvijaḥ śūdrādbhikṣāṃ lipseta dharmavit ..
yajamāno hi bhikṣitvā caṇḍālaḥ pretya jāyate .. 221 ..
3.47.d:
न यज्ञार्थे द्विजः शूद्राद्भिक्षां लिप्सेत धर्मवित् ॥
यजमानो हि भिक्षित्वा चण्डालः प्रेत्य जायते ॥ 221 ॥
3.47.m: A twice-born who knows dharma should not seek alms from a śūdra for the sake of a sacrifice; / for by offering a sacrifice after begging [from a śūdra], he is born as a Caṇḍāla after death.

3.47.s:
yajñārthamarthaṃ bhikṣitvā yo na sarvaṃ prayacchati ..
sa yāti bhāsatāṃ vipraḥ kākatāṃ vā śataṃ samāḥ .. 222 ..
3.47.d:
यज्ञार्थमर्थं भिक्षित्वा यो न सर्वं प्रयच्छति ॥
स याति भासतां विप्रः काकतां वा शतं समाः ॥ 222 ॥
3.47.m: Having begged wealth for the sake of a sacrifice, he who does not give it all, / that brahmin becomes a bird of prey or a crow for a hundred years.

3.47.s:
devasvaṃ brāhmaṇasvaṃ ca yo lobhānnopajīvati ..
sa pāpātmā pare loke gṛddhrocchiṣṭena jīvati .. 223 ..
3.47.d:
देवस्वं ब्राह्मणस्वं च यो लोभान्नोपजीवति ॥
स पापात्मा परे लोके गृद्ध्रोच्छिष्टेन जीवति ॥ 223 ॥
3.47.m: He who, out of greed, [wrongly] lives off the property of the gods or the property of brahmins, / that sinful soul, in the other world, subsists on the leavings of vultures.

3.47.s:
iṣṭiṃ vaiśvānarīṃ vipro nirvapedabdaparyaye ..
kṛtānāṃ paśusomānāṃ niṣkṛtyarthamasambhave .. 224 ..
3.47.d:
इष्टिं वैश्वानरीं विप्रो निर्वपेदब्दपर्यये ॥
कृतानां पशुसोमानां निष्कृत्यर्थमसम्भवे ॥ 224 ॥
3.47.m: At the change of the year, a brahmin should perform the Vaiśvānara sacrifice / as an expiation for the animal and soma sacrifices that were not performed when impossible.

3.47.s:
āpatkalpena yo dharmaṃ kurute'nāpadi dvijaḥ ..
samāpnoti phalaṃ tasya paratreti vicāritam .. 225 ..
3.47.d:
आपत्कल्पेन यो धर्मं कुरुतेऽनापदि द्विजः ॥
समाप्नोति फलं तस्य परत्रेति विचारितम् ॥ 225 ॥
3.47.m: A twice-born man who performs dharma by means of an emergency dispensation when there is no emergency / attains its fruit in the next world: so it is considered.

3.47.s:
prabhuḥ prathamakalpasya yo'nukalpeṣu vartate ..
dharmeṇa yogaṃ nāpnoti narakaṃ caiva gacchati .. 226 ..
3.47.d:
प्रभुः प्रथमकल्पस्य योऽनुकल्पेषु वर्तते ॥
धर्मेण योगं नाप्नोति नरकं चैव गच्छति ॥ 226 ॥
3.47.m: One capable of the primary rule who resorts to secondary rules / does not obtain connection with dharma and goes straight to hell.

3.47.s:
kṣattriyo bāhuvīryeṇa taredāpadamātmanaḥ ..
dhanena vaiśyaśūdrau tu japahomairdvijātayaḥ .. 227 ..
3.47.d:
क्षत्त्रियो बाहुवीर्येण तरेदापदमात्मनः ॥
धनेन वैश्यशूद्रौ तु जपहोमैर्द्विजातयः ॥ 227 ॥
3.47.m: A kṣatriya should cross over his misfortune by the strength of his arms, / a vaiśya and a śūdra by wealth, and the twice-born classes by silent prayer and oblations.

3.47.s:
na vai kanyā na yuvatirnālpavidyo na bāliśaḥ ..
hotā syādagnihotreṣu nārto nāsaṃskṛtastathā .. 228 ..
3.47.d:
न वै कन्या न युवतिर्नाल्पविद्यो न बालिशः ॥
होता स्यादग्निहोत्रेषु नार्तो नासंस्कृतस्तथा ॥ 228 ॥
3.47.m: Neither a maiden, nor a young woman, nor one of little learning, nor a fool / should be the hotṛ priest in Agnihotra rites, nor one who is afflicted, nor one unrefined by sacraments.

3.47.s:
prājāpatyamadattvāśvamagnyādheyasya dakṣiṇām ..
anāhitāgnirbhavati brāhmaṇo vibhave sati ..229..
3.47.d:
प्राजापत्यमदत्त्वाश्वमग्न्याधेयस्य दक्षिणाम् ॥
अनाहिताग्निर्भवति ब्राह्मणो विभवे सति ॥229॥
3.47.m: Without giving a horse dedicated to Prajāpati as the sacrificial fee for establishing the sacred fires, / a brahmin, when he has wealth, remains one who has not established the fires.

3.47.s:
puṇyānyanyāni kurvīta śraddadhāno jitendriyaḥ ..
na tvalpadakṣiṇairyajñairyajeteha kathaṃcana .. 3.233.230 ..
3.47.d:
पुण्यान्यन्यानि कुर्वीत श्रद्दधानो जितेन्द्रियः ॥
न त्वल्पदक्षिणैर्यज्ञैर्यजेतेह कथंचन ॥ 3.233.230 ॥
3.47.m: Endowed with faith and with senses mastered, he should perform other meritorious deeds, / but he should never sacrifice here with sacrifices that have small sacrificial fees.

3.47.s:
hantyalpadakṣiṇo yajñastasmānnālpadhano yajet ..
bālātapaṃ na seveta na divā maithunaṃ vrajet .. 231 ..
3.47.d:
हन्त्यल्पदक्षिणो यज्ञस्तस्मान्नाल्पधनो यजेत् ॥
बालातपं न सेवेत न दिवा मैथुनं व्रजेत् ॥ 231 ॥
3.47.m: A sacrifice with small sacrificial fees destroys [the patron]; therefore one of small wealth should not sacrifice. / He should not bask in the morning sun, nor engage in sexual intercourse by day.

3.47.s:
prāyaścittīyatāṃ prāpya prāyaścittaṃ samācaret ..
mātuḥ svasāraṃ vā putrīṃ parabhāryāṃ prakīrtayet ..232..
3.47.d:
प्रायश्चित्तीयतां प्राप्य प्रायश्चित्तं समाचरेत् ॥
मातुः स्वसारं वा पुत्रीं परभार्यां प्रकीर्तयेत् ॥232॥
3.47.m: Having become liable to expiation, he should perform the expiation. / He should speak of another's wife as a mother, sister, or daughter.

3.47.s:
nadīṃ tarenna bāhubhyāṃ varjayetkūpalaṅghanam ..
yathākathaṃcinnodīkṣedādityaṃ tejasāṃ nidhim .. 233 ..
3.47.d:
नदीं तरेन्न बाहुभ्यां वर्जयेत्कूपलङ्घनम् ॥
यथाकथंचिन्नोदीक्षेदादित्यं तेजसां निधिम् ॥ 233 ॥
3.47.m: He should not cross a river with his arms; he should avoid jumping over a well. / He should never look carelessly at the sun, the treasury of splendors.

3.47.s:
na kruddhasya gurorvaktraṃ naivādarśamamārjitam ..
snānabhojanapānāni vāhebhyo nācaretpunaḥ .. 234 ..
3.47.d:
न क्रुद्धस्य गुरोर्वक्त्रं नैवादर्शममार्जितम् ॥
स्नानभोजनपानानि वाहेभ्यो नाचरेत्पुनः ॥ 234 ॥
3.47.m: He should not [look at] the face of an angry teacher, nor into an unpolished mirror; / nor should he perform bathing, eating, or drinking after [his draft] animals.

3.47.s: yatnena bibhriyāddārānvāgmino'kṛpaṇāndvijān .. 235 ..
3.47.d: यत्नेन बिभ्रियाद्दारान्वाग्मिनोऽकृपणान्द्विजान् ॥ 235 ॥
3.47.m: He should diligently maintain his wives, and eloquent, non-miserly twice-born men.

3.47.s:
baddhaṅgavādikaṃ yastu yavasenodakena ca..
pratijāgarti no vipraḥ sa yāti narakaṃ mahat .. .. 236 ..
3.47.d:
बद्धङ्गवादिकं यस्तु यवसेनोदकेन च॥
प्रतिजागर्ति नो विप्रः स याति नरकं महत् ॥ ॥ 236 ॥
3.47.m: A brahmin who does not tend to tethered cattle and other animals / with grass and water goes to a great hell.

3.47.s:
nārohedviṣamaṃ śailaṃ nāvaṃ saṃśayitāṃstarūn ..
na pātayeta loṣṭena na kāṣṭhena phalaṃ drumāt .. 237 ..
3.47.d:
नारोहेद्विषमं शैलं नावं संशयितांस्तरून् ॥
न पातयेत लोष्टेन न काष्ठेन फलं द्रुमात् ॥ 237 ॥
3.47.m: He should not climb an uneven mountain, a boat, or perilous trees; / he should not bring down fruit from a tree with a clod or a stick.

3.47.s:
śiraḥsnātastu tailena nāṅgaṃ kiñcidapi spṛśet ..
vahenna bhāraṃ śirasā yugapannāgnivāriṇī .. 338 ..
3.47.d:
शिरःस्नातस्तु तैलेन नाङ्गं किञ्चिदपि स्पृशेत् ॥
वहेन्न भारं शिरसा युगपन्नाग्निवारिणी ॥ 338 ॥
3.47.m: Having bathed his head, he should not touch any limb with oil; / he should not carry a burden on his head, nor fire and water together.

3.47.s:
na toyaṃ prakṣipedvahnau vahniṃ toye tathaiva ca ..
varjayedatisauhārdaṃ bhojyānnasya ca kutsanam .. 239 ..
3.47.d:
न तोयं प्रक्षिपेद्वह्नौ वह्निं तोये तथैव च ॥
वर्जयेदतिसौहार्दं भोज्यान्नस्य च कुत्सनम् ॥ 239 ॥
3.47.m: He should not throw water into fire, nor likewise fire into water; / he should avoid excessive intimacy, and disparagement of edible food.

3.47.s:
rājadviṣṭaṃ gaṇadviṣṭaṃ lokadviṣṭaṃ vivarjayet ..
sāyaṃ prātaśca viduṣāṃ śṛṇuyātpuṣkalā giraḥ .. 3.233.240 ..
3.47.d:
राजद्विष्टं गणद्विष्टं लोकद्विष्टं विवर्जयेत् ॥
सायं प्रातश्च विदुषां शृणुयात्पुष्कला गिरः ॥ 3.233.240 ॥
3.47.m: He should avoid what is hated by the king, hated by the community, and hated by the people. / Evening and morning he should listen to the abundant words of the learned.

3.47.s:
saṃskṛtaṃ pāyasaṃ nityaṃ yavāgvāṃ kṛsaraṃ vadet ..
śmaśrukarmaṇi cāyuṣyaṃ jīvitena tathā kṛtiḥ .. 241 ..
3.47.d:
संस्कृतं पायसं नित्यं यवाग्वां कृसरं वदेत् ॥
श्मश्रुकर्मणि चायुष्यं जीवितेन तथा कृतिः ॥ 241 ॥
3.47.m: He should always call rice-milk 'refined', and gruel 'kṛsara'; / in shaving he should say 'life-prolonging', and thus of life, 'successful'.

3.47.s:
vyādhitānāṃ tu sarveṣāmāyuṣaḥ pratinandanam ..
śrāntasya viśramaśceti cāḍhyatāṃ sīriṇastathā .. 242 ..
3.47.d:
व्याधितानां तु सर्वेषामायुषः प्रतिनन्दनम् ॥
श्रान्तस्य विश्रमश्चेति चाढ्यतां सीरिणस्तथा ॥ 242 ॥
3.47.m: To all the sick, [he should utter] a greeting of long life, / and to a weary man, 'rest', and likewise 'wealth' to a plowman;

3.47.s:
āsīnasya sukhaṃ cāpi puṇyāhamapi gacchataḥ ..
devakarmapravṛttasya prāsādaṃ parikīrtayet .. 243 ..
3.47.d:
आसीनस्य सुखं चापि पुण्याहमपि गच्छतः ॥
देवकर्मप्रवृत्तस्य प्रासादं परिकीर्तयेत् ॥ 243 ॥
3.47.m: and to one seated, 'comfort', and 'auspicious day' to one who is departing; / to one engaged in rites for the gods, he should proclaim 'favor'.

3.47.s:
na jātu tvamiti brūyādāpannopi mahattaram ..
tvaṃkāro vā vadho veti vidvatsu na viśiṣyate .. 244 ..
3.47.d:
न जातु त्वमिति ब्रूयादापन्नोपि महत्तरम् ॥
त्वंकारो वा वधो वेति विद्वत्सु न विशिष्यते ॥ 244 ॥
3.47.m: Even when in distress, he should never say 'you' to an elder; / whether addressed with 'you' or struck down, among the wise there is no difference.

3.47.s:
avarāṇāṃ samānānāṃ śiṣyāṇāñcaitadiṣyate ..
eka eva careddharmaṃ na dharmadhvajiko bhavet .. 245 ..
3.47.d:
अवराणां समानानां शिष्याणाञ्चैतदिष्यते ॥
एक एव चरेद्धर्मं न धर्मध्वजिको भवेत् ॥ 245 ॥
3.47.m: This is permitted for inferiors, equals, and disciples. / He should practice dharma alone; he should not be an ostentatious displayer of dharma.

3.47.s:
arceddevānna dambhena sevetāmāyayā gurūn ..
nidhiṃ vidadhyātpārakyaṃ yatrārthaḥ śabdavāniti .. 246 ..
3.47.d:
अर्चेद्देवान्न दम्भेन सेवेतामायया गुरून् ॥
निधिं विदध्यात्पारक्यं यत्रार्थः शब्दवानिति ॥ 246 ॥
3.47.m: He should not worship the gods with hypocrisy, nor serve teachers with deceit. / He should establish a treasure for the other world, where wealth is fruitful.

3.47.s:
karma vai saphalaṃ kṛtvā gurūṇāṃ pratipādayet ..
vṛddhānnāti vadejjātu na tu sampreṣayetkvacit ..247..
3.47.d:
कर्म वै सफलं कृत्वा गुरूणां प्रतिपादयेत् ॥
वृद्धान्नाति वदेज्जातु न तु सम्प्रेषयेत्क्वचित् ॥247॥
3.47.m: Having made an action fruitful, he should dedicate it to his elders; / he should never talk back to elders, nor send them on errands anywhere.

3.47.s:
na vegito'nyakāryaḥ syānnāditvānnāni kutsayet..
muktakeśo na gacchettu svapnāhārasabhāstriyaḥ..248..
3.47.d:
न वेगितोऽन्यकार्यः स्यान्नादित्वान्नानि कुत्सयेत्॥
मुक्तकेशो न गच्छेत्तु स्वप्नाहारसभास्त्रियः॥248॥
3.47.m: Urged by bodily calls, he should not attend to other business; having eaten food, he should not disparage it. / With disheveled hair he should not go to sleep, food, assemblies, or women.

3.47.s:
pāṇinālabhya niṣkrāmedratnapūjyājyamaṇḍalam ..
pradakṣiṇantu kurvīta maṃgalyaṃ sarvadā yatiḥ..249..
3.47.d:
पाणिनालभ्य निष्क्रामेद्रत्नपूज्याज्यमण्डलम् ॥
प्रदक्षिणन्तु कुर्वीत मंगल्यं सर्वदा यतिः॥249॥
3.47.m: Touching a jewel, a venerable object, or a bowl of ghee with his hand, he should step forth. / An ascetic should always circumambulate an auspicious object clockwise.

3.47.s:
sūnāñca bandhanāgāraṃ nṛpanṛtyagṛhe tathā ..
antaḥ puraṃ ca ṛṣayo dūrataḥ parivarjayet .. 3.233.250 ..
3.47.d:
सूनाञ्च बन्धनागारं नृपनृत्यगृहे तथा ॥
अन्तः पुरं च ऋषयो दूरतः परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 3.233.250 ॥
3.47.m: A slaughterhouse, a prison, a king's dance hall, / and an inner chamber: sages should avoid these from afar.

3.47.s:
triḥ pakṣasya kṛtaśmaśrurnakhalomāni kalpayet ..
na pratisphālayedambu pāṇinā caraṇena vā .. 251 ..
3.47.d:
त्रिः पक्षस्य कृतश्मश्रुर्नखलोमानि कल्पयेत् ॥
न प्रतिस्फालयेदम्बु पाणिना चरणेन वा ॥ 251 ॥
3.47.m: Having shaved his beard three times in a fortnight, he should trim his nails and hair. / He should not splash water with his hand or foot.

3.47.s:
nāsaṃvṛtamukhaḥ kuryātkṣutamaṃgavijṛmbhaṇam ..
nādvāreṇa suhṛdveśma na dvāreṇa riporviśet .. 252 ..
3.47.d:
नासंवृतमुखः कुर्यात्क्षुतमंगविजृम्भणम् ॥
नाद्वारेण सुहृद्वेश्म न द्वारेण रिपोर्विशेत् ॥ 252 ॥
3.47.m: He should not sneeze or stretch his limbs without covering his mouth. / He should not enter a friend's house except by the door, nor an enemy's by the door.

3.47.s:
na sarpaśastraiḥ krīḍettu nadīvegaṃ vivarjayet ..
vidyātpratikṣaṇaṃ mṛtyorayathātathaceṣṭitam .. 253 ..
3.47.d:
न सर्पशस्त्रैः क्रीडेत्तु नदीवेगं विवर्जयेत् ॥
विद्यात्प्रतिक्षणं मृत्योरयथातथचेष्टितम् ॥ 253 ॥
3.47.m: He should not play with snakes or weapons; he should avoid the current of a river. / He should know every moment the unpredictable movement of death.

3.47.s:
āharejjñānamarthāṃśca naro hyamaravatsadā ..
keśairiva gṛhītastu mṛtyunā dharmamācaret .. 254 ..
3.47.d:
आहरेज्ज्ञानमर्थांश्च नरो ह्यमरवत्सदा ॥
केशैरिव गृहीतस्तु मृत्युना धर्ममाचरेत् ॥ 254 ॥
3.47.m: A man should always acquire knowledge and wealth as if he were immortal, / but he should practice dharma as if seized by the hair by death.

3.47.s:
praviśejjanasaṃbādhaṃ tathātigahanaṃ na ca ..
hema nāsaṃskṛtaṃ dhāryaṃ niśi loṣṭaṃ na ca kṣipet ..255..
3.47.d:
प्रविशेज्जनसंबाधं तथातिगहनं न च ॥
हेम नासंस्कृतं धार्यं निशि लोष्टं न च क्षिपेत् ॥255॥
3.47.m: He should not enter a crowd of people, nor an impenetrable thicket. / Unrefined gold should not be worn, nor should he throw a clod at night.

3.47.s:
ādau paṅktyāṃ na cāśnīyādvarjayedbhūmitāḍanam..
varjayecchātraśabalaṃ divā nidrāṃ tathaiva ca .. 256 ..
3.47.d:
आदौ पङ्क्त्यां न चाश्नीयाद्वर्जयेद्भूमिताडनम्॥
वर्जयेच्छात्रशबलं दिवा निद्रां तथैव च ॥ 256 ॥
3.47.m: He should not eat first in a row of diners, and he should avoid striking the ground; / he should avoid what is mixed with students, and sleep by day as well.

3.47.s:
kāmaḥ krodho bhayo harṣaṃ lobho darpastathaiva ca ..
ripavaḥ ṣaḍ vijetavyā puruṣeṇa vipaścitā .. 257 ..
3.47.d:
कामः क्रोधो भयो हर्षं लोभो दर्पस्तथैव च ॥
रिपवः षड् विजेतव्या पुरुषेण विपश्चिता ॥ 257 ॥
3.47.m: Desire, anger, fear, exhilaration, greed, and pride: / these six enemies must be conquered by a wise man.

3.47.s:
ariṣaḍvargasaṃnyāsātkuryādindriyanigrahama ..
yogakṣemaṃ sadotthānātprajñāṃ vṛddhopasevanāt .. 258 ..
3.47.d:
अरिषड्वर्गसंन्यासात्कुर्यादिन्द्रियनिग्रहम ॥
योगक्षेमं सदोत्थानात्प्रज्ञां वृद्धोपसेवनात् ॥ 258 ॥
3.47.m: Through the renunciation of the group of six enemies he should restrain the senses, / [procure] welfare through constant enterprise, and wisdom through attendance on elders.

3.47.s:
praśrayeṇa jayenmānaṃ dainyaṃ dṛṣṭāṃta saṃśrayāt ..
akrodhena jayetkrodhaṃ vinayena tvanāryatām .. 259 ..
3.47.d:
प्रश्रयेण जयेन्मानं दैन्यं दृष्टांत संश्रयात् ॥
अक्रोधेन जयेत्क्रोधं विनयेन त्वनार्यताम् ॥ 259 ॥
3.47.m: He should conquer arrogance with modesty, wretchedness by relying on good examples, / anger with freedom from anger, and ignobility with disciplined conduct.

3.47.s:
śīghratvāddhastapādaṃ ca vācamuccāraṇājjayet ..
ajñānaṃ jñānasaṃyogātkāmaṃ kāmāṃgavarjanāt .. 3.233.260 ..
3.47.d:
शीघ्रत्वाद्धस्तपादं च वाचमुच्चारणाज्जयेत् ॥
अज्ञानं ज्ञानसंयोगात्कामं कामांगवर्जनात् ॥ 3.233.260 ॥
3.47.m: He should master hands and feet through slowness of movement, and speech through [deliberate] utterance; / ignorance through union with knowledge, and lust through the avoidance of lust's incitements.

3.47.s:
dharmiṣṭhairāgamairlobhaṃ krodhaṃ maitryādvivarjayet ..
kāruṇyena jayenmānaṃ kālaṃ kāryopapattibhiḥ .. 261 ..
3.47.d:
धर्मिष्ठैरागमैर्लोभं क्रोधं मैत्र्याद्विवर्जयेत् ॥
कारुण्येन जयेन्मानं कालं कार्योपपत्तिभिः ॥ 261 ॥
3.47.m: He should avoid greed through righteous scriptures, anger through friendliness, / conquer arrogance with compassion, and time with proper timing of actions.

3.47.s:
ātmānaṃ sukhaduḥkhādyaṃ tvanabhijñāya yojayet ..
dhṛtyā śiśnodaraṃ rakṣetpāṇipādaṃ ca cakṣuṣā .. 262 ..
3.47.d:
आत्मानं सुखदुःखाद्यं त्वनभिज्ञाय योजयेत् ॥
धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत्पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा ॥ 262 ॥
3.47.m: He should engage himself without being overwhelmed by pleasure, pain, and the rest. / With steadfastness he should guard the genitals and belly, and hands and feet with the eyes;

3.47.s:
cakṣuḥśrotre ca manasā mano vācaṃ ca karmaṇā ..
deśa kālānubandhārthaṃ dharmāṇāmavirodhi yat .. 263 ..
3.47.d:
चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च कर्मणा ॥
देश कालानुबन्धार्थं धर्माणामविरोधि यत् ॥ 263 ॥
3.47.m: eyes and ears with the mind, and mind and speech with action. / For the sake of conformity with place and time, whatever is unopposed to dharma,

3.47.s:
tattatsukhaṃ niṣeveta nākasmānniḥsukhī bhavet ..
rūpasaṃdarśanaśravyarasagandhānsadā jayet..264..
3.47.d:
तत्तत्सुखं निषेवेत नाकस्मान्निःसुखी भवेत् ॥
रूपसंदर्शनश्रव्यरसगन्धान्सदा जयेत्॥264॥
3.47.m: he should enjoy that pleasure; he should not be devoid of happiness without cause. / He should constantly conquer visible forms, sounds, tastes, and scents.

3.47.s:
vasannapi sadomadhye hyasakto manasā bhavet ..
pareṣāntatra saṃdadhyātpratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ .. 265 ..
3.47.d:
वसन्नपि सदोमध्ये ह्यसक्तो मनसा भवेत् ॥
परेषान्तत्र संदध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः ॥ 265 ॥
3.47.m: Even while dwelling in an assembly, he should be unattached in mind; / he should not inflict upon others what is disagreeable to himself.

3.47.s:
kṛcchreṣvapi na tatkuryātsādhūnāṃ yadasammatam ..
jīrṇāśī ca mitāśī ca hitāśī ca tathā bhavet ..266..
3.47.d:
कृच्छ्रेष्वपि न तत्कुर्यात्साधूनां यदसम्मतम् ॥
जीर्णाशी च मिताशी च हिताशी च तथा भवेत् ॥266॥
3.47.m: Even in distress he should not do what is disapproved by the virtuous; / and he should be an eater of digested food, a moderate eater, and an eater of wholesome food.

3.47.s:
śasyate yairguṇairanyairyeranyairarjitaṃ yaśaḥ ..
uñchavṛttirbhavatyeva viparītamatastyajet .. 267 ..
3.47.d:
शस्यते यैर्गुणैरन्यैर्येरन्यैरर्जितं यशः ॥
उञ्छवृत्तिर्भवत्येव विपरीतमतस्त्यजेत् ॥ 267 ॥
3.47.m: By whichever virtues other men are praised, and by which others have acquired fame, / he should live by gleaning them, and abandon the contrary mindset.

3.47.s:
sukāruṇikamātmānaṃ khyāpayennāpi nirghṛṇam ..
deśakālau ca śaktiṃ ca janatāñcāvalokayet .. 268 ..
3.47.d:
सुकारुणिकमात्मानं ख्यापयेन्नापि निर्घृणम् ॥
देशकालौ च शक्तिं च जनताञ्चावलोकयेत् ॥ 268 ॥
3.47.m: One should make oneself known as truly compassionate, not cruel; / and one should consider place, time, power, and the people.

3.47.s:
na mṛduḥ syānna ca krūro hyubhāveva samāśrayet ..
mṛdurbhavatyavajñātaḥ tīkṣṇādudvijate janaḥ .. 269 ..
3.47.d:
न मृदुः स्यान्न च क्रूरो ह्युभावेव समाश्रयेत् ॥
मृदुर्भवत्यवज्ञातः तीक्ष्णादुद्विजते जनः ॥ 269 ॥
3.47.m: One should neither be gentle nor cruel, but indeed adopt both; / a gentle person is treated with contempt, and people tremble before a severe one.

3.47.s:
anālakṣitacittaḥ syānnaikānte kiñcidācaret ..
vidyātparasya randhrāṇi svaraṃdhraṃ chādayetpunaḥ .. 3.233.270 ..
3.47.d:
अनालक्षितचित्तः स्यान्नैकान्ते किञ्चिदाचरेत् ॥
विद्यात्परस्य रन्ध्राणि स्वरंध्रं छादयेत्पुनः ॥ 3.233.270 ॥
3.47.m: One's mind should remain imperceptible; one should perform nothing in solitude. / One should know the weaknesses of another, yet cover one's own weakness.

3.47.s:
gūhetkūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣedātmānamātmanā ..
vāgādīni sahāyāni kṛtvā prajñāṃ ca mantriṇam .. 271 ..
3.47.d:
गूहेत्कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेदात्मानमात्मना ॥
वागादीनि सहायानि कृत्वा प्रज्ञां च मन्त्रिणम् ॥ 271 ॥
3.47.m: One should conceal one's limbs like a tortoise and protect oneself by oneself, / making speech and the [other senses] allies and wisdom the counselor.

3.47.s:
dharmakāmasamṛddhyarthaṃ dāsādyarthaḥ pumānbhavet ..
arthānarthau samāsādya harṣadainye vivarjayet..272..
3.47.d:
धर्मकामसमृद्ध्यर्थं दासाद्यर्थः पुमान्भवेत् ॥
अर्थानर्थौ समासाद्य हर्षदैन्ये विवर्जयेत्॥272॥
3.47.m: For the increase of dharma and pleasure, a man should have slaves and wealth; / encountering profit and loss, one should avoid elation and despair.

3.47.s:
duḥkhe duḥkhādhikānpaśyetsukhe paśyetsukhādhikāna ..
natvevaṃ mūḍhavaddadhyādātmānaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ..273..
3.47.d:
दुःखे दुःखाधिकान्पश्येत्सुखे पश्येत्सुखाधिकान ॥
नत्वेवं मूढवद्दध्यादात्मानं सुखदुःखयोः॥273॥
3.47.m: In sorrow, one should look to those with greater sorrow; in joy, one should look to those with greater joy; / one should not, like a fool, surrender oneself to joy and sorrow.

3.47.s:
harṣasthānasahasrāṇi śokasthānaśatāni ca ..
divasedivase mūḍhamāviśanti na paṇḍitam..274 ..
3.47.d:
हर्षस्थानसहस्राणि शोकस्थानशतानि च ॥
दिवसेदिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम्॥274 ॥
3.47.m: A thousand grounds for elation and a hundred grounds for grief / enter a fool day after day, but not a wise man.

3.47.s:
na tatkurvīta yasyānte harṣopālambhamāpnuyāt ..
ajñānaprabhavo mohastasmādrāgaḥ pravartate ..275..
3.47.d:
न तत्कुर्वीत यस्यान्ते हर्षोपालम्भमाप्नुयात् ॥
अज्ञानप्रभवो मोहस्तस्माद्रागः प्रवर्तते ॥275॥
3.47.m: One should not do that at the end of which one would meet with the reproach of elation. / Delusion arises from ignorance; from that, attachment proceeds;

3.47.s:
rāgādveṣastataḥ krodhaḥ krodhānmāno'bhijāyate ..
mānādapārthakaṃ karma karmato'śubhalakṣaṇam .. 276 ..
3.47.d:
रागाद्वेषस्ततः क्रोधः क्रोधान्मानोऽभिजायते ॥
मानादपार्थकं कर्म कर्मतोऽशुभलक्षणम् ॥ 276 ॥
3.47.m: from attachment arises aversion, from that anger, from anger pride is born; / from pride comes useless action, and from action that which is marked by inauspiciousness,

3.47.s:
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhaśokapravarttanam ..
apramādo vṛddhasevā tatprajñāmūlamiṣyate .. 277 ..
3.47.d:
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखशोकप्रवर्त्तनम् ॥
अप्रमादो वृद्धसेवा तत्प्रज्ञामूलमिष्यते ॥ 277 ॥
3.47.m: the occurrence of birth, death, old age, disease, sorrow, and grief. / Vigilance and service to elders are held to be the root of wisdom.

3.47.s:
jñānāddharmaḥ sukhaṃ dharmānniḥśreyo'bhyudayātmakam ..
iṣṭendriyārthasaṃyogo bhavedudayalakṣaṇam .. 278 ..
3.47.d:
ज्ञानाद्धर्मः सुखं धर्मान्निःश्रेयोऽभ्युदयात्मकम् ॥
इष्टेन्द्रियार्थसंयोगो भवेदुदयलक्षणम् ॥ 278 ॥
3.47.m: From knowledge arises dharma, from dharma happiness, consisting of the highest good and prosperity; / contact with desired sense-objects is the mark of prosperity.

3.47.s:
nāruntudaḥ syādanṛśaṃsavādī nahīnataḥ paramabhyādadīta ..
yayāsya vācā para udvijeta na tāṃ vadeduṣatīṃ pāpalokām .. 279 ..
3.47.d:
नारुन्तुदः स्यादनृशंसवादी नहीनतः परमभ्याददीत ॥
ययास्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत न तां वदेदुषतीं पापलोकाम् ॥ 279 ॥
3.47.m: One should not wound the vitals, one should speak gently, and one should never take what belongs to another from an inferior; / by whatever speech another is agitated, one should not speak that bitter, hell-causing [speech].

3.47.s:
vāksāyakā vadanānniṣpatanti yairāhataḥ śocati rātryahāni..
parasya nurmarmasu te patanti na tāndhīro'vasṛjedvai pareṣu..3.233.280..
3.47.d:
वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि॥
परस्य नुर्मर्मसु ते पतन्ति न तान्धीरोऽवसृजेद्वै परेषु॥3.233.280॥
3.47.m: Arrows of speech fly forth from the mouth, struck by which a person grieves night and day; / they fall upon another's vital spots; a steadfast man should never release them against others.

3.47.s:
priyāṇi loke śṛṇute priyaṃvadaḥ priyāṇi cāpnoti priyāṇi cāśnute ..
priyaśca sarvasya janasya jāyate janānurāgaprabhavā hi saṃpadaḥ .. 281..
3.47.d:
प्रियाणि लोके शृणुते प्रियंवदः प्रियाणि चाप्नोति प्रियाणि चाश्नुते ॥
प्रियश्च सर्वस्य जनस्य जायते जनानुरागप्रभवा हि संपदः ॥ 281॥
3.47.m: One who speaks pleasantly hears pleasant things in the world, obtains pleasant things, and enjoys pleasant things; / he becomes dear to everyone, for fortune springs from the affection of the people.

3.47.s:
ācārayuktastridivaṃ prayāti ācāravāneva bhavatyarogaḥ ..
ācāravāneva cirantu jīvedācāravāneva bhunakti lakṣaṇam .. 282 ..
3.234
haṃsa uvāca ..
prāyaścittīyatāṃ prāpya daivātpūrvakṛtena vā ..
na saṃsargaṃ vrajetsadbhiḥ prāyaścitte'kṛte naraḥ .. 1 ..
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvāṅganāgamaḥ ..
mahānti pātakānyāhuḥ saṃyogamapi taiḥ saha .. 2 ..
anṛtaṃ ca samutkarṣe rājagāmi ca paiśunam ..
guroścālīkanirbandhaḥ samāni brahmahatyayā..3..
brahmojjhatā vedanindā kauṭasākṣyaṃ suhṛdvadhaḥ..
garhitānnādyayorjagdhiḥ surāpānasamāni ṣaṭ ..4..
nikṣepasyāpaharaṇaṃ narāśvarajatasya ca..
bhūmivajramaṇīnāṃ ca rukmasteyasamaṃ smṛtam ..5..
retasekaḥ sayonīṣu kumārīṣvantyajāsu ca..
sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣu gurutalpasamaṃ viduḥ .. 6 ..
3.47.d:
आचारयुक्तस्त्रिदिवं प्रयाति आचारवानेव भवत्यरोगः ॥
आचारवानेव चिरन्तु जीवेदाचारवानेव भुनक्ति लक्षणम् ॥ 282 ॥
3.234
हंस उवाच ॥
प्रायश्चित्तीयतां प्राप्य दैवात्पूर्वकृतेन वा ॥
न संसर्गं व्रजेत्सद्भिः प्रायश्चित्तेऽकृते नरः ॥ 1 ॥
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वाङ्गनागमः ॥
महान्ति पातकान्याहुः संयोगमपि तैः सह ॥ 2 ॥
अनृतं च समुत्कर्षे राजगामि च पैशुनम् ॥
गुरोश्चालीकनिर्बन्धः समानि ब्रह्महत्यया॥3॥
ब्रह्मोज्झता वेदनिन्दा कौटसाक्ष्यं सुहृद्वधः॥
गर्हितान्नाद्ययोर्जग्धिः सुरापानसमानि षट् ॥4॥
निक्षेपस्यापहरणं नराश्वरजतस्य च॥
भूमिवज्रमणीनां च रुक्मस्तेयसमं स्मृतम् ॥5॥
रेतसेकः सयोनीषु कुमारीष्वन्त्यजासु च॥
सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु गुरुतल्पसमं विदुः ॥ 6 ॥
3.47.m:
Endowed with proper conduct, one goes to heaven; possessing proper conduct alone, one is free from disease; / possessing proper conduct alone, one lives long; possessing proper conduct alone, one enjoys good fortune.
3.234 / Haṃsa said: / Having incurred the need for expiation through fate or past deeds, / a man should not associate with good people until the expiation is performed.
Killing a brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, and violating the teacher's bed— / these they call the great sins, and association with those [who commit them] as well.
A lie told for self-exaltation, calumny that reaches the king, / and false accusation of a guru are equal to killing a brahmin.
Abandoning the Veda, reviling the Veda, false testimony, slaying a friend, / and eating forbidden food or drink—these six are equal to drinking liquor.
Misappropriating a deposit, and [stealing] a man, a horse, silver, / land, diamonds, or gems, is considered equal to the theft of gold.
Ejaculating seed into uterine [kinswomen], virgins, outcaste women, / and the wives of a friend or a son, they consider equal to violating the guru's bed.

3.47.s:
govadho'yājyasaṃyājyaṃ pāradāryātmavikrayaḥ ..
gurumātṛparityāgaḥ svādhyāyāgnyoḥ sutasya ca ..7..
parivittitānujenūḍhe paravedanameva ca ..
tayordānaṃ ca kanyāyāstayoreva ca yājanam .. 8 ..
kanyāyādūṣaṇaṃ caiva vārdhuṣyaṃ vratalopanam ..
taḍāgāgamadārāṇāmapatyasya ca vikrayaḥ.. 9 ..
vrātyatā bāndhavatyāgo bhṛtādhyāpanameva ca ..
bhṛtāccādhyayanādānamapaṇyānāṃ ca vikrayaḥ..3.234.10..
sarvakāryeṣvadhīkāro mahāyantrapravartanam ..
hiṃsroṣadhistriyājīvo'bhicāro mūlakarma ca..11..
indhanārthamaśuṣkāṇāṃ drumāṇāmavapātanam ..
ātmārthaṃ ca kriyārambho nindinānnādanaṃ tathā ..12..
anāhitāgnitā steyamṛṇānāṃ cānapākriyā ..
asacchāstrābhigamanaṃ kauśīlavyasya ca kriyā .. 13..
dhānyakupyapaśusteyaṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇam ..
strīśūdraviṭkṣattravadho nāstikyaṃ copapātakam .. 14 ..
3.47.d:
गोवधोऽयाज्यसंयाज्यं पारदार्यात्मविक्रयः ॥
गुरुमातृपरित्यागः स्वाध्यायाग्न्योः सुतस्य च ॥7॥
परिवित्तितानुजेनूढे परवेदनमेव च ॥
तयोर्दानं च कन्यायास्तयोरेव च याजनम् ॥ 8 ॥
कन्यायादूषणं चैव वार्धुष्यं व्रतलोपनम् ॥
तडागागमदाराणामपत्यस्य च विक्रयः॥ 9 ॥
व्रात्यता बान्धवत्यागो भृताध्यापनमेव च ॥
भृताच्चाध्ययनादानमपण्यानां च विक्रयः॥3.234.10॥
सर्वकार्येष्वधीकारो महायन्त्रप्रवर्तनम् ॥
हिंस्रोषधिस्त्रियाजीवोऽभिचारो मूलकर्म च॥11॥
इन्धनार्थमशुष्काणां द्रुमाणामवपातनम् ॥
आत्मार्थं च क्रियारम्भो निन्दिनान्नादनं तथा ॥12॥
अनाहिताग्निता स्तेयमृणानां चानपाक्रिया ॥
असच्छास्त्राभिगमनं कौशीलव्यस्य च क्रिया ॥ 13॥
धान्यकुप्यपशुस्तेयं मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणम् ॥
स्त्रीशूद्रविट्क्षत्त्रवधो नास्तिक्यं चोपपातकम् ॥ 14 ॥

3.47.s:
brāhmaṇasya rujaḥkṛtyaṃ ghrātiraghreyamadyayoḥ ..
jaihmyaṃ puṃsi ca maithunyaṃ jātibhraṃśakaraṃ smṛtam..15..
kharāśvoṣṭramṛgebhānāmajāvikavadhastathā ..
saṃkarīkaraṇaṃ jñeyaṃ mīnāhimahiṣasya ca .. 16 ..
ninditebhyo dhanādānaṃ vāṇijyaṃ śūdra sevanam ..
apātrīkaraṇaṃ jñeyamasatyasya ca bhāṣaṇam .. 17 ..
kṛmikīṭavayohatyā madyānugatabhojanam ..
phalaidhaḥkusumasteyamadhairyaṃ ca malāpaham .. .. 18 ..
etānyanyāni sarvāṇi yathoktāni pṛthakpṛthak ..
dhairyavratairapohyante tāni me sannibodhata .. 19 ..
brahmahā dvādaśasamāḥ kuṭiṃ kṛtvā vane vaset ..

3.47.d:
ब्राह्मणस्य रुजःकृत्यं घ्रातिरघ्रेयमद्ययोः ॥
जैह्म्यं पुंसि च मैथुन्यं जातिभ्रंशकरं स्मृतम्॥15॥
खराश्वोष्ट्रमृगेभानामजाविकवधस्तथा ॥
संकरीकरणं ज्ञेयं मीनाहिमहिषस्य च ॥ 16 ॥
निन्दितेभ्यो धनादानं वाणिज्यं शूद्र सेवनम् ॥
अपात्रीकरणं ज्ञेयमसत्यस्य च भाषणम् ॥ 17 ॥
कृमिकीटवयोहत्या मद्यानुगतभोजनम् ॥
फलैधःकुसुमस्तेयमधैर्यं च मलापहम् ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
एतान्यन्यानि सर्वाणि यथोक्तानि पृथक्पृथक् ॥
धैर्यव्रतैरपोह्यन्ते तानि मे सन्निबोधत ॥ 19 ॥
ब्रह्महा द्वादशसमाः कुटिं कृत्वा वने वसेत् ॥
भैक्ष्याश्यात्मविशुद्ध्यर्थं कृत्वा शवशिरोध्वजम् ॥ 3.234.20 ॥
लक्षं शस्त्रभृतां वा स्याद्विदुषामिच्छयात्मनः ॥
प्राश्येदात्मानमग्नौ वा समिद्धे त्रिरवाक्शिराः ॥ 21 ॥
3.47.m:
Inflicting pain on a brahmin, smelling things that should not be smelled or liquor, / dishonesty, and intercourse with a man are declared to cause loss of caste.
Slaying a donkey, horse, camel, deer, elephant, goat, or sheep, / and [slaying] a fish, snake, or buffalo is to be known as causing mixture of caste.
Receiving wealth from condemned persons, commerce, serving a śūdra, / and uttering a falsehood are to be known as rendering one unfit to receive gifts.
Killing worms, insects, or birds, eating food tainted by liquor, / stealing fruit, firewood, or flowers, and lack of steadfastness are impurity-producing sins.
All these and others, individually stated, / are removed by vows of steadfastness; listen to them from me:
A killer of a brahmin should dwell in the forest for twelve years, having built a hut, / eating alms food for self-purification, carrying a skull upon a staff as his standard.
Or he may offer himself as a target to weapon-bearers, by his own wish, who are skilled; / or he may cast himself into a kindled fire head downwards three times.

यजेत वाश्वमेधेन स्वर्जिता गोसवेन वा ॥
अभिजिद्विश्वजिद्भ्यां वा त्रिवृताग्निष्टुतापि वा ॥ 22 ॥
जपन्वान्यतमं वेदं योजनानां शतं व्रजेत् ॥
ब्रह्महत्यापनोदाय मितभुङ नियतेन्द्रियः ॥ 23 ॥
सर्वस्वं वा वेदविदे ब्राह्मणाश्चोपपादयेत् ॥
धनं हि जीवनायालं गृहं वा सपरिच्छदम् ॥ 24॥
हविष्यभुग्वानुसरेत्प्रतिस्रोतः सरस्वतीम् ॥
जपेद्वा नियताहारस्त्रिर्वै वेदस्य संहिताम् ॥ 25 ॥
कृतवापनो निवसेद्ग्रामान्ते गोव्रजेऽपि वा ॥
आश्रमे वृक्षमूले वा गोब्राह्मणहिते रतः ॥ 26 ॥
ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा सम्यक् प्राणान्परित्यजेत् ॥
मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्याया गोब्राह्मणहिते रतः ॥ 27 ॥
त्रिवारं प्रतिरोद्धा वा सर्वस्वमवजित्य वा ॥
विप्रस्य तन्निमित्ते वा प्राणालाभे विमुच्यते ॥ 28 ॥
एवं दृढव्रतो नित्यं ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः ॥
समाप्ते द्वादशे वर्षे ब्रह्महत्यां विमुञ्चति ॥ 29 ॥
3.47.m:
Or he may sacrifice with the horse-sacrifice, the Svarjit, or the Gosava, / or with the Abhijit and Viśvajit, or with the Trivṛt or the Agniṣṭut.
Or muttering any one of the Vedas, he may walk a hundred yojanas / to remove the murder of a brahmin, eating moderately with restrained senses.
Or he should bestow his entire property upon a brahmin who knows the Veda, / or wealth sufficient for a livelihood, or a house with its furnishings.
Or eating sacrificial food, he should follow the Sarasvatī against the current, / or with controlled diet, mutter three times the Saṃhitā of the Veda.
Having shaved his head, he should dwell at the edge of a village, or in a cattle pen, / or in a hermitage, or at the root of a tree, devoted to the welfare of cows and brahmins.
For the sake of a brahmin or for the sake of cows, he may duly abandon his life; / devoted to the welfare of cows and brahmins, he is freed from the murder of a brahmin.
Or having blocked [the enemies of a brahmin] three times, or having recovered all the property / of a brahmin, or on that account losing his life, he is freed.
Thus steadfast in his vow, always celibate and collected, / when the twelfth year is completed, he is freed from the killing of a brahmin.

3.47.d:
शिष्ट्वा वा भूमिदेवानां नरदेवसमागमे ॥
स्वमेनोऽवभृथस्नातो हयमेधे विमुच्यते ॥ 3.234.30 ॥
धर्मस्य ब्राह्मणो मूलमग्रं राजन्य उच्यते ॥
तस्मात्समागमे तेषामेनो विख्याप्य शुध्यति ॥ 31 ॥
ब्राह्मणः सम्भवेनैव देवानामपि दैवतम् ॥
प्रमाणं चैव लोकस्य ब्रह्मात्रैव हि कारणम् ॥ 32 ॥
तेषां वेदविदो ब्रूयुस्त्रयोऽप्येनःसु निष्कृतिम् ॥
स तेषां पावनाय स्यात्पवित्रा विदुषां हि वाक् ॥ 33 ॥
अतोऽन्यतममास्थाय विधिं विप्रः समाहितः ॥
ब्रह्महत्याकृतं पापं व्यपोहत्यात्मवत्तया ॥34॥
हत्वा गर्भमविज्ञातं चैतदेवव्रतं चरेत्॥
राजन्यवैश्यौ चेज्ज्ञानावात्रेयीमेव च स्त्रियम् ॥35॥
उक्त्वा चैवानृतं साक्ष्ये प्रतिरुध्य गुरूंस्तथा ॥
अपहृत्य च निक्षेपं कृत्वा च स्त्रीसुहृद्वधम् ॥ 36 ॥
3.47.m:
Or having declared his own sin in an assembly of earthly gods and a king, / he is freed when bathed at the concluding bath (avabhṛtha) of a horse sacrifice.
The brahmin is said to be the root of dharma, and the kṣatriya its top; / therefore, having proclaimed his sin in their assembly, he becomes pure.
A brahmin, merely by his birth, is a deity even to the gods / and an authority for the world; indeed, the Veda is the reason here.
Even three of them who know the Veda might state the expiation for sins; / that would serve for their purification, for the word of the learned is purifying.
Therefore, adopting one or another rule, a collected brahmin, / through self-possession, dispels the sin caused by the killing of a brahmin.
Having killed an unknown embryo, he should perform this very vow; / likewise if [he has killed] a kṣatriya or vaiśya who had studied [the Veda], and a woman who has bathed after her period.
And having spoken an untruth in testimony, having obstructed teachers, / having stolen a deposit, and having committed the murder of a woman or a friend;

इयं विशुद्धिरुदिता प्रमाप्याकामतो द्विजम् ॥
कामतो ब्राह्मणवधे निष्कृतिर्न विधीयते ॥ 37 ॥
सुरां पीत्वा द्विजो मोहादग्निवर्णा सुरां पिबेत् ॥
तया स काये निर्दग्धे मुच्यते किल्बिषात्ततः॥ ॥38॥
गोमूत्रमग्निवर्णं वा पिबेदुदकमेव वा ॥
पयो घृतं वा मरणाद्गोशकृद्रसमेव वा ॥ 39 ॥
कणान्वा भक्षयेदब्दं पिण्याकं वा सकृन्निशि ॥
सुरापानोपनोदार्थं वालवासा जटी ध्वजी ॥ 3.234.40 ॥
सुरा वै मलमन्नानां पाप्मा च मलमुच्यते ॥
तस्माद्ब्राह्मणराजन्यौ वैश्यस्तु न सुरां पिबेत् ॥ 41 ॥
गौडी माध्वी च पैष्टी च विज्ञेया त्रिविधा सुरा ॥
यथैवैका तथैवान्या न पातव्या द्विजातिभिः ॥ 42 ॥
यक्षरक्षःपिशाचान्नं मद्यं मांसं सुरासवम् ॥
तद्ब्राह्मणेन नाक्तव्यं देवानामश्नता हविः ॥ 43 ॥
3.47.m:
this purification is declared for having killed a twice-born unintentionally; / for intentionally slaying a brahmin, no expiation is prescribed.
Having drunk wine out of delusion, a twice-born should drink wine the colour of fire; / when his body is thoroughly burnt by that, he is freed from the sin.
Or he should drink cow’s urine the colour of fire, or water, / or milk, or clarified butter, or the juice of cow dung, until death.
Or he should eat grain-particles for a year, or oil-cake once at night, / to remove the drinking of wine, wearing a garment of hair, with matted locks, bearing a staff.
Wine is indeed the dirt of foods, and sin is called dirt; / therefore, a brahmin, a kṣatriya, and a vaiśya should not drink wine.
Wine should be known as threefold: made from molasses, made from honey, and made from flour; / just as the one is, so is another: they must not be drunk by the twice-born.
Liquor, meat, wine, and spirits are the food of Yakṣas, Rakṣases, and Piśācas; / that should not be consumed by a brahmin eating the oblation of the gods.

अमेध्ये वा पतेन्मत्तो वैदिकं वाप्युदाहरेत् ॥

यस्य कायगतं ब्रह्म मद्येनाप्लाव्यते सकृत् ॥
तस्य व्यपैति ब्राह्मण्यं शूद्रत्वं च स गच्छति ॥ 45 ॥
एषा विचित्राभिहिता सुरापानस्य निष्कृतिः ॥

स्वकर्म ख्यापयन्ब्रूयाद्भवान्मामनुशास्त्विति ॥ 47 ॥
गृहीत्वा मुसलं राजा सकृद्धन्यात्तु तं स्वयम् ॥
वधेन शुध्यति स्तेनो ब्राह्मणस्तपसैव वा ॥ 48 ॥
तपसापनुनुत्सुस्तु सुवर्णस्तेयजं मलम् ॥
चीरवासा द्विजोरण्ये चरेद्ब्रह्महणो व्रतम् ॥ 49 ॥
एतैर्व्रतैरपोहेत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः ॥
गुरुस्त्रीगमनीयं तु व्रतैरेतैरपानुदेत् ॥ 3.234.50 ॥
3.47.m:
Intoxicated, he might fall into what is impure, or he might recite Vedic text, / or, deluded by intoxication, a brahmin might do some other forbidden act.
In whose body the Veda, having entered, is flooded even once with liquor, / his brahminhood departs, and he goes to the state of a śūdra.
This manifold expiation for the drinking of wine has been declared; / hereafter I shall explain the expiation for the theft of gold.
A brahmin possessing stolen gold, approaching the king / and proclaiming his own deed, should say: ‘May your majesty punish me.’
Taking a pestle, the king himself should strike him once; / through death the thief is purified, or a brahmin through asceticism alone.
Desiring to remove through asceticism the dirt born of the theft of gold, / a twice-born, dressed in rags, should perform in the forest the vow of a slayer of a brahmin.
Through these vows a twice-born may dispel the sin caused by theft; / but one who has had intercourse with the wife of an elder should remove it by these vows:

गुरुतल्प्यभिभाष्यैनः कुंभे स्वप्यादयोमये ॥
सूर्मीं ज्वलन्तीं वाश्लिष्य मृत्युना स विशुध्यति ॥ 23 ॥

उपपातकिनस्त्वेवं विविधैर्नियमैरपि ॥ 55 ॥
उपपातकसंयुक्तो गोघ्नो मासं यवान्पिबेत् ॥
कृतवापो वसेद्गोष्ठे चर्मणा तेन संवृतः ॥ 56 ॥
चतुर्थकालमश्नीयादक्षारलवणं मितम् ॥
गोमूत्रेणाचरेत्स्नानं द्वौ मासौ नियतेन्द्रियः ॥ 57 ॥
दिवानुगच्छेत्ता गास्तु तिष्ठन्नूर्ध्वं रजः पिबेत् ॥
शुभ्रूषित्वा नमस्कृत्य रात्रौ वीरासनं वसेत् ॥ 58 ॥
3.47.m:
Having proclaimed the sin, he who has violated the bed of an elder should lie down in an iron pot, / or embracing a glowing iron image, he is purified by death;
or having himself cut off his penis and testicles and placed them in his cupped hands, / he should set out towards the southwest direction, walking straight until he collapses.
Or carrying a staff tipped with a skull, clad in rags, with a beard, in a solitary forest, / he should perform the Prājāpatya penance for one year, being collected;
or with restrained senses, he should practice the Cāndrāyaṇa for three months, / with sacrificial food or with barley gruel, for the removal of [the sin of] violating the bed of an elder.
By these vows those guilty of mortal sins should dispel their impurities; / and those guilty of secondary sins [should do so] likewise through various observances.
He who is afflicted with a secondary sin of killing a cow should drink barley gruel for a month; / with shaved head, he should live in a cow-pen, covered with that [cow’s] hide.
He should eat a measured amount without pungent spices or salt at the fourth meal-time; / with restrained senses, he should bathe in cow’s urine for two months.
By day he should follow those cows, and standing upright, inhale their dust; / having served and honoured them, at night he should sit in the vīrāsana posture.

3.47.m:
When they stand, he should stand; when they walk, he should follow them; / and when they are seated, he should sit down likewise, self-restrained and free from malice.
If [a cow is] sick, or attacked by dangers such as lions and tigers, / or fallen, or stuck in mud, he should rescue her with all his might.
In heat, in rain, or in cold, or when the wind blows violently, / he should not protect himself without first protecting the cow according to his ability.
Whether in his own or another’s house, field, or threshing floor, / he should not report her eating [crops] or nursing her calf.
The killer of a cow who follows cows according to this rule / dispels in three months the sin caused by the killing of a cow.
Having observed the vow well, he should give [ten] cows with a bull as the eleventh; / if these are not available, he should offer all his possessions to those who know the Veda.
Twice-born guilty of secondary sins should perform this very vow, / or the Cāndrāyaṇa for the purification of one who has broken his vow of celibacy (avakīrṇin).
One who has broken his vow of celibacy, however, should sacrifice to Nirṛti at night / at a crossroads with a one-eyed donkey according to the rite of a pākayajña.

एतस्मिन्नेनसि प्राप्ते वसित्वा गर्दभाजिनम् ॥

3.47.m:
Having offered the oblations into the fire according to rule, and at the end with the Samidh verse, / he should offer oblations of clarified butter to Vāta, Indra, Guru, and Agni.
The intentional emission of semen by a twice-born while bound by a vow / is declared by the knowers of dharma and speakers of the Veda to be a transgression of the vow.
The Maruts, Puruhūta, Guru, and Pāvaka: / to these four goes the Vedic splendour of one who has broken his vow.
When this sin has occurred, having put on the skin of an ass, / he should go begging at seven houses, proclaiming his own deed.
Subsisting on the alms obtained from them, eating once a day, / and bathing at the three junctures of the day, he becomes purified in a year.
Having committed intentionally any act that causes loss of caste, / he should perform the Sāntapana penance; if unintentionally, the Prājāpatya penance.
For deeds causing mixture [of castes] or rendering one unworthy to receive gifts, one [should observe] the lunar fast [subsisting on] cow-products for a month; / for deeds causing defilement, one should take hot barley-gruel for three days.

तुरीयं ब्रह्महत्यायाः क्षत्त्रियस्य वधे स्मृतम् ॥
वैश्येऽष्टमांशं वृत्तस्थे शूद्रे ज्ञेयं तु षोडशम्॥ 74 ॥
अकामतस्तु राजन्यं विनिपात्य द्विजोत्तमः ॥

त्र्यब्दं चरेद्वा नियतो जटी ब्रह्महणो व्रतम् ॥
वसन्दूरतरे ग्रामे वृक्षमूलनिकेतनः ॥76॥
एतदेव चरेदब्दं प्रायश्चित्तं द्विजोत्तमः ॥
प्रमाप्य वैश्यं वृत्तस्थं दद्याद्वै शतकं गवाम् ॥ 77॥
एतदेव व्रतं कृत्स्नं षण्मासाञ्छूद्रहा चरेत् ॥
वृषभैकादशा वापि दद्याद्विप्राय गाः सिताः ॥78॥
मार्जारनकुलं हत्वा चाषं मण्डूकमेव च॥
श्वगोधोलूककाकांश्च शूद्रहत्याव्रतं चरेत् ॥79॥
पयः पिबेत्त्रिरात्रं वा योजनं वाध्वनो व्रजेत् ॥
उपस्पृशेत्स्रवन्त्यां वा सूक्तं वाब्दैवतं जपेत् ॥3.234.80॥
3.47.m:
A fourth of [the penance for] killing a brahmin is prescribed for killing a kṣatriya; / an eighth part for a vaiśya established in good conduct, but a sixteenth is known for a śūdra.
If a foremost twice-born slays a kṣatriya unintentionally, / he should give a thousand cows together with a bull for the purification of himself;
or, restrained, wearing matted hair, he should observe the vow of a brahmin-slayer for three years, / dwelling in a village far away, having his abode at the foot of a tree.
A foremost twice-born should observe this very penance for a year / having killed a vaiśya established in good conduct, or he should give a hundred cows.
A slayer of a śūdra should observe this entire vow for six months, / or he should give to a brahmin white cows with a bull as the eleventh.
Having killed a cat, a mongoose, a blue jay, or a frog, / or a dog, an iguana, an owl, or a crow, he should observe the vow for killing a śūdra;
or he should drink milk for three nights, or walk the path of a yojana, / or bathe in a flowing stream, or recite a hymn addressed to the waters.

एकैकशश्चरेत्कृच्छ्रं द्विजः पापापनुत्तये ॥87॥
3.47.m:
Having killed a snake, a foremost twice-born should give a spade made of black iron; / for a eunuch, a load of straw and one māṣaka of lead.
For a boar, a pot of ghee; but a droṇa of sesame for a partridge; / for a parrot, a two-year-old calf; and having killed a curlew, a three-year-old [calf].
Having killed a swan, a crane, a heron, and a peacock, / a monkey, a hawk, or a vulture, he should present a cow to a brahmin.
Having killed a horse, he should give a garment, or five dark-blue bulls; / a goat and a sheep [for killing each other], a draft-ox [for killing an ox], and a one-year-old [calf] having killed a donkey.
Having killed a carnivorous deer, he should give a milch cow; / for a non-carnivorous one, a heifer; but having killed a camel, a kṛṣṇala [of gold].
He should give respectively a deer-skin, a bow, a goat, or a sheep for purification / upon killing a woman of any of the four varnas who is living in the forest.
A twice-born who is unable to effect expiation by giving gifts for [killing] snakes and the like / should perform a kṛcchra penance for each one in order to remove the sin.

कृष्टजानामौषधानां जातानाञ्च स्वयं वने॥

3.47.m:
Upon slaying a thousand creatures possessing bones, / or a full cart-load of boneless ones, he should observe the vow for killing a śūdra.
He should give something small to a brahmin for the killing of boned [creatures]; / and for boneless creatures, breath-control is the purification.
For cutting down fruit-bearing trees, a hundred Ṛgvedic verses are to be recited, / and [the same for cutting] shrubs, climbing vines, creepers, and flowering plants.
For [killing] creatures born in food and the like, or those born everywhere in liquids, / and those originating in fruits and flowers, the sipping of ghee is the purification.
For needlessly destroying herbs born of cultivation / or those grown of themselves in the forest, he should follow [a cow] or keep a vow of [drinking only] milk for one day.
By these vows, the sin arising from injury is to be dispelled. / Hear completely [about the sin] committed knowingly or unknowingly in eating improper food and the like.
Having drunk spirituous liquor through ignorance, he is purified by the sacrament alone; / [if drunk] intentionally, there is no expiation; it terminates only with life: such is the established rule.

3.47.s:
apaḥ surābhājanasthā madyabhāṇḍasthitāstathā ..
pañcarātraṃ vasetpītvā śaṅkhapuṣpīśṛtaṃ payaḥ ..95 ..
spṛṣṭvā dattvā ca madirāṃ vidhivanpratigṛhya ca ..
śūdrocchiṣṭāśca pītvāpaḥ kuśavāri pibettryaham..96..
brāhmaṇastu surāpasya gandhamāghrāya somapaḥ ..
prāṇānapsu trirācamya ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśuddhyati ..97..
ajñānātprāśya viṇmūtraṃ surāsaṃspṛṣṭameva ca ..
punaḥ saṃskāramarhanti trayo varṇā dvijātayaḥ..98..
vasanaṃ mekhalā daṇḍaṃ bhaikṣyacaryā vratāni ca ..
nivartante dvijātīnāṃ punaḥsaṃskārakarmaṇi ..99..
abhojyānāntu bhuktānnaṃ strīśūdrocchiṣṭameva ca ..
jagdhvā māṃsamabhojyaṃ ca saptarātraṃ payaḥ pibet .. 3.234.100 ..
śuktāni ca kaṣāyām̐śca pītvāmedhyānapi dvijaḥ ..
tāvadbhavatyaprayato yāvattanna vrajatyadhaḥ .. 101 ..
3.47.d:
अपः सुराभाजनस्था मद्यभाण्डस्थितास्तथा ॥
पञ्चरात्रं वसेत्पीत्वा शङ्खपुष्पीशृतं पयः ॥95 ॥
स्पृष्ट्वा दत्त्वा च मदिरां विधिवन्प्रतिगृह्य च ॥
शूद्रोच्छिष्टाश्च पीत्वापः कुशवारि पिबेत्त्र्यहम्॥96॥
ब्राह्मणस्तु सुरापस्य गन्धमाघ्राय सोमपः ॥
प्राणानप्सु त्रिराचम्य घृतं प्राश्य विशुद्ध्यति ॥97॥
अज्ञानात्प्राश्य विण्मूत्रं सुरासंस्पृष्टमेव च ॥
पुनः संस्कारमर्हन्ति त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः॥98॥
वसनं मेखला दण्डं भैक्ष्यचर्या व्रतानि च ॥
निवर्तन्ते द्विजातीनां पुनःसंस्कारकर्मणि ॥99॥
अभोज्यानान्तु भुक्तान्नं स्त्रीशूद्रोच्छिष्टमेव च ॥
जग्ध्वा मांसमभोज्यं च सप्तरात्रं पयः पिबेत् ॥ 3.234.100 ॥
शुक्तानि च कषायाम्̐श्च पीत्वामेध्यानपि द्विजः ॥
तावद्भवत्यप्रयतो यावत्तन्न व्रजत्यधः ॥ 101 ॥
3.47.m:
Having drunk water kept in a vessel for liquor or remaining in a jar for spirits, / he should stay for five nights drinking milk boiled with śaṅkhapuṣpī.
Having touched or given wine, or having accepted it in accordance with the rule, / and having drunk water left by a śūdra, he should drink kuśa-water for three days.
A brahmin who drinks soma, having smelled the breath of a liquor-drinker, / is purified by [controlling his] breaths in water, sipping water thrice, and consuming ghee.
Having consumed feces or urine through ignorance, or [food] touched by liquor, / the three twice-born varnas require the sacrament again.
The garment, the girdle, the staff, the begging of alms, and the vows / cease for the twice-born in the rite of the renewed sacrament.
Having eaten the food of those whose food should not be eaten, or the leftovers of a woman or a śūdra, / or having consumed uneatable meat, he should drink milk for seven nights.
Having drunk fermented drinks, astringent brews, and impure [beverages], a twice-born / remains impure only for as long as that [drink] does not pass downward.

3.47.s:
viḍvarāha kharoṣṭrāṇāṃ gomāyoḥ kāpakākayoḥ ..
prāśya mūtrapurīṣāṇi dvitriścāndrāyaṇaṃ caret .. 102 ..
śuṣkāṇi bhuktvā māṃsāni bhaumāni kavakāni vā ..
ajñātaṃ caiva sūpasthaṃ caitadeva vrataṃ caret .. 103 ..
kravyādasūkarāṇāṃ ca kukkuṭānāṃ ca bhakṣaṇe ..
narakākakharāṇāñca taptakṛcchraṃ viśodhanam .. .. 104 ..
māsikānnañca yo'śnīyādavṛttyā karṣito dvijaḥ ..
sa trīṇyahānyupavasedekāhaṃ codake vaset .. 105 ..
vratacārī tu yo'śnīyānmadhumāse kathañcana ..
sa kṛtvā prākṛtaṃ kṛcchraṃ vrataśeṣaṃ samāpayet .. 106 ..
biḍālakākākhūcchiṣṭaṃ jagdhvā śvanakulasya ca..
keśakīṭāvapannañca pibedbrāhmasuvarcalam .. 107 ..
abhojyamannaṃ nāttavyaṃ cātmanaḥ śuddhimicchatā..
ajñānabhuktaṃ tūttāryaṃ śodhyaṃ vāpyāśu śodhanaiḥ .. 108 ..
3.47.d:
विड्वराह खरोष्ट्राणां गोमायोः कापकाकयोः ॥
प्राश्य मूत्रपुरीषाणि द्वित्रिश्चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥ 102 ॥
शुष्काणि भुक्त्वा मांसानि भौमानि कवकानि वा ॥
अज्ञातं चैव सूपस्थं चैतदेव व्रतं चरेत् ॥ 103 ॥
क्रव्यादसूकराणां च कुक्कुटानां च भक्षणे ॥
नरकाकखराणाञ्च तप्तकृच्छ्रं विशोधनम् ॥ ॥ 104 ॥
मासिकान्नञ्च योऽश्नीयादवृत्त्या कर्षितो द्विजः ॥
स त्रीण्यहान्युपवसेदेकाहं चोदके वसेत् ॥ 105 ॥
व्रतचारी तु योऽश्नीयान्मधुमासे कथञ्चन ॥
स कृत्वा प्राकृतं कृच्छ्रं व्रतशेषं समापयेत् ॥ 106 ॥
बिडालकाकाखूच्छिष्टं जग्ध्वा श्वनकुलस्य च॥
केशकीटावपन्नञ्च पिबेद्ब्राह्मसुवर्चलम् ॥ 107 ॥
अभोज्यमन्नं नात्तव्यं चात्मनः शुद्धिमिच्छता॥
अज्ञानभुक्तं तूत्तार्यं शोध्यं वाप्याशु शोधनैः ॥ 108 ॥
3.47.m:
Having consumed the urine and feces of a village pig, a donkey, a camel, / a jackal, a monkey, or a crow, he should perform a cāndrāyaṇa twice or thrice.
Having eaten dried meats, or mushrooms grown from the ground, / or [meat] of unknown origin lying in broth, he should perform this very vow.
For eating carnivorous animals, pigs, and cocks, / or men, crows, and donkeys, the taptakṛcchra is the purification.
And a twice-born who, distressed by lack of livelihood, eats food of a monthly ancestral rite, / should fast for three days and dwell in water for one day.
A keeper of vows who should somehow eat honey or meat / should perform an ordinary kṛcchra and then complete the remainder of the vow.
Having eaten the leftovers of a cat, a crow, a mouse, a dog, or a mongoose, / or [food] fallen upon by hair or insects, he should drink [an extract of] brāhmī and suvarcalā.
Food that is unfit to be eaten should not be consumed by one desiring purity for himself; / but if eaten through ignorance, it should be vomited out, or purified quickly by purifying rites.

3.47.s:
eṣo'nādyādanasyokto vratānāṃ vividho vidhiḥ ..
steyadoṣāpahartṝṇāṃ vratānāṃ śrūyatāṃ vidhiḥ .. 109 ..
dhānyānnadhanacauryāṇi kṛtvā kāmāddvijottamaḥ ..
svajātīyagṛhādeva kṛcchrābdena viśuddhati .. 3.234.110 ..
manuṣyāṇāntu haraṇe strīṇāṃ kṣetragṛhasya ca ..
kūpavāpījalānāñca śuddhiścāndrāyaṇaṃ smṛtam .. 111 ..
dravyāṇāmalpasārāṇāṃ steyaṃ kṛtvānyaveśmataḥ ..
caretsāntapanaṃ kṛcchrantanniryātyātmaśuddhaye .. 112 ..
bhakṣyabhojyāpaharaṇe yānaśayyāsanasya ca ..
puṣpamūlaphalānāñca pañcagavyaṃ viśodhanam.. 113 ..
tṛṇakāṣṭhadrumāṇāñca śuṣkānnasya guḍasya ca ..
cailacarmāmiṣāṇāñca trirātraṃ syādabhojanam .. 114 ..
maṇimuktāpravālānāṃ tāmrasya rajatasya ca ..
ayaḥkāṃsyopalānāñca dvādaśāhaṃ kaṇānnataḥ .. 115 ..
3.47.d:
एषोऽनाद्यादनस्योक्तो व्रतानां विविधो विधिः ॥
स्तेयदोषापहर्तॄणां व्रतानां श्रूयतां विधिः ॥ 109 ॥
धान्यान्नधनचौर्याणि कृत्वा कामाद्द्विजोत्तमः ॥
स्वजातीयगृहादेव कृच्छ्राब्देन विशुद्धति ॥ 3.234.110 ॥
मनुष्याणान्तु हरणे स्त्रीणां क्षेत्रगृहस्य च ॥
कूपवापीजलानाञ्च शुद्धिश्चान्द्रायणं स्मृतम् ॥ 111 ॥
द्रव्याणामल्पसाराणां स्तेयं कृत्वान्यवेश्मतः ॥
चरेत्सान्तपनं कृच्छ्रन्तन्निर्यात्यात्मशुद्धये ॥ 112 ॥
भक्ष्यभोज्यापहरणे यानशय्यासनस्य च ॥
पुष्पमूलफलानाञ्च पञ्चगव्यं विशोधनम्॥ 113 ॥
तृणकाष्ठद्रुमाणाञ्च शुष्कान्नस्य गुडस्य च ॥
चैलचर्मामिषाणाञ्च त्रिरात्रं स्यादभोजनम् ॥ 114 ॥
मणिमुक्ताप्रवालानां ताम्रस्य रजतस्य च ॥
अयःकांस्योपलानाञ्च द्वादशाहं कणान्नतः ॥ 115 ॥
3.47.m:
This various rule of vows has been stated for the eating of improper food. / Let the rule of vows for the removers of the sin of theft be heard.
A foremost twice-born who intentionally commits thefts of grain, cooked food, or wealth / from the house of a member of his own caste, is purified by a year-long kṛcchra.
For the abduction of men, of women, or [the theft] of a field or a house, / and of the waters of wells and tanks, the cāndrāyaṇa is remembered as the purification.
Having committed the theft of articles of small value from another's house, / he should perform the sāntapana kṛcchra after returning that [article], for his own purification.
For stealing solid or liquid food, a vehicle, a bed, or a seat, / and flowers, roots, or fruits, the five cow-products are the purification.
For [stealing] grass, wood, trees, dry food, and jaggery, / and clothes, leather, and meat, there should be fasting for three nights.
For [stealing] gems, pearls, coral, copper, and silver, / iron, bell-metal, and stones, [he should subsist] on broken grains of rice for twelve days.

3.47.s:
kārpāsakīṭajīrṇānāṃ dviśaphaikaśaphasya ca ..
pakṣigandhauṣadhīnāñca rajjvāścaiva tryahaṃ payaḥ .. 116 ..
ebhirvratairapohyeta pāpaṃ steyakṛtaṃ dvijaḥ ..
agamyagamanīyantu vratairebhirapānudet .. 117 ..
gurutalpavrataṃ kuryādretaḥ siktvā svayoniṣu ..
sakhyuḥ putrasya ca strīṣu kumārīṣvantyajāsu ca..118..
paitṛṣvasreyāṃ bhaginīṃ svasrīyāṃ mātureva ca..
mātuśca bhrāturāptasya gatvā cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret ..119..
etāḥ striyastu bhāryārthe nopayacchettu buddhimān..
jñātitvenānupeyāstāḥ patanti hyupayannadhaḥ ..3.234.120..
amānuṣīṣu puruṣa udakyāyāmayoniṣu ..
retaḥ siktvā jale caiva kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret .. 121 ..
maithunaṃ tu samāsevya puṃsi yoṣiti vā dvijaḥ ..
goyānepsu divā caiva savāsā snānamācaret .. 122 ..
3.47.d:
कार्पासकीटजीर्णानां द्विशफैकशफस्य च ॥
पक्षिगन्धौषधीनाञ्च रज्ज्वाश्चैव त्र्यहं पयः ॥ 116 ॥
एभिर्व्रतैरपोह्येत पापं स्तेयकृतं द्विजः ॥
अगम्यगमनीयन्तु व्रतैरेभिरपानुदेत् ॥ 117 ॥
गुरुतल्पव्रतं कुर्याद्रेतः सिक्त्वा स्वयोनिषु ॥
सख्युः पुत्रस्य च स्त्रीषु कुमारीष्वन्त्यजासु च॥118॥
पैतृष्वस्रेयां भगिनीं स्वस्रीयां मातुरेव च॥
मातुश्च भ्रातुराप्तस्य गत्वा चान्द्रायणं चरेत् ॥119॥
एताः स्त्रियस्तु भार्यार्थे नोपयच्छेत्तु बुद्धिमान्॥
ज्ञातित्वेनानुपेयास्ताः पतन्ति ह्युपयन्नधः ॥3.234.120॥
अमानुषीषु पुरुष उदक्यायामयोनिषु ॥
रेतः सिक्त्वा जले चैव कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं चरेत् ॥ 121 ॥
मैथुनं तु समासेव्य पुंसि योषिति वा द्विजः ॥
गोयानेप्सु दिवा चैव सवासा स्नानमाचरेत् ॥ 122 ॥
3.47.m:
For [stealing] cotton, silk, and worn garments, two-hoofed and one-hoofed animals, / birds, perfumes, medicinal herbs, and rope, [he should drink] milk for three days.
By these observances a twice-born would remove the sin committed by theft; / but one who has had intercourse with an forbidden woman should dispel it by these observances:
He should perform the observance for violating the guru's bed after discharging semen into women of his own clan, / into the wives of a friend or a son, into maidens, and into outcaste women.
Having approached the daughter of his father's sister, his sister, his sister's daughter, or [the daughter] of his mother, / or [the daughter] of a close brother of his mother, he should perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance.
A wise man should not marry these women as his wife; / they are not to be approached on account of kinship, for by marrying [them] one falls downward.
After discharging semen into non-human females, into a menstruating woman, into improper orifices, / and into water, a man should perform the santapana-kṛcchra penance.
Having engaged in sexual intercourse with a man or a woman, / in an ox-cart, in water, or by day, a twice-born should bathe with his clothes on.

3.47.s:
cāṇḍālāntya striyaṃ gatvā bhuktvā ca pratigṛhya ca ..
patatyajñānato vipro jñānātsāmyantu gacchati .. 123 ..
vipraduṣṭāṃ striyaṃ bhartā nirundhyādekaveśmani ...
yatpuṃsaḥ paradāreṣu taccaināṃ cārayedvratam..124..
sā cetpunaḥ praduṣyeta sadṛśenopayantritā..
kṛcchraṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ caiva tadasyāḥ pāvanaṃ smṛtam ..125..
yatkarotyaikarātreṇa vṛṣalīsevanaṃ dvijaḥ ..
tadbhaikṣyabhugjapannityaṃ tribhirvaṣairvyapohati ..126..
eṣā pāpakṛtāmuktā caturṇāmapi niṣkṛtiḥ ..
patitaiḥ saṃprayuktānāṃ cemāḥ śṛṇuta niṣkṛtīḥ .. 127 ..
saṃvatsareṇa patati patitena sahācaran ..
yājanādhyāpanādyaunānna tu yānāsanāśanāt .. 128 ..
yo yena patitenaivaṃ saṃsargaṃ yāti mānavaḥ ..
sa tasyaiva vrataṃ kuryāttatsaṃsargasya śuddhaye .. 129..
3.47.d:
चाण्डालान्त्य स्त्रियं गत्वा भुक्त्वा च प्रतिगृह्य च ॥
पतत्यज्ञानतो विप्रो ज्ञानात्साम्यन्तु गच्छति ॥ 123 ॥
विप्रदुष्टां स्त्रियं भर्ता निरुन्ध्यादेकवेश्मनि ॥।
यत्पुंसः परदारेषु तच्चैनां चारयेद्व्रतम्॥124॥
सा चेत्पुनः प्रदुष्येत सदृशेनोपयन्त्रिता॥
कृच्छ्रं चान्द्रायणं चैव तदस्याः पावनं स्मृतम् ॥125॥
यत्करोत्यैकरात्रेण वृषलीसेवनं द्विजः ॥
तद्भैक्ष्यभुग्जपन्नित्यं त्रिभिर्वषैर्व्यपोहति ॥126॥
एषा पापकृतामुक्ता चतुर्णामपि निष्कृतिः ॥
पतितैः संप्रयुक्तानां चेमाः शृणुत निष्कृतीः ॥ 127 ॥
संवत्सरेण पतति पतितेन सहाचरन् ॥
याजनाध्यापनाद्यौनान्न तु यानासनाशनात् ॥ 128 ॥
यो येन पतितेनैवं संसर्गं याति मानवः ॥
स तस्यैव व्रतं कुर्यात्तत्संसर्गस्य शुद्धये ॥ 129॥
3.47.m:
Having approached a Caṇḍāla or outcaste woman, eaten [her food], or accepted gifts [from her], / a brahmin falls through ignorance; through intentional action, however, he becomes equal [to her].
A husband should confine an adulterous wife in a single room; / whatever observance is [prescribed] for a man [who approaches] another's wife, he should make her perform that.
If, though restrained, she should again become unchaste with an equal, / a kṛcchra and a cāndrāyaṇa penance are traditionally taught as her purifier.
Whatever [sin] a twice-born incurs by spending a single night serving an outcaste woman, / he removes by eating begged food and reciting [prayers] constantly for three years.
This expiation has been stated for those of all four [castes] who commit sins; / hear now these expiations for those who associate with fallen persons:
Associating with a fallen person, one falls within a year / through sacrificing for him, teaching him, or matrimonial alliance, but not through riding, sitting, or eating [with him].
Whatever person enters into association with whatever fallen one in this manner, / he should perform that very one's observance for the purification of that association.

3.47.s:
patitasyodakaṃ kāryaṃ sapiṇḍairbāndhavairbahiḥ ..
nindite 'hani sāyāhne jñātyṛtviggurusannidhau .. 3.234.130 ..
dāsīghaṭamapāṃ pūrṇaṃ paryasyetpretavatsadā ..
ahorātramupāsīrannaśaucaṃ bāndhavaiḥ saha .. 131 ..
nivartayeraṃstasmāttu sambhāṣaṇasahāśane ..
dāyādasya pradānaśca yātrāmeva ca laukike ..132..
jyeṣṭhatā ca nivartteta jyeṣṭhaṃ vāpi ca yadvasu ..
jyeṣṭhāṃśaṃ prāpnuyāccāsya yavīyānguṇato'dhikaḥ .. 133..
prāyaścitte tu carite pūrṇakumbhamapāṃ navam ..
tenaiva sārdhaṃ prāśyeyuḥ snātvā puṇyajalāśaya ..134 ..
sa tvapsu taṃ ghaṭaṃ prāsya praviśya bhavanaṃ svakam ..
sarvāṇi jñātikāryāṇi yathāpūrvaṃ samācaret .. 135 ..
etameva vidhiṃ kuyārdyoṣitsu patitāsvapi ..
vastrānnapānaṃ deyaṃ tu vaseyuśca gṛhāntike .. 136 ..
3.47.d:
पतितस्योदकं कार्यं सपिण्डैर्बान्धवैर्बहिः ॥
निन्दिते ऽहनि सायाह्ने ज्ञात्यृत्विग्गुरुसन्निधौ ॥ 3.234.130 ॥
दासीघटमपां पूर्णं पर्यस्येत्प्रेतवत्सदा ॥
अहोरात्रमुपासीरन्नशौचं बान्धवैः सह ॥ 131 ॥
निवर्तयेरंस्तस्मात्तु सम्भाषणसहाशने ॥
दायादस्य प्रदानश्च यात्रामेव च लौकिके ॥132॥
ज्येष्ठता च निवर्त्तेत ज्येष्ठं वापि च यद्वसु ॥
ज्येष्ठांशं प्राप्नुयाच्चास्य यवीयान्गुणतोऽधिकः ॥ 133॥
प्रायश्चित्ते तु चरिते पूर्णकुम्भमपां नवम् ॥
तेनैव सार्धं प्राश्येयुः स्नात्वा पुण्यजलाशय ॥134 ॥
स त्वप्सु तं घटं प्रास्य प्रविश्य भवनं स्वकम् ॥
सर्वाणि ज्ञातिकार्याणि यथापूर्वं समाचरेत् ॥ 135 ॥
एतमेव विधिं कुयार्द्योषित्सु पतितास्वपि ॥
वस्त्रान्नपानं देयं तु वसेयुश्च गृहान्तिके ॥ 136 ॥
3.47.m:
The sapinda relatives should perform the water-offering for the fallen person outside, / on an inauspicious day at twilight, in the presence of relatives, officiating priests, and the guru.
A female slave should overturn a pot full of water as if he were deceased; / together with the relatives, they should observe ritual impurity for a day and a night.
From then on, they should cease conversation and eating together with him, / the bestowal of inheritance, and social interaction in worldly life.
Seniority ceases, as well as whatever wealth belongs to the eldest; / a younger [brother] superior in virtue should obtain the eldest's share of his [estate].
When the penance has been performed, however, having bathed at an auspicious reservoir of water / together with him, they should drink from a fresh pot full of water.
Throwing that pot into the water and entering his own home, / he may perform all rituals with relatives as before.
One should perform this very rule even for fallen women; / clothing, food, and drink must be given, and they should dwell near the house.

3.47.s:
enasvibhiranirṇiktairnārthaṃ kañcitsamācaret ..
kṛtanirṇejanāścainānna jugupseta karhicit ..137..
bālaghnāṃśca kṛtaghnāṃśca viśuddhānapi dharmataḥ ..
śaraṇāgatahantṝm̐śca strīhantṝm̐śca na saṃvaset..138..
yeṣāṃ dvijānāṃ sāvitrī nānūcyeta yathāvidhi ..

prāyaścittaṃ cikīrṣanti vikarmasthāstu ye dvijāḥ ..
brahmaṇā ca parityaktāsteṣāmapyetadādiśet .. 3.234.140 ..
yadgarhitenārjayanti karmaṇā brāhmaṇā dhanam ..
tasyotsargeṇa śuddhyanti japyena tapasaiva ca .. 141 ..

3.47.d:
एनस्विभिरनिर्णिक्तैर्नार्थं कञ्चित्समाचरेत् ॥
कृतनिर्णेजनाश्चैनान्न जुगुप्सेत कर्हिचित् ॥137॥
बालघ्नांश्च कृतघ्नांश्च विशुद्धानपि धर्मतः ॥
शरणागतहन्तॄम्̐श्च स्त्रीहन्तॄम्̐श्च न संवसेत्॥138॥
येषां द्विजानां सावित्री नानूच्येत यथाविधि ॥
ताम्̐श्चारयित्वा त्रीन्कृच्छ्रान्यथाविध्युपनाययेत् ॥ 139 ॥
प्रायश्चित्तं चिकीर्षन्ति विकर्मस्थास्तु ये द्विजाः ॥
ब्रह्मणा च परित्यक्तास्तेषामप्येतदादिशेत् ॥ 3.234.140 ॥
यद्गर्हितेनार्जयन्ति कर्मणा ब्राह्मणा धनम् ॥
तस्योत्सर्गेण शुद्ध्यन्ति जप्येन तपसैव च ॥ 141 ॥
जपित्वा त्रीणि सावित्र्याः सहस्राणि समाहितः ॥
मासं गोष्ठे पयः पीत्वा मुच्यतेऽसत्प्रतिग्रहात् ॥ 142 ॥
उपवासकृशन्तं तु गोव्रजात्पुनरागतम् ॥
प्रणतं परिपृच्छेयुः साम्यं सौम्येच्छसीति किम् ॥ 143 ॥
3.47.m:
One should not conduct any business with sinners who are unpurified; / but once they have performed purification, one should never despise them.
Even if purified in accordance with dharma, killers of children, the ungrateful, / killers of those seeking refuge, and killers of women—one must not live together with them.
Those twice-born to whom the Sāvitrī has not been taught according to rule, / having caused them to perform three kṛcchra penances, one should initiate according to rule.
Those twice-born who are engaged in improper acts and desire penance, / and those abandoned by the Veda, one should also prescribe this for them.
Whatever wealth brahmins acquire through reprehensible action, / they become pure by relinquishing it, by recitation of prayers, and by ascetic practice.
Having recited three thousand [verses] of the Sāvitrī with concentrated mind / and drinking milk in a cowpen for a month, one is released from improper acceptance of gifts.
When he returns from the cowpen, emaciated from fasting / and bowing down, they should ask him: 'Gentle one, do you desire equality [with us]?'

3.47.s:
satyamuktvā tu viprebhyo vikiredyavasaṅgavām ..
gobhiḥ pravartite tīrthe kuryuste'sya parigraham .. 144 ..
vrātyānāṃ yājanaṃ kṛtvā pareṣāmantyakarma va ..
abhicāramahīnaṃ ca tribhiḥ kṛcchrairviśuddhyati .. 145 ..
śaraṇāgataṃ parityajya vedaṃ viplāvya ca dvijaḥ ..
saṃvatsaraṃ yavāhārastatpāpamapasedhati .. 146 ..
śvasṛgālakharairdaṣṭo grāmyaiḥ kravyādbhireva ca ..
kharāśvoṣṭrairvarāhaiśca prāṇāyāmena śuddhyati .. 147..
ṣaṣṭhānnakālatā māsaṃ saṃhitājapa eva vā ..
homāśca sakalā nityamapāṅktyānāṃ viśodhanam .. 148 ..
uṣṭrayānaṃ samāruhya kharayānañca kāmataḥ ..
snātvā ca vipro digvāsāḥ prāṇāyāmena śuddhyati .. 149 ..
vinādbhirapsu vāpyantaḥ śarīre saṃniveśya tu ..
sacailo bahirāplutya gāmālabhya viśuddhyati .. 3.234.150 ..
3.47.d:
सत्यमुक्त्वा तु विप्रेभ्यो विकिरेद्यवसङ्गवाम् ॥
गोभिः प्रवर्तिते तीर्थे कुर्युस्तेऽस्य परिग्रहम् ॥ 144 ॥
व्रात्यानां याजनं कृत्वा परेषामन्त्यकर्म व ॥
अभिचारमहीनं च त्रिभिः कृच्छ्रैर्विशुद्ध्यति ॥ 145 ॥
शरणागतं परित्यज्य वेदं विप्लाव्य च द्विजः ॥
संवत्सरं यवाहारस्तत्पापमपसेधति ॥ 146 ॥
श्वसृगालखरैर्दष्टो ग्राम्यैः क्रव्याद्भिरेव च ॥
खराश्वोष्ट्रैर्वराहैश्च प्राणायामेन शुद्ध्यति ॥ 147॥
षष्ठान्नकालता मासं संहिताजप एव वा ॥
होमाश्च सकला नित्यमपाङ्क्त्यानां विशोधनम् ॥ 148 ॥
उष्ट्रयानं समारुह्य खरयानञ्च कामतः ॥
स्नात्वा च विप्रो दिग्वासाः प्राणायामेन शुद्ध्यति ॥ 149 ॥
विनाद्भिरप्सु वाप्यन्तः शरीरे संनिवेश्य तु ॥
सचैलो बहिराप्लुत्य गामालभ्य विशुद्ध्यति ॥ 3.234.150 ॥
3.47.m:
Having spoken the truth to the brahmins, he should scatter fodder for the cows; / at a watering place made by cows, they should receive him.
Having officiated at sacrifices for the degraded, or performed funeral rites for others, / or performed malevolent sorcery and an ahīna sacrifice, one is purified by three kṛcchra penances.
A twice-born who abandons one who has sought refuge and one who reviles the Veda / dispels that sin by subsisting on barley for a year.
Bitten by dogs, jackals, or donkeys, or by domestic carnivorous animals, / or by donkeys, horses, camels, and boars, one is purified by breath-control.
Eating only at the sixth mealtime for a month, or recitation of the Saṃhitā, / and daily oblations of all kinds are the purification of those unfit to sit in the row.
Mounting a camel cart or a donkey cart intentionally, / a brahmin, having bathed unclothed, is purified by breath-control.
Passing urine or feces without water or into water, / having plunged into water outside with his clothes on and touched a cow, he is purified.

3.47.s:
vedoditānāṃ nityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ samatikrame ..
snātakavratalope ca prāyaścittamabhojanam .. .. 151 ..
huṅkāraṃ brāhmaṇasyoktā tvaṅkāraṃ tu garīyasaḥ ..
snātvānaśnannahaḥśeṣaṃ cābhivādya prasādayet .. 152 ..
tāḍayitvā tṛṇenāpi kaṇṭhe baddhvā ca vāsasā ..
vivāde vāpi nirjitya praṇipatya prasādayet .. 153 ..
avagūrya tvabdaśataṃ sahasramabhihanya tu ..
jighāṃsayā brāhmaṇasya narakaṃ pratipadyate .. 154 ..
śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūnsaṃgṛhṇāti dvijanmanaḥ ..
tāvantyabdasahasrāṇi tatkarttā narakaṃ vaset .. 155 ..
avagūryācaretkṛcchramatikṛcchraṃ nipātane ..
kṛcchrātikṛcchraṃ kurvīta viprasyotpādya śoṇitam .. 156 ..
vedābhyāsonvahaṃ śaktyā mahāyajñakriyā kṣamā ..
nāśayantyāśu pāpāni mahāpātakajānyapi .. 157 ..
3.47.d:
वेदोदितानां नित्यानां कर्मणां समतिक्रमे ॥
स्नातकव्रतलोपे च प्रायश्चित्तमभोजनम् ॥ ॥ 151 ॥
हुङ्कारं ब्राह्मणस्योक्ता त्वङ्कारं तु गरीयसः ॥
स्नात्वानश्नन्नहःशेषं चाभिवाद्य प्रसादयेत् ॥ 152 ॥
ताडयित्वा तृणेनापि कण्ठे बद्ध्वा च वाससा ॥
विवादे वापि निर्जित्य प्रणिपत्य प्रसादयेत् ॥ 153 ॥
अवगूर्य त्वब्दशतं सहस्रमभिहन्य तु ॥
जिघांसया ब्राह्मणस्य नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 154 ॥
शोणितं यावतः पांसून्संगृह्णाति द्विजन्मनः ॥
तावन्त्यब्दसहस्राणि तत्कर्त्ता नरकं वसेत् ॥ 155 ॥
अवगूर्याचरेत्कृच्छ्रमतिकृच्छ्रं निपातने ॥
कृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रं कुर्वीत विप्रस्योत्पाद्य शोणितम् ॥ 156 ॥
वेदाभ्यासोन्वहं शक्त्या महायज्ञक्रिया क्षमा ॥
नाशयन्त्याशु पापानि महापातकजान्यपि ॥ 157 ॥
3.47.m:
In the neglect of the daily rituals prescribed by the Veda / and in the breach of the observances of a graduate, fasting is the penance.
Having said 'Hum' to a brahmin, or 'Thou' to a superior, / having bathed, not eating for the remainder of the day, and saluting him, one should propitiate him.
Having struck him even with a blade of grass, or tied him by the neck with a cloth, / or defeated him in debate, one should bow down and propitiate him.
Raising [a hand or weapon against a brahmin], one goes to hell for a hundred years; / but striking [him] with the desire to kill, for a thousand [years].
As many dust particles as the blood of a twice-born binds, / for that many thousands of years the perpetrator shall dwell in hell.
Having threatened [a brahmin], he should perform a kṛcchra; an ati-kṛcchra upon striking down; / having caused blood from a brahmin, he should perform a kṛcchrātikṛcchra.
Daily study of the Veda according to ability, performance of the great sacrifices, and forbearance / swiftly destroy even sins born of mortal sins.

3.47.s:
yathaiva tejasā vahniḥ prāptānnirdahati kṣaṇāt ..
tathā jñānāgninā pāpaṃ kṛtsnaṃ dahati vedavit .. 158 ..

anuktaśuddhiḥ pravicārya deyā ukte tathaitacca nirūpaṇīyam ..159..

3.47.d:
यथैव तेजसा वह्निः प्राप्तान्निर्दहति क्षणात् ॥
तथा ज्ञानाग्निना पापं कृत्स्नं दहति वेदवित् ॥ 158 ॥
पापानुबन्धं पुरुषस्य शक्तिं देशं च कालं च तथा विदित्वा ॥
अनुक्तशुद्धिः प्रविचार्य देया उक्ते तथैतच्च निरूपणीयम् ॥159॥
3.235
हंस उवाच ॥
इत्येतदेनसामुक्तं प्रायश्चित्तं यधाविधि ॥
अत ऊर्ध्वं रहस्यानां प्रायश्चित्तं निबोधत ॥ 1 ॥
सव्याहृतीकाप्रणवाः प्राणायामास्तु षोडश ॥
अपि भ्रूणहनं मासात्पुनन्त्यहरहः कृताः ॥ 2 ॥
कौत्सं जप्त्वाज इत्येतद्वासिष्ठं च त्र्यृचं प्रति ॥
माहित्रं शुद्धवत्यश्च सुरापोऽपि विशुध्यति ॥ 3 ॥
सकृज्जप्त्वास्यवामीयं शिवसंकल्पमेव च ॥
अपहृत्य सुवर्णं तु क्षणाद्भवति निर्मलः ॥ 4 ॥
हविष्मन्तीयमभ्यस्य न तमंह इतीति च ॥
जप्त्वा तु पौरुषं सूक्तं मुच्यते गुरुतल्पगः ॥ 5 ॥
3.47.m:
Just as fire instantly burns what it encounters through its brilliance, / so the knower of the Veda burns all sin through the fire of knowledge.
Having ascertained a man's persistence in sin, his capacity, place, and time, / purification not explicitly taught should be given upon reflection, and this must also be examined when it has been stated.
3.235
The Haṃsa said:
Thus has been spoken the expiation for sins according to rule.
Henceforth, learn the expiation for secret [sins].
Sixteen breath-controls with the vyāhṛtis and the Praṇava,
performed day after day, purify even the slayer of an embryo in a month.
Having recited the Kautsa [hymn], the one beginning with 'aja', the Vāsiṣṭha [hymn], and each triplet,
the Māhitra and the Śuddhavatīs, even a drinker of liquor is purified.
Having recited once the Asyavāmīya hymn and the Śivasaṃkalpa,
one who has stolen gold becomes stainless in an instant.
Having repeated the Haviṣmat hymn and the one beginning 'na tamaṃhaḥ',
and reciting the Puruṣasūkta, a violator of the Guru's bed is freed.

3.47.s:

japaṃstaratsamandīyaṃ pūyate mānavastryahāt ..7 ..

mantraiḥ śākalahomīyairabdaṃ hutvā ghṛtaṃ dvijaḥ ..
