3.47.d:
एनसां स्थूलसूक्ष्माणां चिकीर्षन्नपनोदनम् ॥
अपेत्यृचं जपेदब्दं यत्किञ्चेदमितीति च ॥ 6 ॥
प्रतिगृह्याप्रतिग्राह्यं भुक्त्वा चान्नं विगर्हितम् ॥
जपंस्तरत्समन्दीयं पूयते मानवस्त्र्यहात् ॥7 ॥
सोमारौद्रं तु बह्वेना मासमभ्यस्य शुध्यति ॥
स्रवन्त्यामाचरन्स्नानमर्यम्णमिति च त्यृचम् ॥ 8 ॥
अब्दार्धमिन्द्रमित्येतदेनस्वी सप्तकं जपेत् ॥
अप्रशस्तन्तु कृत्वाप्सु मासमासीत भैक्ष्यभुक् ॥ 9 ॥
मन्त्रैः शाकलहोमीयैरब्दं हुत्वा घृतं द्विजः ॥
सुगुर्वप्यपहन्त्येनो जप्त्वा वा नम इत्यृचम् ॥ 3.235.10 ॥
उपपातकसंयुक्तोनुगच्छेद्गाः समाहितः ॥
अभ्यस्याब्दं पावमानीर्भैक्ष्याहारो विशुध्यति ॥ 11 ॥
अरण्ये वा त्रिरभ्यस्य प्रयतो वेदसंहिताम् ॥
मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैः पराकैः शोधितस्त्रिभिः ॥ 12 ॥
3.47.m:
Wishing to dispel sins, gross or subtle,
one should recite for a year the verse 'apa' and that beginning 'yat kiñcedam'.
Having accepted what should not be accepted and having eaten condemned food,
a man reciting the Taratsamandı̄ya is purified in three days.
One of many sins is purified by repeating the Somāraudra hymn for a month,
bathing in a river, and [reciting] the triplet beginning 'aryamṇam'.
A sinner should recite the heptad beginning 'indram' for half a year;
having done what is blameworthy in water, he should subsist on alms for a month.
Having offered ghee for a year with the Śākalahomīya mantras,
or reciting the verse 'namaḥ', a twice-born destroys even very heavy sin.
One tainted by minor sins should follow cows with concentrated mind;
repeating the Pāvamānī hymns for a year while subsisting on alms, he is purified.
Or repeating the Vedic Saṃhitā three times in a forest, restrained,
he is freed from all sins, purified by three Parāka austerities.

3.47.s:
tryahaṃ tūpavasedyastu trirahnobhyupayannapaḥ ..
mucyate pātakaiḥ sarvaistrijapitvāghamarṣaṇam .. 13 ..
ṛksaṃhitāṃ trirabhyasya yajuṣāṃ vā samāhitaḥ ..
sāmnāṃ vā sarahasyānāṃ sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 14 ..
yadvācikaṃ tasya parasya puṃso yasminnibaddhaṃ bhuvanaṃ samagram ..
japantamoṅkāramatandritātmā pāpāni śīghraṃ prajahāti martyaḥ .. 15 ..
3.47.d:
त्र्यहं तूपवसेद्यस्तु त्रिरह्नोभ्युपयन्नपः ॥
मुच्यते पातकैः सर्वैस्त्रिजपित्वाघमर्षणम् ॥ 13 ॥
ऋक्संहितां त्रिरभ्यस्य यजुषां वा समाहितः ॥
साम्नां वा सरहस्यानां सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 14 ॥
यद्वाचिकं तस्य परस्य पुंसो यस्मिन्निबद्धं भुवनं समग्रम् ॥
जपन्तमोङ्कारमतन्द्रितात्मा पापानि शीघ्रं प्रजहाति मर्त्यः ॥ 15 ॥
3.47.m:
One who fasts for three days, going to the waters thrice a day,
is freed from all sins having recited the Aghamarṣaṇa thrice.
Repeating three times the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā or that of the Yajurvedas with concentrated mind,
or of the Sāmans along with the secret teachings, he is freed from all sins.
Which is the verbal form of that Supreme Person in whom the entire world is bound—
reciting that Oṃkāra with unflagging mind, a mortal quickly casts off sins.

3.48.s:
3.236
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
karmāṇi śrotumicchāmo yaiḥ pāpaṃ vipraṇaśyati ..
prāpnotyabhyudayaṃ caiva puruṣaḥ pakṣisattama .. 1 ..
3.48.d:
3.236
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
कर्माणि श्रोतुमिच्छामो यैः पापं विप्रणश्यति ॥
प्राप्नोत्यभ्युदयं चैव पुरुषः पक्षिसत्तम ॥ 1 ॥
3.48.m:
3.236
The sages said:
We wish to hear of the deeds by which sin is destroyed,
and a person attains prosperity, O best of birds.

3.48.s:
haṃsa uvāca ..
tryahaṃ prātastryahaṃ sāyaṃ tryahamadyādayācitam ..
tryahaṃ parañca nāśnīyātprājāpatyaṃ carandvijaḥ .. 2 ..
3.48.d:
हंस उवाच ॥
त्र्यहं प्रातस्त्र्यहं सायं त्र्यहमद्यादयाचितम् ॥
त्र्यहं परञ्च नाश्नीयात्प्राजापत्यं चरन्द्विजः ॥ 2 ॥
3.48.m:
The Haṃsa said:
For three days in the morning, for three days in the evening, for three days he should eat unasked-for food,
and for the next three days he should not eat; [thus] a twice-born performs the Prājāpatya vow.

3.48.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiḥ kuśodakam ..
ekarātropavāsaśca kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ smṛtam .. 3 ..
3.48.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिः कुशोदकम् ॥
एकरात्रोपवासश्च कृच्छ्रं सान्तपनं स्मृतम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.48.m:
Cow's urine, cow dung, milk, curd, ghee, and kuśa-grass water,
and fasting for one night: this is known as the Sāntapana penance.

3.48.s:
ekaikaṃ grāsamaśnīyāttryahāṇi trīṇi pūrvavat ..
tryahaṃ copavasedanyadatikṛcchraṃ carandvijaḥ .. 4 ..
3.48.d:
एकैकं ग्रासमश्नीयात्त्र्यहाणि त्रीणि पूर्ववत् ॥
त्र्यहं चोपवसेदन्यदतिकृच्छ्रं चरन्द्विजः ॥ 4 ॥
3.48.m:
He should eat a single mouthful for three periods of three days as before,
and fast for another three days; [thus] a twice-born performs the Atikṛcchra penance.

3.48.s:
taptakṛcchraṃ caranvipro dadhikṣīra ghṛtānilāna ..
pratitryahaṃ pibeduṣṇaṃ sakṛtsnāyī samāhitaḥ .. 5 ..
3.48.d:
तप्तकृच्छ्रं चरन्विप्रो दधिक्षीर घृतानिलान ॥
प्रतित्र्यहं पिबेदुष्णं सकृत्स्नायी समाहितः ॥ 5 ॥
3.48.m:
Performing the Taptakṛcchra penance, a brahmin should drink hot curd, milk, ghee, and air,
each for three days, bathing once a day, with concentrated mind.

3.48.s:
yatātmano'pramattasya dvādaśāhamabhojanam ..
parāko nāma kṛcchro'yaṃ sarvapāpāpanodanaḥ .. 6 ..
3.48.d:
यतात्मनोऽप्रमत्तस्य द्वादशाहमभोजनम् ॥
पराको नाम कृच्छ्रोऽयं सर्वपापापनोदनः ॥ 6 ॥
3.48.m:
Not eating for twelve days, self-controlled and heedful:
this penance called Parāka removes all sins.

3.48.s:
yathākathañcitpiṇḍānāṃ tisro'śītiḥ samāhitaḥ ..
māsenāśnanhaviṣyasya candrasyaiti salokatām .. 7 ..
3.48.d:
यथाकथञ्चित्पिण्डानां तिस्रोऽशीतिः समाहितः ॥
मासेनाश्नन्हविष्यस्य चन्द्रस्यैति सलोकताम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.48.m:
Concentrated, eating in any manner three times eighty mouthfuls
of sacrificial food over a month, he attains the world of the Moon.

3.48.s:
mahāvyāhṛtibhirhomaḥ kartavyaḥ svayamanvaham ..
ahiṃsāsatyamakrodhamārjavaṃ ca samācaret .. 8 ..
3.48.d:
महाव्याहृतिभिर्होमः कर्तव्यः स्वयमन्वहम् ॥
अहिंसासत्यमक्रोधमार्जवं च समाचरेत् ॥ 8 ॥
3.48.m:
An oblation with the Mahāvyāhṛtis should be performed by himself daily;
he should practice non-violence, truth, freedom from anger, and uprightness.

3.48.s:
trirahni trirniśāyāñca savāsā jalamāviśet ..
strīśūdrapatitāṃścaiva nābhibhāṣeta karhicit .. 9 ..
3.48.d:
त्रिरह्नि त्रिर्निशायाञ्च सवासा जलमाविशेत् ॥
स्त्रीशूद्रपतितांश्चैव नाभिभाषेत कर्हिचित् ॥ 9 ॥
3.48.m:
Thrice by day and thrice by night he should enter the water with his clothes on;
and he should never speak to women, śūdras, or fallen outcasts.

3.48.s:
sthānāsanābhyāṃ viharedaśakto'dhaḥśayīta vā ..
brahmacārī vratī ca syādgurudevadvijārcakaḥ .. .. 3.236.10 ..
3.48.d:
स्थानासनाभ्यां विहरेदशक्तोऽधःशयीत वा ॥
ब्रह्मचारी व्रती च स्याद्गुरुदेवद्विजार्चकः ॥ ॥ 3.236.10 ॥
3.48.m:
He should pass the time by standing and sitting, or if unable, he may lie on the ground;
he should be celibate, observing vows, worshipping gurus, gods, and twice-borns.

3.48.s:
sāvitrīṃ ca japennityaṃ pavitrāṇi ca śaktitaḥ ..
sarveṣveva vrateṣvevaṃ prāyaścittārthamāditaḥ .. 11 ..
3.48.d:
सावित्रीं च जपेन्नित्यं पवित्राणि च शक्तितः ॥
सर्वेष्वेव व्रतेष्वेवं प्रायश्चित्तार्थमादितः ॥ 11 ॥
3.48.m:
He should recite the Sāvitrī constantly, and purifying verses according to his capacity;
in all vows for the purpose of expiation, [the procedure is] thus from the beginning.

3.48.s:
kṛtvā pāpaṃ hi saṃtapya tasmātpāpātpramucyate ..
nainaṃ kuryāmpunariti nivṛttyā pūyate tu saḥ .. 12 ..
3.48.d:
कृत्वा पापं हि संतप्य तस्मात्पापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
नैनं कुर्याम्पुनरिति निवृत्त्या पूयते तु सः ॥ 12 ॥
3.48.m:
Indeed, having committed a sin and feeling remorse, he is freed from that sin;
he is purified by desisting, thinking: 'I shall not do this again.'

3.48.s:
khyāpanenānutāpena tapasādhyayanena ca ..
pāmakṛnmucyate pāpāttathā dānena cāparaḥ..13..
3.48.d:
ख्यापनेनानुतापेन तपसाध्ययनेन च ॥
पामकृन्मुच्यते पापात्तथा दानेन चापरः॥13॥
3.48.m:
By confession, by repentance, by ascetic austerity, and by sacred study,
a sinner is freed from sin; and another likewise by giving gifts.

3.48.s:
yasminkarmaṇyapi kṛte manasaḥ syādalāghavam ..
tasmim̐stāvattapaḥ kuryādyāvattuṣṭikaraṃ bhavet..14..
3.48.d:
यस्मिन्कर्मण्यपि कृते मनसः स्यादलाघवम् ॥
तस्मिम्̐स्तावत्तपः कुर्याद्यावत्तुष्टिकरं भवेत्॥14॥
3.48.m:
Whatever deed having been done causes unease of mind,
one should perform ascetic austerity for that until satisfaction arises.

3.48.s:
pāpasya nāśastapasā vidheyo dharmasya vṛddhistapasā vidheyā ..
pāpapraṇāśe tvatha dharmavṛddhau kāmāḥ samṛdhyanti narasya viprāḥ .. 15 ..
3.237
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
karmaṇā kena puruṣaḥ kimāpnoti mahāmate ..
etannaḥ saṃśayaṃ chindhi dvijānāṃ dvijasattama .. 1 ..
.. haṃsa uvāca ..
dānena bhogī bhavati tapasā vindate mahaḥ ..
vṛddhopasevayā viprāḥ prājño bhavati mānavaḥ .. 2 ..
yajñena lokānāpnoti pāpanāśaṃ hutena ca ..
japyena kāmānāpnoti satyena ca parāṃ gatim ..3 ..
snānena śuddhimāpnoti prāṇāyāmādviśeṣataḥ ..
dhyānena dhāraṇābhiśca padamāpnotyanuttamam ..4 ..
damena sarvamāpnoti yatkiñcinmanasecchati ..
śaucena devāḥ prīyante prīyante copavāsataḥ .. 5..
upavāsaprataptānāṃ kāmāvāptirdhruvaṃ bhavet ..
dadāti vipulānbhogānsaṃgrāmeṣvapalāyinām .. 6 ..
3.48.d:
पापस्य नाशस्तपसा विधेयो धर्मस्य वृद्धिस्तपसा विधेया ॥
पापप्रणाशे त्वथ धर्मवृद्धौ कामाः समृध्यन्ति नरस्य विप्राः ॥ 15 ॥
3.237
॥ ऋषय ऊचुः ॥ ॥
कर्मणा केन पुरुषः किमाप्नोति महामते ॥
एतन्नः संशयं छिन्धि द्विजानां द्विजसत्तम ॥ 1 ॥
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
दानेन भोगी भवति तपसा विन्दते महः ॥
वृद्धोपसेवया विप्राः प्राज्ञो भवति मानवः ॥ 2 ॥
यज्ञेन लोकानाप्नोति पापनाशं हुतेन च ॥
जप्येन कामानाप्नोति सत्येन च परां गतिम् ॥3 ॥
स्नानेन शुद्धिमाप्नोति प्राणायामाद्विशेषतः ॥
ध्यानेन धारणाभिश्च पदमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥4 ॥
दमेन सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति ॥
शौचेन देवाः प्रीयन्ते प्रीयन्ते चोपवासतः ॥ 5॥
उपवासप्रतप्तानां कामावाप्तिर्ध्रुवं भवेत् ॥
ददाति विपुलान्भोगान्संग्रामेष्वपलायिनाम् ॥ 6 ॥

3.48.s:
madhumāṃsanivṛtto'pi paraṃ saukhyamupāśnute ..
ahiṃsayā tvarogī syāddīrghāyuścāpyahiṃsayā..7..
rūpalāvaṇyasaubhāgyadhanadhānyayutaḥ sadā ..
tīrthānusaraṇādviprāḥ pāpanāśamavāpnuyāt.8..
sarvakalmaṣahīnaśca yām̐llokānmanasecchati ..
pratiśrayapradānena sthānamāpnotyanuttamam ..9..
pūjyapūjayitā viprā yaśasā yujyate naraḥ ..
abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ..3.237.10..
samaṃ kṛtvā vivardhante kīrtirāryuyaśo balam .. 11 ..
ṛtukālādṛte bhāryā tathaiva parivarjayet ..
sarvakāmānavāpnoti brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati .. 12 ..
ubhau kālau tu bhuñjānastvantarā parivarjayet ..
pānīyamapi viprendrā brāhmaṃ lokaṃ prapadyate .. 13 ..
anenaiva vidhānena deśakālāśano naraḥ ..
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti gatimāpnotyabhīpsitām .. 14 ..
3.48.d:
मधुमांसनिवृत्तोऽपि परं सौख्यमुपाश्नुते ॥
अहिंसया त्वरोगी स्याद्दीर्घायुश्चाप्यहिंसया॥7॥
रूपलावण्यसौभाग्यधनधान्ययुतः सदा ॥
तीर्थानुसरणाद्विप्राः पापनाशमवाप्नुयात्.8॥
सर्वकल्मषहीनश्च याम्̐ल्लोकान्मनसेच्छति ॥
प्रतिश्रयप्रदानेन स्थानमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥9॥
पूज्यपूजयिता विप्रा यशसा युज्यते नरः ॥
अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोपसेविनः॥3.237.10॥
समं कृत्वा विवर्धन्ते कीर्तिरार्युयशो बलम् ॥ 11 ॥
ऋतुकालादृते भार्या तथैव परिवर्जयेत् ॥
सर्वकामानवाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ॥ 12 ॥
उभौ कालौ तु भुञ्जानस्त्वन्तरा परिवर्जयेत् ॥
पानीयमपि विप्रेन्द्रा ब्राह्मं लोकं प्रपद्यते ॥ 13 ॥
अनेनैव विधानेन देशकालाशनो नरः ॥
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति गतिमाप्नोत्यभीप्सिताम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.48.m:
One who abstains from alcohol and meat also enjoys supreme happiness;
by non-violence one is free from disease, and by non-violence one gains long life.
He is constantly endowed with physical beauty, charm, good fortune, wealth, and grain;
by visiting sacred bathing places, O brahmins, one obtains destruction of sins.
Free from all defilements, whatever worlds he desires in his mind,
by giving shelter he attains the unsurpassed abode.
The man who honours those worthy of honour, O brahmins, is endowed with glory. / For one who is inclined to prostration and constantly attends upon the elders,
all together increase: fame, lifespan, glory, and strength.
Likewise, one who avoids his wife except during the fertile period / obtains all desires and goes to the world of Brahmā.
Eating at both times, but avoiding [food] in between, / even water, O foremost of brahmins, he attains the world of Brahmā.
A man who eats according to place and time by this very rule / obtains all desires and attains his wished-for state.

3.48.s:
tathā bhojanakāle tu maunaṃ yastu samācaret ..
upavāsaphalantasya pratyahaṃ bhojane smṛtam .. 15 ..
3.48.d:
तथा भोजनकाले तु मौनं यस्तु समाचरेत् ॥
उपवासफलन्तस्य प्रत्यहं भोजने स्मृतम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.48.m: Moreover, he who observes silence at the time of eating / is regarded as gaining the fruit of fasting each day with his meal.

3.48.s:
sarvānkāmānavāpnoti maunī naktāśanassakṛt ..
nāpnoti nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ nityasnāyī naro bahiḥ ..16..
3.48.d:
सर्वान्कामानवाप्नोति मौनी नक्ताशनस्सकृत् ॥
नाप्नोति नारकं दुःखं नित्यस्नायी नरो बहिः ॥16॥
3.48.m: Silent, eating only at night, he obtains all desires; / a man who constantly bathes outdoors does not encounter the suffering of hell.

3.48.s:
yo dadyādaparikliṣṭamannamadhvani vartate ..
śrāntāyādṛṣṭapūrvāya tasya puṇyaphalaṃ mahat .. 17 ..
3.48.d:
यो दद्यादपरिक्लिष्टमन्नमध्वनि वर्तते ॥
श्रान्तायादृष्टपूर्वाय तस्य पुण्यफलं महत् ॥ 17 ॥
3.48.m: Whoever gives unwearied food to someone travelling on the road, / tired and never seen before, gains great meritorious fruit.

3.48.s:
pādyamāsanamevātha dīpamannaṃ pratiśrayam ..
dadyādatithipūjārthaṃ yajñāḥ pañca sudakṣiṇāḥ.. 18 ..
3.48.d:
पाद्यमासनमेवाथ दीपमन्नं प्रतिश्रयम् ॥
दद्यादतिथिपूजार्थं यज्ञाः पञ्च सुदक्षिणाः॥ 18 ॥
3.48.m: Water for the feet, a seat, a lamp, food, and shelter: / one should provide these to honour a guest; these are five sacrifices with generous fees.

3.48.s:
cakṣurdadyānmano dadyādvācaṃ dadyācca sūnṛtām ..
anuvrajedupāsīta yajñāḥ pañca sudakṣiṇāḥ ..19..
3.48.d:
चक्षुर्दद्यान्मनो दद्याद्वाचं दद्याच्च सूनृताम् ॥
अनुव्रजेदुपासीत यज्ञाः पञ्च सुदक्षिणाः ॥19॥
3.48.m: One should offer a friendly look, one should offer a kindly mind, and one should speak truthful, pleasant speech; / one should accompany [him when leaving] and attend upon [him]: these are five sacrifices with generous fees.

3.48.s:
sthaṇḍileṣu śayānānāṃ gṛhāṇi śayanāni ca ..
cīra valkalasaṃvīta vāsāṃsyābharaṇāni ca ..3.237.20..
3.48.d:
स्थण्डिलेषु शयानानां गृहाणि शयनानि च ॥
चीर वल्कलसंवीत वासांस्याभरणानि च ॥3.237.20॥
3.48.m: For those who sleep on bare ground, houses and beds [are granted]; / for those clad in rags and bark, garments and ornaments [are granted];

3.48.s:
vāhanāsanayānāni yogātmani tapodhane ..
agnīnupaśayānasya rājapauruṣamucyate .. 21..
3.48.d:
वाहनासनयानानि योगात्मनि तपोधने ॥
अग्नीनुपशयानस्य राजपौरुषमुच्यते ॥ 21॥
3.48.m: mounts, seats, and vehicles for one whose self is in yoga and whose wealth is asceticism; / for one who sleeps beside the fires, royal prowess is declared.

3.48.s:
rasānāṃ prati saṃhāre saubhāgyamadhigacchati ..
āmiṣapratisaṃhāre sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt ..22..
3.48.d:
रसानां प्रति संहारे सौभाग्यमधिगच्छति ॥
आमिषप्रतिसंहारे सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥22॥
3.48.m: By giving up relishes, he attains good fortune; / by giving up meat, he would obtain all desires.

3.48.s:
arvākśirāstu yo lambettoyavāsaṃ ca yo vaset ..
satataṃ caikaśāyī ca labhate cepsitāṃ gatim ..23..
3.48.d:
अर्वाक्शिरास्तु यो लम्बेत्तोयवासं च यो वसेत् ॥
सततं चैकशायी च लभते चेप्सितां गतिम् ॥23॥
3.48.m: He who hangs head downwards, he who dwells in water, / and he who constantly sleeps alone, attains his desired destination.

3.48.s:
vīrāsanaṃ vīraśayyāṃ vīrasthānamupāsataḥ ..
akṣayāstasya vai lokāḥ sarvakāmapradāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 24 ..
3.48.d:
वीरासनं वीरशय्यां वीरस्थानमुपासतः ॥
अक्षयास्तस्य वै लोकाः सर्वकामप्रदाः स्मृताः ॥ 24 ॥
3.48.m: For one who practises the hero's posture, the hero's bed, and the hero's station, / imperishable worlds granting all desires are declared for him.

3.48.s:
dhanaṃ bhavati dānena maunenājñāṃ prayacchati ..
upabhogām̐śca tapasā brahmacaryeṇa jīvitam .. 25 ..
3.48.d:
धनं भवति दानेन मौनेनाज्ञां प्रयच्छति ॥
उपभोगाम्̐श्च तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण जीवितम् ॥ 25 ॥
3.48.m: Wealth comes through giving; through silence he imparts authority; / pleasures through ascetic heat, and long life through celibacy.

3.48.s:
rūpamaiśvaryamārogyamahiṃsāphalamaśnute ..
phalaṃ phalāśināṃ rājyaṃ svargaḥ parṇāśināṃ phalam ..26..
3.48.d:
रूपमैश्वर्यमारोग्यमहिंसाफलमश्नुते ॥
फलं फलाशिनां राज्यं स्वर्गः पर्णाशिनां फलम् ॥26॥
3.48.m: Beauty, sovereignty, and health he enjoys as the fruit of non-violence. / Sovereignty is the fruit for those who eat fruit; heaven is the fruit for those who eat leaves.

3.48.s:
puṣpāśināṃ tathaiśvaryaṃ dhanaṃ śākāśināṃ mahat ..
payobhakṣyā divaṃ yāṃti abbhakṣyāścāmitāṃ gatim ..27 ..
3.48.d:
पुष्पाशिनां तथैश्वर्यं धनं शाकाशिनां महत् ॥
पयोभक्ष्या दिवं यांति अब्भक्ष्याश्चामितां गतिम् ॥27 ॥
3.48.m: Sovereignty likewise for those who eat flowers; great wealth for those who eat greens. / Those who subsist on milk go to heaven, and those who subsist on water go to an immeasurable destination.

3.48.s:
daṃtolūkhaliko vipro yaścāpyuñchena jīvati ..
kāpotīñcāśrito vṛttiṃ yatheṣṭāṅgatimāpnuyāt .. 28 ..
3.48.d:
दंतोलूखलिको विप्रो यश्चाप्युञ्छेन जीवति ॥
कापोतीञ्चाश्रितो वृत्तिं यथेष्टाङ्गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 28 ॥
3.48.m: A brahmin using his teeth as a mortar, and he who lives by gleaning, / or undertakes the livelihood of a pigeon, would attain a destination as he desires.

3.48.s:
prāyopaveśanādrājyaṃ sarvatra phalamaśnute..
svargaṃ satyena labhate dīkṣayā kulamuttamam .. 29 ..
3.48.d:
प्रायोपवेशनाद्राज्यं सर्वत्र फलमश्नुते॥
स्वर्गं सत्येन लभते दीक्षया कुलमुत्तमम् ॥ 29 ॥
3.48.m: From fasting unto death, he enjoys sovereignty everywhere as the fruit; / he obtains heaven through truthfulness, and a superior lineage through consecration.

3.48.s: gavoḍhāḥ śākadīkṣāyāḥ svargakāmī tṛṇāśanaḥ ..3.237.30..
3.48.d: गवोढाः शाकदीक्षायाः स्वर्गकामी तृणाशनः ॥3.237.30॥
3.48.m: Desiring heaven, one who bears the yoke of cattle, who is consecrated to eating greens, or who eats grass,

3.48.s:
tryahastriṣavaṇaṃ snātvā vāyuṃ pītvā kratuṃ labhet ..
yajñayājī tathāpnoti yām̐llokānmanasecchati .. 31 ..
3.48.d:
त्र्यहस्त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा वायुं पीत्वा क्रतुं लभेत् ॥
यज्ञयाजी तथाप्नोति याम्̐ल्लोकान्मनसेच्छति ॥ 31 ॥
3.48.m: bathing at the three junctures of the day for three days and drinking wind, obtains [the fruit of] a sacrifice; / a performer of sacrifice likewise attains whatever worlds he desires in his mind.

3.48.s:
upavāsaṃ ca dīkṣāṃ cāpyabhiṣekaṃ ca vai dvijāḥ ..
kṛtvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi vīrasthānādviśiṣyate ..32..
3.48.d:
उपवासं च दीक्षां चाप्यभिषेकं च वै द्विजाः ॥
कृत्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि वीरस्थानाद्विशिष्यते ॥32॥
3.48.m: O twice-born, having performed fasting, consecration, and ablutions / for twelve years, he surpasses the hero's station.

3.48.s:
adhītya sarvānvedānvai sarvaduḥkhairvimucyate ..
mānasaṃ hi dhanaṃ dharmaḥ svargalokamavāpnuyāt ..33..
3.48.d:
अधीत्य सर्वान्वेदान्वै सर्वदुःखैर्विमुच्यते ॥
मानसं हि धनं धर्मः स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥33॥
3.48.m: Having studied all the Vedas, he is indeed freed from all suffering; / dharma is mental wealth; he would attain the heavenly world.

3.48.s:
yena prīṇāti pitaraṃ tena prītaḥ prajāpatiḥ..
prīṇāti mātaraṃ yena pṛthivī tena pūjitā.. 34..
3.48.d:
येन प्रीणाति पितरं तेन प्रीतः प्रजापतिः॥
प्रीणाति मातरं येन पृथिवी तेन पूजिता॥ 34॥
3.48.m: By that with which he pleases his father, Prajāpati is pleased; / by that with which he pleases his mother, the Earth is honoured.

3.48.s:
yena prīṇātyupādhyāyantena syādbrahma pūjitam..
sarve tasyādṛtā dharmā yasyaite traya ādṛtāḥ..35...
3.48.d:
येन प्रीणात्युपाध्यायन्तेन स्याद्ब्रह्म पूजितम्॥
सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः॥35॥।
3.48.m: By that with which he pleases his teacher, the Veda would be honoured; / all dharmas are revered for him by whom these three are revered.

3.48.s:
anādṛtāstu yasyaite sarvāstasyāphalāḥ kriyāḥ ..
guruśuśrūṣayā vidyā nityaṃ śrāddheṣu santatiḥ..36..
3.48.d:
अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः ॥
गुरुशुश्रूषया विद्या नित्यं श्राद्धेषु सन्ततिः॥36॥
3.48.m: For him by whom these are disregarded, all his rites are fruitless. / Knowledge comes through service to the guru, and constant progeny through ancestral rites.

3.48.s:
nityasnāyī bhaveddakṣaḥ saṃdhye tu dve japansadā..
dvijaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ dvijatvaṃ vāpi puṣkalam ..37 ..
3.48.d:
नित्यस्नायी भवेद्दक्षः संध्ये तु द्वे जपन्सदा॥
द्विजशुश्रूषया राज्यं द्विजत्वं वापि पुष्कलम् ॥37 ॥
3.48.m: One who bathes regularly should become capable, constantly reciting [mantras] at the two twilights. / Sovereignty or abundant brahminhood comes through service to the twice-born.

3.48.s:
devaśuśrūṣayā kāmānyatheṣṭānprāpnuyānnaraḥ ..
sāntvadaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvaśokaiḥ pramucyate .. 38 ..
3.48.d:
देवशुश्रूषया कामान्यथेष्टान्प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥
सान्त्वदः सर्वभूतानां सर्वशोकैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 38 ॥
3.48.m: Through service to the gods, a man would obtain desires as he wishes; / one who gives comfort to all beings is freed from all griefs.

3.48.s:
keśaśmaśrūnvārayataḥ tvagryā bhavati santatiḥ ..
gandhamālyānnivṛttyā tu kīrtirbhavati puṣkalā .. 39 ..
3.48.d:
केशश्मश्रून्वारयतः त्वग्र्या भवति सन्ततिः ॥
गन्धमाल्यान्निवृत्त्या तु कीर्तिर्भवति पुष्कला ॥ 39 ॥
3.48.m: For one who restrains his hair and beard, foremost progeny arises; / through abstention from perfume and garlands, abundant fame arises.

3.48.s:
paricaryārataḥ samyaṅ na rogaistvabhibhūyate ..
golokamāpnoti tathā gavāñca paricaryayā .. 3.237.40 ..
3.48.d:
परिचर्यारतः सम्यङ् न रोगैस्त्वभिभूयते ॥
गोलोकमाप्नोति तथा गवाञ्च परिचर्यया ॥ 3.237.40 ॥
3.48.m: One who is devoted to proper service is not overcome by illnesses; / and through service to cattle he attains the world of cows.

3.48.s:
devamālyāpanayanātpādaśaucāddvijasya tu ..
śrāntasaṃvāhanādviprāḥ sukhamatyantamaśnute .. 41 ..
3.48.d:
देवमाल्यापनयनात्पादशौचाद्द्विजस्य तु ॥
श्रान्तसंवाहनाद्विप्राः सुखमत्यन्तमश्नुते ॥ 41 ॥
3.48.m: From clearing away the god’s garlands, from washing the feet of a twice-born, / and from massaging the weary, O brahmins, he enjoys supreme happiness.

3.48.s:
jale saptasahasrāṇi ekādaśa hutāśane ..
bhṛguprapāte ca daśa saṃgrāme viṃśatistathā .. 42 ..
3.48.d:
जले सप्तसहस्राणि एकादश हुताशने ॥
भृगुप्रपाते च दश संग्रामे विंशतिस्तथा ॥ 42 ॥
3.48.m: [He rejoices for] seven thousand [years] in water, eleven [thousand] in fire, / and ten [thousand] from falling from a cliff, and twenty [thousand] in battle;

3.48.s:
naro varṣasahasrāṇi tanuṃ tyaktvā tu modate .
anāśake tu dharmajñāḥ parisaṃkhyā na vidyate .. 43 ..
3.48.d:
नरो वर्षसहस्राणि तनुं त्यक्त्वा तु मोदते ।
अनाशके तु धर्मज्ञाः परिसंख्या न विद्यते ॥ 43 ॥
3.48.m: having abandoned his body, a man rejoices for thousands of years. / But for death by starvation, O knowers of dharma, no limit is found.

3.48.s:
merau sādhayate rājyaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ bhuvi jāyate ..
mahāprasthānamāviśya yatheṣṭāṃ gatimāpnuyāt .. 44 ..
3.48.d:
मेरौ साधयते राज्यं यथेष्टं भुवि जायते ॥
महाप्रस्थानमाविश्य यथेष्टां गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 44 ॥
3.48.m: He establishes sovereignty on Meru, or is born on earth as he desires; / having entered upon the great departure, he would obtain his desired destination.

3.48.s:
vahnipraveśaniyatamamīṣṭaṃ lokamaśnute ..
vāruṇaṃ lokamāpnoti tyaktvāmbhasi tanuṃ naraḥ..45..
3.48.d:
वह्निप्रवेशनियतममीष्टं लोकमश्नुते ॥
वारुणं लोकमाप्नोति त्यक्त्वाम्भसि तनुं नरः॥45॥
3.48.m: He who is disciplined in entering fire enjoys his desired world; / a man who casts off his body in water attains the world of Varuṇa.

3.48.s:
anārto vyādhirahito na tyajedātmanastanum ..
asūryā nāma te lokā andhena tamasā vṛtāḥ ..
tām̐ste pretyābhigacchanti ye ke cātmahano janāḥ ..46..
3.48.d:
अनार्तो व्याधिरहितो न त्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम् ॥
असूर्या नाम ते लोका अन्धेन तमसा वृताः ॥
ताम्̐स्ते प्रेत्याभिगच्छन्ति ये के चात्महनो जनाः ॥46॥
3.48.m: One who is not afflicted and is free from disease must not cast off his own body. / Sunless indeed are those worlds, enveloped in blind darkness; / to them after death go those people who are slayers of the self.

3.48.s:
aniṣṭairātmano jñātvā mṛtyukālamupasthitam ..
vyādhito bhiṣajā tyaktaḥ pūrṇe cāyuṣi vāsake .. ..47..
3.48.d:
अनिष्टैरात्मनो ज्ञात्वा मृत्युकालमुपस्थितम् ॥
व्याधितो भिषजा त्यक्तः पूर्णे चायुषि वासके ॥ ॥47॥
3.48.m: Having recognised by inauspicious signs that the time of death has arrived, / sick, given up by the physician, when his lifespan has been completed,

3.48.s:
yathāgamānusāreṇa saṃtyajedātmanastanum ..
tasminkāle tanutyāgādyathoktaṃ phalamāpnuyāt ..48..
3.48.d:
यथागमानुसारेण संत्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम् ॥
तस्मिन्काले तनुत्यागाद्यथोक्तं फलमाप्नुयात् ॥48॥
3.48.m: he should cast off his own body in accordance with the scriptures. / From the abandonment of the body at that time, he would obtain the fruit as stated.

3.48.s:
āyuṣastu paraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ maraṇaṃ brāhmaṇa dvayoḥ ..
kṣatriyasya tu saṅgrāme mṛte bhartari yoṣitaḥ ..49..
3.48.d:
आयुषस्तु परं दृष्टं मरणं ब्राह्मण द्वयोः ॥
क्षत्रियस्य तु सङ्ग्रामे मृते भर्तरि योषितः ॥49॥
3.48.m: Death after the end of lifespan is seen for the two: / for a kṣatriya in battle, and for a woman when her husband has died.

3.48.s:
brāhmaṇārthe gavārthe vā yastyajedātmanastanum ..
ātmānaṃ yūpamutsṛjya sa yajño'nantadakṣiṇaḥ .. .. 3.237.50 ..
3.48.d:
ब्राह्मणार्थे गवार्थे वा यस्त्यजेदात्मनस्तनुम् ॥
आत्मानं यूपमुत्सृज्य स यज्ञोऽनन्तदक्षिणः ॥ ॥ 3.237.50 ॥
3.48.m: Whoever casts off his own body for the sake of a brahmin or for the sake of a cow, / abandoning himself as the sacrificial post, that sacrifice has infinite fees.

3.48.s:
śaṣpaṃ mṛgakharotsṛṣṭaṃ yo mṛgaiḥ saha sevate ..
dīkṣito vai mudā yuktaḥ sa gacchatyamarāvatīm .. 51 ..
3.48.d:
शष्पं मृगखरोत्सृष्टं यो मृगैः सह सेवते ॥
दीक्षितो वै मुदा युक्तः स गच्छत्यमरावतीम् ॥ 51 ॥
3.48.m: He who partakes of young grass left by deer and wild asses, together with deer, / consecrated and filled with joy, goes to Amarāvatī.

3.48.s:
rovalaṃ śīrṇaparṇaṃ vā tadvrataṃ yo niṣevate ..
śānto yo manasā nityaṃ sa gacchetparamāṅgatim .. 52 ..
3.48.d:
रोवलं शीर्णपर्णं वा तद्व्रतं यो निषेवते ॥
शान्तो यो मनसा नित्यं स गच्छेत्परमाङ्गतिम् ॥ 52 ॥
3.48.m: He who observes that vow [living on] roots or fallen leaves, / who is ever calm in mind, would go to the supreme state.

3.48.s:
vāyubhakṣyombubhakṣyo vā phalamūlāśanopi vā ..
yakṣeśaiśvaryamādāya modate'psarasāṅgaṇaiḥ .. 53 ..
3.48.d:
वायुभक्ष्योम्बुभक्ष्यो वा फलमूलाशनोपि वा ॥
यक्षेशैश्वर्यमादाय मोदतेऽप्सरसाङ्गणैः ॥ 53 ॥
3.48.m: Subsisting on wind, subsisting on water, or eating fruit and roots, / receiving the sovereignty of the lord of the yakṣas, he rejoices with hosts of apsarases.

3.48.s:
agniyogavaho grīṣme vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā ..
tīrttvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ .. 54 ..
3.48.d:
अग्नियोगवहो ग्रीष्मे विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
तीर्त्त्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि राजा भवति पार्थिवः ॥ 54 ॥
3.48.m: Enduring the yoga of the [five] fires in the summer, through rites prescribed by rule, / having crossed twelve years, he becomes an earthly king.

3.48.s:
āhāraniyamaṃ kṛtvā munirdvādaśavārṣikam ..
vrataṃ saṃsādhya kāle tu rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ .. 55 ..
3.48.d:
आहारनियमं कृत्वा मुनिर्द्वादशवार्षिकम् ॥
व्रतं संसाध्य काले तु राजा भवति पार्थिवः ॥ 55 ॥
3.48.m: The sage, having observed dietary restriction for twelve years / and having fulfilled the vow in due time, becomes an earthly king.

3.48.s:
sthaṇḍile śuddhamākāśaṃ parigṛhya samantataḥ ..
praviśya ca mudā yukto dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm .. 56 ..
3.48.d:
स्थण्डिले शुद्धमाकाशं परिगृह्य समन्ततः ॥
प्रविश्य च मुदा युक्तो दीक्षां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् ॥ 56 ॥
3.48.m: Surrounding himself completely with clear open space on a bare patch of ground, / and entering upon a twelve-year consecration with a joyful mind,

3.48.s:
sthaṇḍilasya phalānyāhuryānāni śayanāni ca ..
gṛhāṇi śayanārhāṇi candraśubhrāṇi brāhmaṇaḥ .. 57 .
3.48.d:
स्थण्डिलस्य फलान्याहुर्यानानि शयनानि च ॥
गृहाणि शयनार्हाणि चन्द्रशुभ्राणि ब्राह्मणः ॥ 57 ।
3.48.m: they say the fruits of [lying on] bare ground are vehicles and couches, / and houses worthy of reclining in, bright as the moon, O brahmin.

3.48.s:
ātmānamupajīvanyo niyato niyatāśanaḥ ..
dehaṃ cānaśane tyaktvā sa svargaṃ samupāśnute .. 58 ..
3.48.d:
आत्मानमुपजीवन्यो नियतो नियताशनः ॥
देहं चानशने त्यक्त्वा स स्वर्गं समुपाश्नुते ॥ 58 ॥
3.48.m: One who relies only on himself, restrained and of measured food, / and gives up his body through fasting, attains heaven.

3.48.s:
ātmānamupajīvanyo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm ..
aśmanā caraṇau hatvā guhyakeṣu ca modate .. 59 ..
3.48.d:
आत्मानमुपजीवन्यो दीक्षां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् ॥
अश्मना चरणौ हत्वा गुह्यकेषु च मोदते ॥ 59 ॥
3.48.m: One who relies only on himself through a twelve-year consecration, / having struck his feet with a stone, rejoices among the Guhyakas.

3.48.s:
sādhayitvātmanātmānaṃ nirdvandvo niṣparigrahaḥ ..
tīrtvā dvādaśavarṣāṇi dīkṣāmekāṃmanogatām ..
svargalokamavāpnoti devaiśca saha modate .. 3.237.60 ..
3.48.d:
साधयित्वात्मनात्मानं निर्द्वन्द्वो निष्परिग्रहः ॥
तीर्त्वा द्वादशवर्षाणि दीक्षामेकांमनोगताम् ॥
स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नोति देवैश्च सह मोदते ॥ 3.237.60 ॥
3.48.m: Having perfected the self by means of the self, free from the pairs of opposites, without possessions, / having passed through twelve years of an exclusive consecration fixed in the mind, / he reaches the heavenly world and rejoices with the gods.

3.48.s:
ātmānamupajīvanyo dīkṣāṃ dvādaśavārṣikīm ..
hutvāgnau dehamutsṛjya vahniloke mahīyate .. 61 ..
3.48.d:
आत्मानमुपजीवन्यो दीक्षां द्वादशवार्षिकीम् ॥
हुत्वाग्नौ देहमुत्सृज्य वह्निलोके महीयते ॥ 61 ॥
3.48.m: One who relies only on himself through a twelve-year consecration, / having offered himself into the fire and cast off his body, is glorified in the world of Agni.

3.48.s:
yastu vipro yathānyāyaṃ dīkṣito niyatendriyaḥ ..
ātmanyātmānamādāya nirdvandvo dharmalālasaḥ .. 62 ..
3.48.d:
यस्तु विप्रो यथान्यायं दीक्षितो नियतेन्द्रियः ॥
आत्मन्यात्मानमादाय निर्द्वन्द्वो धर्मलालसः ॥ 62 ॥
3.48.m: A wise brahmin who is consecrated according to rule, with restrained senses, / withdrawing the self into the self, free from the pairs of opposites, eager for dharma,

3.48.s:
cīrtvā dvādaśa varṣāṇi dīkṣāmetāṃ manogatām..
araṇīsahitaḥ skandhe baddhvā gacchatyanāvṛtam .. 63 ..
3.48.d:
चीर्त्वा द्वादश वर्षाणि दीक्षामेतां मनोगताम्॥
अरणीसहितः स्कन्धे बद्ध्वा गच्छत्यनावृतम् ॥ 63 ॥
3.48.m: having observed this consecration fixed in the mind for twelve years, / with fire-sticks bound upon his shoulder, goes to the unobstructed realm.

3.48.s:
vīrāddhvānamanānītya vīrāsanaratassadā ..
vīrasthāyī ca satataṃ sa vīragatimāpnuyāt .. 64 ..
3.48.d:
वीराद्ध्वानमनानीत्य वीरासनरतस्सदा ॥
वीरस्थायी च सततं स वीरगतिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 64 ॥
3.48.m: Not swerving from the path of heroes, always devoted to the hero's posture, / and ever abiding as a hero, he would attain the destiny of heroes.

3.48.s:
dhīralokagato vīro vīrayogavahaḥ sadā ..
satvasthaḥ sarvamutsṛjya dīkṣito niyataḥ śuciḥ ..
śakralokagataḥ śrīmānmodate divi devavat .. 65 ..
3.48.d:
धीरलोकगतो वीरो वीरयोगवहः सदा ॥
सत्वस्थः सर्वमुत्सृज्य दीक्षितो नियतः शुचिः ॥
शक्रलोकगतः श्रीमान्मोदते दिवि देववत् ॥ 65 ॥
3.48.m: The hero who has gone to the world of the steadfast, always maintaining heroic discipline, / established in sattva, casting aside everything, consecrated, self-controlled, pure, / having gone to Śakra's world, radiant, rejoices in heaven like a god.

3.48.s:
upavāsavratairdāntā ahiṃsāsatyavādinaḥ ..
saṃsiddhāḥ pretya gandharvaiḥ saha modantyanāmayāḥ .. 66 ..
3.48.d:
उपवासव्रतैर्दान्ता अहिंसासत्यवादिनः ॥
संसिद्धाः प्रेत्य गन्धर्वैः सह मोदन्त्यनामयाः ॥ 66 ॥
3.48.m: Subdued through vows of fasting, devoted to non-violence and speaking the truth, / perfected, free from affliction, after death they rejoice with the Gandharvas.

3.48.s:
maṇḍūkayogaśayanā yathāsthānaṃ yathāvidhi ..
dīkṣāṃ carati dharmātmā sa nāgaiḥ saha modate .. 67 ..
3.48.d:
मण्डूकयोगशयना यथास्थानं यथाविधि ॥
दीक्षां चरति धर्मात्मा स नागैः सह मोदते ॥ 67 ॥
3.48.m: Lying down in the frog posture according to place and according to rule, / the righteous one who observes this consecration rejoices with the Nāgas.

3.48.s:
ārdravāsāstu śiśire vrataṃ vahati yo naraḥ ..
dvādaśābdāni niyataṃ rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ ..68..
3.48.d:
आर्द्रवासास्तु शिशिरे व्रतं वहति यो नरः ॥
द्वादशाब्दानि नियतं राजा भवति पार्थिवः ॥68॥
3.48.m: The man who, clad in wet clothes during the cold season, bears this vow / with restraint for twelve years, becomes an earthly king.

3.48.s:
varṣarātre tathā yaśca bhavatyākāśasādhakaḥ ..
anapastīrthaśāyī ca rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ..69 ..
3.48.d:
वर्षरात्रे तथा यश्च भवत्याकाशसाधकः ॥
अनपस्तीर्थशायी च राजा भवति पार्थिवः॥69 ॥
3.48.m: And he who, during the rainy season, accomplishes [his vow] under the open sky / and lies down at a sacred ford without [shelter from] water, becomes an earthly king.

3.48.s:
tyaktvā vanagatāḥ prāṇānsaptapūrvāṃstathāparān ..
narāṃstārayitā duḥkhādātmānaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ .. 3.237.70 ..
3.48.d:
त्यक्त्वा वनगताः प्राणान्सप्तपूर्वांस्तथापरान् ॥
नरांस्तारयिता दुःखादात्मानं च विशेषतः ॥ 3.237.70 ॥
3.48.m: Having given up their life-breaths in the forest, / they deliver from suffering seven preceding generations and seven succeeding, and especially themselves.

3.48.s:
yenayena śarīreṇa yadyatkarma karoti yaḥ ..
tenatena śarīreṇa tattatphalamupāśnute .. 71 ..
3.48.d:
येनयेन शरीरेण यद्यत्कर्म करोति यः ॥
तेनतेन शरीरेण तत्तत्फलमुपाश्नुते ॥ 71 ॥
3.48.m: With whatever body one performs whatever deed, / with that very body he experiences that very fruit.

3.48.s:
yasyāṃ yasyāmavasthāyāṃ yatkaroti śubhāśubham ..
tasyāṃ tasyāmavasthāyāṃ tatphalamupāśnute .. 72 ..
3.48.d:
यस्यां यस्यामवस्थायां यत्करोति शुभाशुभम् ॥
तस्यां तस्यामवस्थायां तत्फलमुपाश्नुते ॥ 72 ॥
3.48.m: In whatever stage of life one does good or evil, / in that very stage of life he experiences its fruit.

3.48.s:
nareṇa hi kṛtaṃ karma sadā pañcendriyairiha ..
te hyasya sākṣiṇo nityaṃ ṣaṣṭha ātmā tathaiva ca .. 73 ..
3.48.d:
नरेण हि कृतं कर्म सदा पञ्चेन्द्रियैरिह ॥
ते ह्यस्य साक्षिणो नित्यं षष्ठ आत्मा तथैव च ॥ 73 ॥
3.48.m: A deed performed here by a man always through his five senses / has those very [senses] as its eternal witnesses, and the sixth is the self likewise.

3.48.s:
yathā dhenusahasreṣu vatso vindati mātaram ..
evametatkṛtaṃ karma karttāramanuvindati..74..
3.48.d:
यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् ॥
एवमेतत्कृतं कर्म कर्त्तारमनुविन्दति॥74॥
3.48.m: Just as a calf finds its mother among a thousand cows, / so this deed that was performed finds its doer.

3.48.s:
avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ vāpi tasmātsukṛtamācaret ..75..
3.48.d:
अवश्यं हि कृतं कर्म भोक्तव्यं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वापि तस्मात्सुकृतमाचरेत् ॥75॥
3.48.m: For a deed that has been done must inevitably be experienced, O foremost of the twice-born, / whether it be good or evil; therefore one should practice good deeds.

3.48.s:
acodyamānāni yathā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca ..
svakālaṃ nātivartante tathā karma purā kṛtam .. 76 ..
3.48.d:
अचोद्यमानानि यथा पुष्पाणि च फलानि च ॥
स्वकालं नातिवर्तन्ते तथा कर्म पुरा कृतम् ॥ 76 ॥
3.48.m: Just as flowers and fruits, without being urged, / do not pass by their proper season, so it is with deeds done in the past.

3.48.s:
yanmantre bhavati vṛthābhiyujyamāne yatsatye bhavati vṛthābhipūyamāne ..
yaccāgnau bhavati vṛthābhihūyamāne tatsarvaṃ bhavati vṛthābhidhīyamāne .. 77..
3.238
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
dṛṣṭāriṣṭasya bhavatā dehatyāgaḥ prakīrttitaḥ ..
tasmādasmākamācakṣva tvariṣṭāni mahāmate .. 1 ..
haṃsa uvāca ..
pravṛttervikṛtirnṝṇāṃ buddhīndriyaśarīrajā ..
akasmāddṛśyate yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ maraṇamādiśet .. 2..
etatsamāsātkathitaṃ vistaro'yamataḥ param ..
sūkṣmāriṣṭāvabodhārthaṃ tathā spaṣṭārthameva ca ..3..
na tu karmaṇi yo vyabhre prabhākarma niśābhṛtaḥ ..
chāyāṃ candrārkayorvāpi tayośca gamanaṃ tathā .. 4..
devamārge prabhā vahnerdhruvaṃ tārāmarundhatīm ..
paśyatyadṛṣṭāmanyairvā mṛtyuḥ syāttasya vatsarāt ..5 ..
saprabhānāmathānyeṣāṃ prabhāṃ yastu na paśyati ..
tasyaikādaśame māse maraṇaṃ parikīrtitam .. 6 ..
3.48.d:
यन्मन्त्रे भवति वृथाभियुज्यमाने यत्सत्ये भवति वृथाभिपूयमाने ॥
यच्चाग्नौ भवति वृथाभिहूयमाने तत्सर्वं भवति वृथाभिधीयमाने ॥ 77॥
3.238
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
दृष्टारिष्टस्य भवता देहत्यागः प्रकीर्त्तितः ॥
तस्मादस्माकमाचक्ष्व त्वरिष्टानि महामते ॥ 1 ॥
हंस उवाच ॥
प्रवृत्तेर्विकृतिर्नॄणां बुद्धीन्द्रियशरीरजा ॥
अकस्माद्दृश्यते येषां तेषां मरणमादिशेत् ॥ 2॥
एतत्समासात्कथितं विस्तरोऽयमतः परम् ॥
सूक्ष्मारिष्टावबोधार्थं तथा स्पष्टार्थमेव च ॥3॥
न तु कर्मणि यो व्यभ्रे प्रभाकर्म निशाभृतः ॥
छायां चन्द्रार्कयोर्वापि तयोश्च गमनं तथा ॥ 4॥
देवमार्गे प्रभा वह्नेर्ध्रुवं तारामरुन्धतीम् ॥
पश्यत्यदृष्टामन्यैर्वा मृत्युः स्यात्तस्य वत्सरात् ॥5 ॥
सप्रभानामथान्येषां प्रभां यस्तु न पश्यति ॥
तस्यैकादशमे मासे मरणं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 6 ॥
3.48.m:
Whatever [fault] occurs when a mantra is employed in vain, whatever occurs when truth is declared in vain, / and whatever occurs when an oblation is offered into the fire in vain—all that occurs when words are spoken in vain.
3.238 / The sages said: / The abandonment of the body was proclaimed by you for one who has seen portents of death. / Therefore, O high-minded one, declare the portents of death to us.
Haṃsa said: / When a sudden distortion of the natural functioning of men arising in the intellect, senses, or body / is observed, one should predict their death.
This has been told in brief; now follows the detailed explanation, / for the sake of understanding subtle portents of death as well as obvious ones.
He who in a cloudless sky does not see the light-action of the moon, / or the shadow of the moon and the sun, or their movement,
[or who sees] in the path of the gods the brilliance of fire, the Pole Star, the star Arundhatī, / or sees what is unseen by others, his death will occur within a year.
And he who does not see the radiance of other things that possess radiance, / his death is declared to occur in the eleventh month.

3.48.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vamate niśi ..
svapne sa māse daśame prayāti yamamandiram .. 7 ..
rakṣaḥpretapiśācānāṃ yakṣāṇāmapi darśanāt ..
atīndriyāṇāmanyeṣāṃ navame maraṇaṃ dhuvam .. 8 ..
daurbalyaṃ jāyate yasya bahusampannabhojinaḥ ..
anaśnanto'pi pīnatvamaṣṭame syātsa mṛtyubhāk .. 9..
padaṃ cāsakalaṃ yasya khaṇḍaṃ vikṛtameva vā ..
pāṃsukardamayordṛśyetsaptame māsi mṛtyubhāk ..3.238.10..
kravyādāḥ pakṣiṇo yasya mūrdhni līyanti vai dvijāḥ..
kākaśyenādayastasya paṣṭhe maraṇamādiśet.. .. 11..
yasya gomayacūrṇābhaṃ śarīrānmṛjyate rajaḥ ..
svadehacchāyāvikṛtiḥ pañcame sa tu mṛtyubhāk.. 12 ..
anabhre vidyutaṃ dṛṣṭvā caturthe mriyate dhruvam.. .. 13 ..
śakracāpaṃ jale dṛṣṭvā gaganaṃ vā dvijottamāḥ ..
avidyamānaṃ dharmajñastṛtīye mriyate dhruvam .. 14 ..
3.48.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं मूत्रं पुरीषं वमते निशि ॥
स्वप्ने स मासे दशमे प्रयाति यममन्दिरम् ॥ 7 ॥
रक्षःप्रेतपिशाचानां यक्षाणामपि दर्शनात् ॥
अतीन्द्रियाणामन्येषां नवमे मरणं धुवम् ॥ 8 ॥
दौर्बल्यं जायते यस्य बहुसम्पन्नभोजिनः ॥
अनश्नन्तोऽपि पीनत्वमष्टमे स्यात्स मृत्युभाक् ॥ 9॥
पदं चासकलं यस्य खण्डं विकृतमेव वा ॥
पांसुकर्दमयोर्दृश्येत्सप्तमे मासि मृत्युभाक् ॥3.238.10॥
क्रव्यादाः पक्षिणो यस्य मूर्ध्नि लीयन्ति वै द्विजाः॥
काकश्येनादयस्तस्य पष्ठे मरणमादिशेत्॥ ॥ 11॥
यस्य गोमयचूर्णाभं शरीरान्मृज्यते रजः ॥
स्वदेहच्छायाविकृतिः पञ्चमे स तु मृत्युभाक्॥ 12 ॥
अनभ्रे विद्युतं दृष्ट्वा चतुर्थे म्रियते ध्रुवम्॥ ॥ 13 ॥
शक्रचापं जले दृष्ट्वा गगनं वा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
अविद्यमानं धर्मज्ञस्तृतीये म्रियते ध्रुवम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.48.m:
He who in a dream at night vomits gold, silver, urine, or feces, / goes to the abode of Yama in the tenth month.
From seeing rākṣasas, the deceased, piśācas, or yakṣas, / or other beings beyond the senses, death is certain in the ninth [month].
He who grows weak though eating rich food in abundance, / or grows fat though not eating, falls into death in the eighth [month].
He whose footprint in dust or mud is seen to be incomplete, / broken, or distorted, falls into death in the seventh month.
He upon whose head carnivorous birds settle, O twice-born— / crows, hawks, and the like—for him one should predict death in the sixth [month].
He from whose body dust resembling cow-dung powder is wiped away, / and whose own shadow is distorted, falls into death in the fifth [month].
Having seen lightning in a cloudless sky, he certainly dies in the fourth [month].
Having seen a rainbow in water, or a sky that is not there, / O foremost of the twice-born, O knowers of dharma, he certainly dies in the third [month].

3.48.s:
avaghaṭṭanaṃ netrasya vinā rogaṃ yadā bhavet ..
ekasya yadi vā dṛśyetsthānabhraṃśo vidhīyate .. 15 ..
māsena vikṛtā nāsā vakrā ca maraṇapradā .. 16 ..
ardhamāsena durgandhaprabhavaṃ svaśarīrataḥ ..
paracakṣuṣi yaśchāyāmātmanastu na paśyati..
sa paśyati mahābhāgā dvādaśāhena vai yamam..17..
nirvāṇadīpagandhaṃ tu yastu nāghrāti mānavaḥ ..
saptāhena tu dharmajñāḥ paśyatyarkasutaṃ dhruvam ..18..
sadyaḥ snātānuliptasya hṛtpādaśirasā bhavet ..
kṣipraṃ saṃśoṣaṇaṃ tasya tryahānmaraṇamādiśet ..19..
gaṇḍayostilakānraktānvarṇavaikṛtameva ca ..
ahorātreṇa maraṇaṃ puruṣasya samādiśet ..3.238.20..
aṅgulibhyāntu pihite śrotre tu na śṛṇoti yaḥ .. 21 ..
śabdaṃ na paśyettu mukhaṃ nirmale darpaṇe tathā ..
paśyecca puruṣānprāptānsadyo maraṇamādiśet .. 22 ..
3.48.d:
अवघट्टनं नेत्रस्य विना रोगं यदा भवेत् ॥
एकस्य यदि वा दृश्येत्स्थानभ्रंशो विधीयते ॥ 15 ॥
मासेन विकृता नासा वक्रा च मरणप्रदा ॥ 16 ॥
अर्धमासेन दुर्गन्धप्रभवं स्वशरीरतः ॥
परचक्षुषि यश्छायामात्मनस्तु न पश्यति॥
स पश्यति महाभागा द्वादशाहेन वै यमम्॥17॥
निर्वाणदीपगन्धं तु यस्तु नाघ्राति मानवः ॥
सप्ताहेन तु धर्मज्ञाः पश्यत्यर्कसुतं ध्रुवम् ॥18॥
सद्यः स्नातानुलिप्तस्य हृत्पादशिरसा भवेत् ॥
क्षिप्रं संशोषणं तस्य त्र्यहान्मरणमादिशेत् ॥19॥
गण्डयोस्तिलकान्रक्तान्वर्णवैकृतमेव च ॥
अहोरात्रेण मरणं पुरुषस्य समादिशेत् ॥3.238.20॥
अङ्गुलिभ्यान्तु पिहिते श्रोत्रे तु न शृणोति यः ॥ 21 ॥
शब्दं न पश्येत्तु मुखं निर्मले दर्पणे तथा ॥
पश्येच्च पुरुषान्प्राप्तान्सद्यो मरणमादिशेत् ॥ 22 ॥
3.48.m:
When there is twitching of an eye without any disease, / or if one [eye] is seen displaced from its socket, [death] is ordained.
A distorted and crooked nose brings death within a month.
Within half a month [when there is] the arising of a foul stench from one's own body. / And he who does not see his own reflection in another's eye, / he sees Yama within twelve days, O fortunate ones.
The man who does not smell the scent of an extinguished lamp, / O knowers of dharma, certainly sees the son of Sūrya within seven days.
When, for one who has just bathed and been anointed, the chest, feet, and head / dry up quickly, one should predict death for him in three days.
When red spots appear on the cheeks and there is discoloration of the skin, / one should predict the death of that man within a day and night.
And he who, when both ears are closed with his fingers, does not hear [the inner sound],
sound, and does not see his face in a spotless mirror, / and sees men who have arrived, one should indicate immediate death.

3.48.s:
mūrdhadhūmavināśe tu jalārdrādvā tadudbhavet ..
nāsābhaṅgena dharmajñā dvyahānmaraṇamādiśet .. 23 ..
sparśadṛṣṭirasaprāṇaśabdaceṣṭāviparyayaḥ ..
dṛśyate tu mumūrṣūṇāṃ svasthāturaśarīriṇām .. 24 ..
ślakṣṇaṃ khagaṃ varaṃ lakṣma śītoṣṇasya viparyayaḥ ..
akasmādvetti yo dehī durlabhaṃ tasya jīvitam ..25..
toyavanmedinīṃ toyaṃ medinīmiva paśyati ..
atīndriyaṃ nirīkṣeta na vīkṣeta karasthitam .. 26 ..
pṛthivīmiva cākāśaṃ cākāśamiva medinīm ..
ākāśamiva cātmānaṃ pūrṇamindumathātithau .. 27 ..
śuklakṛṣṇaviparyāsaṃ sthūlasūkṣmaviparyayam ..
viparyāsaṃ sadasatāṃ dṛśyate jīvitakṣaye .. 28 ..

sarvathā grahaṇaṃ paśyannigrahātīndriyagrahaḥ .. 29 ..
abhakṣyalaulyamatyarthaṃ maraṇāyopajāyate ..

3.48.d:
मूर्धधूमविनाशे तु जलार्द्राद्वा तदुद्भवेत् ॥
नासाभङ्गेन धर्मज्ञा द्व्यहान्मरणमादिशेत् ॥ 23 ॥
स्पर्शदृष्टिरसप्राणशब्दचेष्टाविपर्ययः ॥
दृश्यते तु मुमूर्षूणां स्वस्थातुरशरीरिणाम् ॥ 24 ॥
श्लक्ष्णं खगं वरं लक्ष्म शीतोष्णस्य विपर्ययः ॥
अकस्माद्वेत्ति यो देही दुर्लभं तस्य जीवितम् ॥25॥
तोयवन्मेदिनीं तोयं मेदिनीमिव पश्यति ॥
अतीन्द्रियं निरीक्षेत न वीक्षेत करस्थितम् ॥ 26 ॥
पृथिवीमिव चाकाशं चाकाशमिव मेदिनीम् ॥
आकाशमिव चात्मानं पूर्णमिन्दुमथातिथौ ॥ 27 ॥
शुक्लकृष्णविपर्यासं स्थूलसूक्ष्मविपर्ययम् ॥
विपर्यासं सदसतां दृश्यते जीवितक्षये ॥ 28 ॥
षण्णां रसानां पर्यास इष्टानिष्टविपर्ययः॥
सर्वथा ग्रहणं पश्यन्निग्रहातीन्द्रियग्रहः ॥ 29 ॥
अभक्ष्यलौल्यमत्यर्थं मरणायोपजायते ॥
शोभनाशोभनघ्रेयग्रहणे तु विपर्ययः ॥ 3.238.30 ॥
3.48.m:
When the smoke from the head ceases, or if it arises from something wet with water, / [or] upon the sinking of the nose, O knowers of dharma, one should predict death in two days.
An inversion of touch, sight, taste, smell, sound, and movement / is observed in those about to die, whether healthy or afflicted with illness.
When an embodied being suddenly perceives smooth as rough, / or a reversal of cold and heat, his survival is rare.
He sees the earth like water and water like the earth; / he looks upon what is beyond the senses, but does not see what is placed in his hand.
And [he sees] space like the earth, and the earth like space; / and he sees himself like space, and the full moon on the new moon day.
An inversion of white and black, an inversion of gross and subtle, / and an inversion of the real and unreal are seen when life comes to an end.
An inversion of the six tastes, a reversal of the desirable and undesirable, / grasping in every way, seeing restraint, grasping what is beyond the senses—
excessive craving for inedible things leads to death; / and an inversion occurs in the perception of good and bad odors.

3.48.s:
iṣṭairaniṣṭaiḥ saṃyogo'niṣṭairiṣṭasamāgamaḥ ..
bhayadhairyaviparyāso jāyate prāṇasaṃkṣaye .. 31 ..
atidīrgho'tihrasvo vā satamasko'tiśītalaḥ ..
ucchvāsa prāṇasantyāge gatāsūnāṃ prajāyate .. 32 ..
anāhatānāṃ śabdaḥ syādāhatānāmaśabdatā ..
āhatānāmaśabdatvaṃ mumūrṣūṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ gṛhe .. 33 ..
udak pravṛtte divasasya nāthe puṇye dine mohavivarjitasya ..
nārāyaṇe cetasi saṃsthite vā mṛtyurbhavetpuṇyavato dvijendrāḥ .. 34 ..
3.239
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
ke doṣāḥ pāpaśamanā manuṣyāṇāṃ vināśakāḥ ..
ke guṇāśca mahādeva nityamabhyudayātmakāḥ .. 1 ..
haṃsa uvāca ..
sarveṣāmeva doṣāṇāmajñānaḥ paramo mataḥ ..
ajñaścāśraddhadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati .. 2 ..
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobho harṣo mānaḥ sadaiva ca ..
ajñānenāvṛtaṃ jantuṃ niviśante dvijottamāḥ..3..
3.48.d:
इष्टैरनिष्टैः संयोगोऽनिष्टैरिष्टसमागमः ॥
भयधैर्यविपर्यासो जायते प्राणसंक्षये ॥ 31 ॥
अतिदीर्घोऽतिह्रस्वो वा सतमस्कोऽतिशीतलः ॥
उच्छ्वास प्राणसन्त्यागे गतासूनां प्रजायते ॥ 32 ॥
अनाहतानां शब्दः स्यादाहतानामशब्दता ॥
आहतानामशब्दत्वं मुमूर्षूणां नृणां गृहे ॥ 33 ॥
उदक् प्रवृत्ते दिवसस्य नाथे पुण्ये दिने मोहविवर्जितस्य ॥
नारायणे चेतसि संस्थिते वा मृत्युर्भवेत्पुण्यवतो द्विजेन्द्राः ॥ 34 ॥
3.239
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
के दोषाः पापशमना मनुष्याणां विनाशकाः ॥
के गुणाश्च महादेव नित्यमभ्युदयात्मकाः ॥ 1 ॥
हंस उवाच ॥
सर्वेषामेव दोषाणामज्ञानः परमो मतः ॥
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्धधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ॥ 2 ॥
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभो हर्षो मानः सदैव च ॥
अज्ञानेनावृतं जन्तुं निविशन्ते द्विजोत्तमाः॥3॥
3.48.m:
Union with the undesirable [as if] desirable, union with the desirable [as if] undesirable, / and an inversion of fear and courage occurs when life comes to an end.
Extremely long or extremely short, accompanied by darkness, and very cold / becomes the exhalation of those whose life is departing, when prāṇa is abandoned.
There is sound from things unstruck, and soundlessness from struck things; / soundlessness from struck things occurs in the house of men about to die.
When the lord of day has turned north, on an auspicious day, free of delusion, / or with Nārāyaṇa abiding in his heart, death comes to a virtuous person, O chiefs of the twice-born.
3.239
The sages said:
Which faults destroy sin, and which destroy men? / And which virtues, O Mahādeva, always bring about prosperity?
Haṃsa said:
Ignorance is considered the greatest of all faults. / The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting soul perishes.
Desire, anger, greed, joyous excitement, and pride / constantly enter a creature shrouded by ignorance, O best of the twice-born.

3.48.s:
ajñānādeva pāpāni vicinotyavicakṣaṇaḥ ..
ajñānādutpathaṃ gatvā narakaṃ pratipadyate .. 4 ..

ajñānaśamane yatnastataḥ kāryo vijānatā .. 5 ..
śāstrānvavekṣaṇaṃ tasya vṛddhasevā tathaiva ca ..
tathā ca guruśuśrūṣā tvajñānaśamanī matā .. 6 ..

ato hi lokadvitayaṃ sukhārthī jñāne tu kuryātpuruṣaḥ prayatnam .. 7 ..
3.240
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
pāpena sarvaduḥkhānāṃ naro bhavati bhājanam ..
pāpena narakaṃ yāti dveṣyaśceha tathā bhavet .. .. 1 ..
naraḥ pāpasamācāraḥ pāpādapi vinaśyati ..
pāpamekaṃ paraṃ duḥkhaṃ sarveṣāṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ ..2..
kṛtapuṇyo'pi yaḥ pāpaṃ karoti puruṣaḥ kvacit ..
svarge'pi na sukhaṃ tasya tadbhayādupajāyate .. 3 ..
3.48.d:
अज्ञानादेव पापानि विचिनोत्यविचक्षणः ॥
अज्ञानादुत्पथं गत्वा नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 4 ॥
अज्ञानेनावृतो जन्तुः शुभे मार्गे न तिष्ठति ॥
अज्ञानशमने यत्नस्ततः कार्यो विजानता ॥ 5 ॥
शास्त्रान्ववेक्षणं तस्य वृद्धसेवा तथैव च ॥
तथा च गुरुशुश्रूषा त्वज्ञानशमनी मता ॥ 6 ॥
लोकद्वये नास्ति महानुभावा अज्ञानतुल्यः पुरुषस्य शत्रुः ॥
अतो हि लोकद्वितयं सुखार्थी ज्ञाने तु कुर्यात्पुरुषः प्रयत्नम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.240
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
पापेन सर्वदुःखानां नरो भवति भाजनम् ॥
पापेन नरकं याति द्वेष्यश्चेह तथा भवेत् ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
नरः पापसमाचारः पापादपि विनश्यति ॥
पापमेकं परं दुःखं सर्वेषां द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥2॥
कृतपुण्योऽपि यः पापं करोति पुरुषः क्वचित् ॥
स्वर्गेऽपि न सुखं तस्य तद्भयादुपजायते ॥ 3 ॥
3.48.m:
Only through ignorance does the undiscerning person gather sins; / having taken the wrong path through ignorance, he goes to hell.
A creature shrouded by ignorance does not stand on the auspicious path; / therefore, an effort must be made by the discerning person to calm ignorance.
Study of the scriptures, the service of elders, / and likewise devotion to the guru are deemed to pacify ignorance.
In the two worlds, O illustrious ones, there is no enemy of man equal to ignorance; / therefore, one who desires happiness in both worlds should make an effort toward knowledge.
3.240
Haṃsa said:
Through sin, a man becomes a vessel for all miseries; / through sin, he goes to hell, and becomes odious here in this world.
A man of sinful conduct perishes even from sin; / sin alone is the supreme misery of all beings, O bulls among the twice-born.
Even if a man has performed merit, if he commits a sin anywhere, / there is no happiness for him even in heaven, out of fear of that [sin].

3.48.s:
sa ekaḥ puruṣo loke yasya pāpaṃ na vidyate ..
dīnāndhakṛpaṇānāthāṃstathā ca paramārbhakāḥ .. 4..
tiryagyonigatāścānye narakeṣu tathā pare ..
sthāvarāsu ca yonīṣu tiryagyoniṣu cāpyatha .. 5 ..
vyādhibandhavadhakleśatāḍanānyapyanekaśaḥ..
naraḥ prāpnoti dharmajñastathā pāpena karmaṇā .. 6 ..
ye pāpahīnāḥ puruṣāḥ pradhānāsteṣāṃ na duḥkhaṃ bhavatīha kiñcit ..
tasmātprayatnena vivarjanīyaṃ pāpaṃ budhaiḥ puṇyacayaśca kāryaḥ .. 7 ..
3.48.d:
स एकः पुरुषो लोके यस्य पापं न विद्यते ॥
दीनान्धकृपणानाथांस्तथा च परमार्भकाः ॥ 4॥
तिर्यग्योनिगताश्चान्ये नरकेषु तथा परे ॥
स्थावरासु च योनीषु तिर्यग्योनिषु चाप्यथ ॥ 5 ॥
व्याधिबन्धवधक्लेशताडनान्यप्यनेकशः॥
नरः प्राप्नोति धर्मज्ञस्तथा पापेन कर्मणा ॥ 6 ॥
ये पापहीनाः पुरुषाः प्रधानास्तेषां न दुःखं भवतीह किञ्चित् ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन विवर्जनीयं पापं बुधैः पुण्यचयश्च कार्यः ॥ 7 ॥
3.48.m:
He alone is [fortunate] among men in this world who has no sin. / [Look at] the wretched, the blind, the miserable, the helpless, and exceedingly frail children,
and others born in animal wombs, and others in hells, / and in plant wombs, and also in animal wombs.
Diseases, imprisonment, execution, torment, and beatings many times over / a man incurs, O knower of dharma, through sinful action.
Those foremost men who are free from sin experience no suffering whatsoever here; / therefore, sin should be avoided with effort by the wise, and a store of merit should be made.

3.49.s:
3.241
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
kāmānusārī puruṣaḥ kāmādanu vinaśyati ..
yastu kevalakāmātmā so'cirādbhraśyate śriyaḥ .. 1 ..
3.49.d:
3.241
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
कामानुसारी पुरुषः कामादनु विनश्यति ॥
यस्तु केवलकामात्मा सोऽचिराद्भ्रश्यते श्रियः ॥ 1 ॥
3.49.m:
3.241
Haṃsa said:
A man who follows desire perishes following desire; / but he whose soul consists purely of desire soon falls from fortune.

3.49.s:
kāmānusārī dharmārthau na tiṣṭhati ciraṃ naraḥ ..
tasmātkāmaṃ na seveta naro dharmārthavarjitam .. 2 ..
3.49.d:
कामानुसारी धर्मार्थौ न तिष्ठति चिरं नरः ॥
तस्मात्कामं न सेवेत नरो धर्मार्थवर्जितम् ॥ 2 ॥
3.49.m: A man who follows desire does not long abide in dharma and wealth; / therefore, a man should not indulge in desire devoid of dharma and wealth.

3.49.s:
kṣayo dharmārthayoḥ kāme dhruvaṃ bhavati sevite ..
kāmāndhena vijānāti kartavyaṃ kiñcideva tu .. 3 ..
3.49.d:
क्षयो धर्मार्थयोः कामे ध्रुवं भवति सेविते ॥
कामान्धेन विजानाति कर्तव्यं किञ्चिदेव तु ॥ 3 ॥
3.49.m: The destruction of dharma and wealth is certain when desire is pursued; / blinded by desire, one hardly knows what ought to be done.

3.49.s:
paradāre tvagamye vā prapātaṃ nāvabudhyate ..
dhruvaṃ prāṇaviyoge'pi krīḍāmītyeva manyate .. 4 ..
3.49.d:
परदारे त्वगम्ये वा प्रपातं नावबुध्यते ॥
ध्रुवं प्राणवियोगेऽपि क्रीडामीत्येव मन्यते ॥ 4 ॥
3.49.m: He does not perceive the downfall in [approaching] another's wife or an forbidden woman; / even at the certain loss of his life, he thinks only, 'I am playing.'

3.49.s:
yastu kevalakāmātmā dharmārthaparivarjitam ..
kāmamāsevate nityaṃ vijñeyaḥ puruṣādhamaḥ .. 5 ..
3.49.d:
यस्तु केवलकामात्मा धर्मार्थपरिवर्जितम् ॥
काममासेवते नित्यं विज्ञेयः पुरुषाधमः ॥ 5 ॥
3.49.m: He whose soul consists purely of desire, who constantly pursues / desire devoid of dharma and wealth, is to be known as the lowest of men.

3.49.s:
dharme kṣīṇe tathaivārthe kāmamāsevite dvijaḥ ..
dhruvaṃ narakapātaḥ syānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 6 ..
3.49.d:
धर्मे क्षीणे तथैवार्थे काममासेविते द्विजः ॥
ध्रुवं नरकपातः स्यान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 6 ॥
3.49.m: When dharma and wealth are destroyed while desire is pursued, O twice-born, / falling into hell is certain; there is no doubt about this.

3.49.s:
dharmārthayuktaṃ puruṣastu kāmaṃ saṃsevamāno hi na jātu kāmaiḥ ..
viyogamāpnoti tatastu vidvāndharmārthayukte satataṃ niṣevet .. 7 ..
3.242
haṃsa uvāca ..
nātyarthaharṣaḥ kāryastu kadācidapi paṇḍitaiḥ..
atyarthahṛṣṭaḥ puruṣaḥ kāryaṃ vetti na kiñcana .. 1 ..
sampadañcañcalāṃ prāpya harṣaṃ prājño vivarjayet ..
dṛṣṭā hi bahavo naṣṭā loke sampatpralambitāḥ .. .. 2 ..
sampattau vā vipattau vā svabhāvaṃ na tyajedbudhaḥ ..
cañcalāḥ sampadaḥ sarvāḥ svabhāvādeva vai dvijāḥ .. 3 ..
kastāsāṃ viśvasetprājño veśyāsstrīṇāṃ yathā tathā ..
saṃsargānmohamāpnoti tāsāṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 4 ..
sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ ..
saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam .. 5 ..
na prajñā dhanalābhāya na jāḍyamasamṛddhaye ..
lokaparyāyavṛttāntaṃ prājño jānāti netaraḥ .. 6 ..
3.49.d:
धर्मार्थयुक्तं पुरुषस्तु कामं संसेवमानो हि न जातु कामैः ॥
वियोगमाप्नोति ततस्तु विद्वान्धर्मार्थयुक्ते सततं निषेवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.242
हंस उवाच ॥
नात्यर्थहर्षः कार्यस्तु कदाचिदपि पण्डितैः॥
अत्यर्थहृष्टः पुरुषः कार्यं वेत्ति न किञ्चन ॥ 1 ॥
सम्पदञ्चञ्चलां प्राप्य हर्षं प्राज्ञो विवर्जयेत् ॥
दृष्टा हि बहवो नष्टा लोके सम्पत्प्रलम्बिताः ॥ ॥ 2 ॥
सम्पत्तौ वा विपत्तौ वा स्वभावं न त्यजेद्बुधः ॥
चञ्चलाः सम्पदः सर्वाः स्वभावादेव वै द्विजाः ॥ 3 ॥
कस्तासां विश्वसेत्प्राज्ञो वेश्यास्स्त्रीणां यथा तथा ॥
संसर्गान्मोहमाप्नोति तासां प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥ 4 ॥
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः ॥
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम् ॥ 5 ॥
न प्रज्ञा धनलाभाय न जाड्यमसमृद्धये ॥
लोकपर्यायवृत्तान्तं प्राज्ञो जानाति नेतरः ॥ 6 ॥
3.49.m:
A man who pursues desire conjoined with dharma and wealth is never separated / from desires; therefore, a wise person should always indulge [desire] conjoined with dharma and wealth.
3.242
Haṃsa said:
Excessive joy should never be indulged in by the wise; / an excessively joyful man knows nothing of what is to be done.
Having attained unsteady fortune, the wise person should avoid excessive joy; / for many have been seen ruined in this world, deluded by fortune.
In prosperity or in adversity, the wise person should not abandon his innate nature; / all fortunes are fickle by their very nature, O twice-born.
What wise man would trust them, just as [he would not trust] courtesans? / A man incurs delusion through contact with them.
All accumulations end in exhaustion; elevations end in falling; / unions end in separation; and indeed, life ends in death.
Wisdom does not lead to wealth, nor does dullness lead to poverty. / A wise man knows the course of worldly alternation; no other does.

3.49.s:
prājñastu samyakcapalāṃ viditvā tāṃ prāpya harṣaṃ parivarjayeta ..
sampadvināśe na ca duḥkhamīyādyadbhāvi tadbhāvi na tasya nāśaḥ .. 7 ..
3.243
haṃsa uvāca..
mānaṃ vivarjitaṃ sadbhirvarjanīyaṃ sadā budhaiḥ..
mānena naṣṭā bahavo rājānaḥ saparicchadāḥ...
brāhmaṇyācca paribhraṣṭā brāhmaṇā bahavo dvijāḥ..
sarvadoṣāspadaṃ mānaṃ lokadvayavivātakam .. 2 ..
yuktāyuktaṃ na jānāti mānena puruṣādhamaḥ ..
mānagrasto naro loke gurūnapyavamanyate .. .. 3 ..
karotyakāryaṃ puruṣo mānena ca tathā dhruvam ..
mānagrāhagṛhītasya nāsti mokṣaḥ kathañcana .. 4 ..
kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca sarvajantu vināśakāḥ ..
mānagrastaṃ tu puruṣamāviśanti dvijottamāḥ .. 5 ..
mānābhibhūtaśca tathā narakaṃ pratipadyate ..
apratiṣṭhannaraśreṣṭhāstasmāttaṃ parivarjayet .. 6 ..
3.49.d:
प्राज्ञस्तु सम्यक्चपलां विदित्वा तां प्राप्य हर्षं परिवर्जयेत ॥
सम्पद्विनाशे न च दुःखमीयाद्यद्भावि तद्भावि न तस्य नाशः ॥ 7 ॥
3.243
हंस उवाच॥
मानं विवर्जितं सद्भिर्वर्जनीयं सदा बुधैः॥
मानेन नष्टा बहवो राजानः सपरिच्छदाः॥।
ब्राह्मण्याच्च परिभ्रष्टा ब्राह्मणा बहवो द्विजाः॥
सर्वदोषास्पदं मानं लोकद्वयविवातकम् ॥ 2 ॥
युक्तायुक्तं न जानाति मानेन पुरुषाधमः ॥
मानग्रस्तो नरो लोके गुरूनप्यवमन्यते ॥ ॥ 3 ॥
करोत्यकार्यं पुरुषो मानेन च तथा ध्रुवम् ॥
मानग्राहगृहीतस्य नास्ति मोक्षः कथञ्चन ॥ 4 ॥
कामः क्रोधश्च लोभश्च सर्वजन्तु विनाशकाः ॥
मानग्रस्तं तु पुरुषमाविशन्ति द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 5 ॥
मानाभिभूतश्च तथा नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
अप्रतिष्ठन्नरश्रेष्ठास्तस्मात्तं परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 6 ॥
3.49.m:
A wise man, understanding that [wealth] to be completely fickle, should avoid rejoicing upon attaining it, / and he should not feel grief at the loss of wealth. Whatever is to be, will be; there is no destruction of that.
3.243
Haṃsa said:
Pride has been avoided by the virtuous; it must always be avoided by the wise. / Through pride, many kings have perished along with their retinues, / and many brahmin twice-born have fallen from their brahminhood. / Pride is the locus of all faults, the destroyer of both worlds.
The basest of men does not distinguish the proper from the improper because of pride. / A man seized by pride disrespects even his elders in this world.
A man certainly performs wrongful acts because of pride. / For one seized by the crocodile of pride, there is no liberation whatsoever.
Desire, anger, and greed are the destroyers of all living beings; / they enter a man seized by pride, O foremost of the twice-born.
And overcome by pride, he goes to hell, / without foundation, O best of men; therefore, one should avoid it.

3.49.s:
śatrurna mānena samo'sti puṃso mānena nāśaṃ vrajatīha jantuḥ ..
māno hi tasmātparivarjanīyo budhaistu nityaṃ narakasya mārgaḥ .. 7 ..
3.244
haṃsa uvāca ..
mado vivarjitaḥ sadbhirvarjanīyaḥ prayatnataḥ ..
made tu bahavo doṣā lokadvayavivātakāḥ .. 1 ..
mattaḥ kāryaṃ na jānāti gurūnapyavamanyate ..
mattasya narakadvāraṃ nityaṃ viprāstvapāvṛtam .. 2 ..
matto bhayaṃ na jānāti maraṇe'pyatikutsite ..
matto mohasamāpanno na vijānāti kiñcana .. 3 ..
madānāmapi sarveṣāṃ jñeyaḥ pānamado'dhamaḥ ..
tenābhibhūtaḥ puruṣo na mṛtādatiricyate .. 4 ..
ajñānatulyaṃ na hi doṣamasti hetuśca tasyeha paro madaḥ syāt ..
tasmātprayatnena madasya heturnareṇa pānaṃ parivarjanīyam..5..
3.245
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
lubdho doṣānna jānāti lubdhaḥ pāpaṃ na budhyate ..
naro lobhasamāviṣṭo vaśameti tathāpadām .. 1 ..
3.49.d:
शत्रुर्न मानेन समोऽस्ति पुंसो मानेन नाशं व्रजतीह जन्तुः ॥
मानो हि तस्मात्परिवर्जनीयो बुधैस्तु नित्यं नरकस्य मार्गः ॥ 7 ॥
3.244
हंस उवाच ॥
मदो विवर्जितः सद्भिर्वर्जनीयः प्रयत्नतः ॥
मदे तु बहवो दोषा लोकद्वयविवातकाः ॥ 1 ॥
मत्तः कार्यं न जानाति गुरूनप्यवमन्यते ॥
मत्तस्य नरकद्वारं नित्यं विप्रास्त्वपावृतम् ॥ 2 ॥
मत्तो भयं न जानाति मरणेऽप्यतिकुत्सिते ॥
मत्तो मोहसमापन्नो न विजानाति किञ्चन ॥ 3 ॥
मदानामपि सर्वेषां ज्ञेयः पानमदोऽधमः ॥
तेनाभिभूतः पुरुषो न मृतादतिरिच्यते ॥ 4 ॥
अज्ञानतुल्यं न हि दोषमस्ति हेतुश्च तस्येह परो मदः स्यात् ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन मदस्य हेतुर्नरेण पानं परिवर्जनीयम्॥5॥
3.245
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
लुब्धो दोषान्न जानाति लुब्धः पापं न बुध्यते ॥
नरो लोभसमाविष्टो वशमेति तथापदाम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.49.m:
There is no enemy of man equal to pride; a creature in this world goes to destruction through pride. / Therefore, pride, the path to hell, must always be avoided by the wise.
3.244
Haṃsa said:
Intoxication has been abandoned by the virtuous; it must be avoided with effort. / In intoxication, there are many faults that destroy both worlds.
One who is intoxicated does not know his duty; he even disrespects his elders. / For the intoxicated, O brahmins, the gate to hell is always wide open.
The intoxicated does not know fear, even in a most dreadful death. / One who is intoxicated, overtaken by delusion, understands nothing.
Even among all intoxications, the intoxication from drinking is known to be the lowest. / Overpowered by it, a man is no different from a dead corpse.
There is no fault equal to ignorance, and intoxication is its supreme cause here. / Therefore, drinking, the cause of intoxication, must be avoided with effort by a man.
3.245
Haṃsa said:
The greedy man does not recognize faults; the greedy man does not realize sin. / A man possessed by greed falls under the sway of misfortunes.

3.49.s:
jīryanti jīryataḥ keśā nakhā jīryanti jīryataḥ ..
jīryanti jīryato dantāstṛṣṇā tvekā na jīryate .. 2 ..
tṛṣṇākhuniragādheyamapūrvā dvijapuṅgavāḥ..
pūryamāṇāpi satataṃ khanyate'bhyadhikaṃ tayā .. 3 ..
na tāṃ pūrayituṃ śaktaḥ kadācidapi kaścana ..
na tāṃ pūrayituṃ śaktāḥ sarve santoṣamāśritāḥ .. 4 ..
yatpṛthivyāṃ vrīhiyavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ ..
nālamekasya paryāptamiti matvā śamaṃ vrajeta .. 5 ..
yā dustyajā durmatibhiryā na jīryati jīryataḥ ..
yo'sau prāṇāntiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham .. 6 ..
lubdhasya bandhurna suto gururvā lubdhasya lokā na ca lokayātrā ..
lubdhasya doṣāḥ sakalāḥ pradiṣṭā lokadvaye duḥkhakarāḥ suraughāḥ .. 7 ..
3.49.d:
जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा नखा जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः ॥
जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतो दन्तास्तृष्णा त्वेका न जीर्यते ॥ 2 ॥
तृष्णाखुनिरगाधेयमपूर्वा द्विजपुङ्गवाः॥
पूर्यमाणापि सततं खन्यतेऽभ्यधिकं तया ॥ 3 ॥
न तां पूरयितुं शक्तः कदाचिदपि कश्चन ॥
न तां पूरयितुं शक्ताः सर्वे सन्तोषमाश्रिताः ॥ 4 ॥
यत्पृथिव्यां व्रीहियवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः ॥
नालमेकस्य पर्याप्तमिति मत्वा शमं व्रजेत ॥ 5 ॥
या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः ॥
योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् ॥ 6 ॥
लुब्धस्य बन्धुर्न सुतो गुरुर्वा लुब्धस्य लोका न च लोकयात्रा ॥
लुब्धस्य दोषाः सकलाः प्रदिष्टा लोकद्वये दुःखकराः सुरौघाः ॥ 7 ॥
3.49.m:
The hairs age as a man ages; the nails age as he ages; / the teeth age as he ages; but craving alone does not age.
This bottomless mine of craving is unprecedented, O bulls among the twice-born: / even while being filled constantly, it is dug out all the more by it.
No one is ever able to fill it. / Only those who have taken refuge in contentment are able to fulfill it.
Whatever rice, barley, gold, cattle, and women exist upon the earth— / thinking that all this is not enough for a single person, one should attain tranquility.
That which is hard to cast off by the evil-minded, which does not age as one ages, / which is a fatal disease—giving up that craving brings happiness.
The greedy man has no kinsman, no son, no elder; the greedy man has no other worlds and no livelihood. / For the greedy man, all faults are declared to cause misery in both worlds, O hosts of gods.

3.50.s:
3.246
haṃsa uvāca ..
krodha ekaḥ paraḥ śatruḥ krodha eko vināśakṛt ..
krodhābhibhūtaḥ puruṣastvātmānamapi ghātayet .. 1 ..
3.50.d:
3.246
हंस उवाच ॥
क्रोध एकः परः शत्रुः क्रोध एको विनाशकृत् ॥
क्रोधाभिभूतः पुरुषस्त्वात्मानमपि घातयेत् ॥ 1 ॥
3.50.m:
3.246
Haṃsa said:
Anger alone is the supreme enemy; anger alone is the destroyer. / A man overcome by anger would even kill himself.

3.50.s:
arthānarthau na jānāti kāryākāryau tathaiva ca ..
naraḥ krodhasamāviṣṭo nānyaṃ mitramapi dvijān .. 2 ..
3.50.d:
अर्थानर्थौ न जानाति कार्याकार्यौ तथैव च ॥
नरः क्रोधसमाविष्टो नान्यं मित्रमपि द्विजान् ॥ 2 ॥
3.50.m: He distinguishes neither benefit nor harm, nor proper action from improper action; / a man seized by anger sees no other friend, nor even brahmins, O twice-born.

3.50.s:
gurūnākṣipati krodhānnainaṃ hi namate janaḥ ..
anarthaiḥ saha saṃsargastasmātkrodhaṃ vivarjayet .. 3 ..
3.50.d:
गुरूनाक्षिपति क्रोधान्नैनं हि नमते जनः ॥
अनर्थैः सह संसर्गस्तस्मात्क्रोधं विवर्जयेत् ॥ 3 ॥
3.50.m: Out of anger, he insults his elders; people do not bow to him. / It is an association with misfortunes; therefore, one should abandon anger.

3.50.s:
krodhaṃ mūlamanarthānāṃ dvāraṃ hi narakasya ca ..
āpadāmāspadaṃ ghorantaṃ prayatnena varjayet .. 4 ..
3.50.d:
क्रोधं मूलमनर्थानां द्वारं हि नरकस्य च ॥
आपदामास्पदं घोरन्तं प्रयत्नेन वर्जयेत् ॥ 4 ॥
3.50.m: Anger is the root of calamities, the gateway to hell, / and the dreadful abode of misfortunes; one should avoid it with effort.

3.50.s:
krodhena vijito yastu kathamanyaṃ sa jeṣyati..
krodhe jite jitaṃ viddhi trailokyaṃ sacarācaram .. 5 ..
3.50.d:
क्रोधेन विजितो यस्तु कथमन्यं स जेष्यति॥
क्रोधे जिते जितं विद्धि त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.50.m: How will he conquer another who is conquered by anger? / When anger is conquered, know that the three worlds, moving and unmoving, are conquered.

3.50.s:
anarthakāriṇaṃ krodhaṃ yadā tejasvitā matā ..
krodhe doṣamataḥ kṛtvā jitaḥ krodho mahātmabhiḥ .. 6 ..
3.50.d:
अनर्थकारिणं क्रोधं यदा तेजस्विता मता ॥
क्रोधे दोषमतः कृत्वा जितः क्रोधो महात्मभिः ॥ 6 ॥
3.50.m: Since anger causes harm, even when it is considered fiery spirit, / high-souled men have conquered anger by considering it a fault.

3.50.s:
yajñaśca dānāni tapaḥ pavitraṃ tīrthopasevā ca tathaiva vedāḥ ..
krodhābhibhūtasya bhavanti mithyā narasya tasmātparivarjayettam .. 7 ..
3.247
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
sarveṣāmeva pāpānāṃ nāstikyaṃ pātakaṃ param ..
nāstikyāddhi paraṃ nāsti kiñcinpāpaṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 1 ..
akāryamiti kāryāṇi kṛtvā kāryavaśānnaraḥ ..
paścāttāpena saṃyuktaḥ kṣipraṃ pāpaṃ vyapohati .. 2 ..
kāryabuddhyā tvakāryāṇi yaḥ karoti narādhamaḥ ..
kathaṃ nivartanaṃ tebhyo jāyate tasya vai dvijāḥ .. 3..
nāstikyasya tathā mūlaṃ tvasacchāstrāvagāhanam ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena tadvivarjyaṃ vijānatā ..4..
sarvo hi mānavo loke paralokanibandhanaḥ ..
tatrāpi nirapekṣasya kinnu loke nibandhanam ..5..
ye tu vai nāstikā loke narā lokaṃ prati dvijāḥ ..
narake te hi pacyante bahukālaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ..6..
3.50.d:
यज्ञश्च दानानि तपः पवित्रं तीर्थोपसेवा च तथैव वेदाः ॥
क्रोधाभिभूतस्य भवन्ति मिथ्या नरस्य तस्मात्परिवर्जयेत्तम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.247
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
सर्वेषामेव पापानां नास्तिक्यं पातकं परम् ॥
नास्तिक्याद्धि परं नास्ति किञ्चिन्पापं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 1 ॥
अकार्यमिति कार्याणि कृत्वा कार्यवशान्नरः ॥
पश्चात्तापेन संयुक्तः क्षिप्रं पापं व्यपोहति ॥ 2 ॥
कार्यबुद्ध्या त्वकार्याणि यः करोति नराधमः ॥
कथं निवर्तनं तेभ्यो जायते तस्य वै द्विजाः ॥ 3॥
नास्तिक्यस्य तथा मूलं त्वसच्छास्त्रावगाहनम् ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तद्विवर्ज्यं विजानता ॥4॥
सर्वो हि मानवो लोके परलोकनिबन्धनः ॥
तत्रापि निरपेक्षस्य किन्नु लोके निबन्धनम् ॥5॥
ये तु वै नास्तिका लोके नरा लोकं प्रति द्विजाः ॥
नरके ते हि पच्यन्ते बहुकालं न संशयः ॥6॥
3.50.m:
Sacrifice, gifts, purifying austerities, visiting sacred places, and the Vedas / become futile for a man overcome by anger; therefore, one should avoid it.
3.247
Haṃsa said:
Of all sins, disbelief is the supreme degradation; / indeed, there is no sin greater than disbelief, O foremost of the twice-born.
A man who performs actions under the compulsion of necessity, knowing them to be forbidden, / quickly dispels the sin when accompanied by remorse.
But the lowest of men who performs forbidden acts with the notion that they are duties— / how can there be turning away from them for him, O twice-born?
The root of disbelief is immersion in false scriptures; / therefore, with all effort, it must be avoided by one who understands.
For every human in this world is bound to the other world; / and what bond can there be in this world for one who disregards even that?
Moreover, those men who are atheists regarding the world, O twice-born, / they are indeed roasted in hell for a long time, there is no doubt.

3.50.s:
nāstikyamekaṃ puruṣasya loke vināśanaṃ vipravarāḥ pradiṣṭam ..
tasmātprayatnena vivarjanīyo nāstikyabhāvaḥ sukhamīpsamānaiḥ..7..
3.248
haṃsa uvāca ..
ahaṅkārātparaṃ nāsti loke kiñcidvināśanam ..
ahaṅkāreṇa bhūpālāḥ śataśo nidhanaṅgatāḥ .. 1 ..
ahaṃkṛtāstathā naṣṭā brāhmaṇāśca sahasraśaḥ ..
mānyāmānyanna jānanti kāryākāryaṃ tvahaṃkṛtāḥ .. 2 ..
ahaṃkṛtastathā loke na vidyāmadhigacchati ..
vipannakāryaśca tathā na prājñānparipṛcchati .. 3 ..
na śṛṇoti tathānyeṣāṃ darpapūrṇo vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
pātādanyannabhaiṣajyaṃ darpānnāstyeha kīrtanam .. 4 ..
balādhikaistathā vīrairgurubhiśca tathaiva ca ..
maraṇe saṃnikṛṣṭepi maraṇasya vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 5 ..
hetubhūtāni karmāṇi ninditāni niṣevate ..
sthite sthitāṃstathā prājñānbhāṣamāṇānvinindati .. 6 ..
3.50.d:
नास्तिक्यमेकं पुरुषस्य लोके विनाशनं विप्रवराः प्रदिष्टम् ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन विवर्जनीयो नास्तिक्यभावः सुखमीप्समानैः॥7॥
3.248
हंस उवाच ॥
अहङ्कारात्परं नास्ति लोके किञ्चिद्विनाशनम् ॥
अहङ्कारेण भूपालाः शतशो निधनङ्गताः ॥ 1 ॥
अहंकृतास्तथा नष्टा ब्राह्मणाश्च सहस्रशः ॥
मान्यामान्यन्न जानन्ति कार्याकार्यं त्वहंकृताः ॥ 2 ॥
अहंकृतस्तथा लोके न विद्यामधिगच्छति ॥
विपन्नकार्यश्च तथा न प्राज्ञान्परिपृच्छति ॥ 3 ॥
न शृणोति तथान्येषां दर्पपूर्णो विचक्षणः ॥
पातादन्यन्नभैषज्यं दर्पान्नास्त्येह कीर्तनम् ॥ 4 ॥
बलाधिकैस्तथा वीरैर्गुरुभिश्च तथैव च ॥
मरणे संनिकृष्टेपि मरणस्य विचक्षणः ॥ 5 ॥
हेतुभूतानि कर्माणि निन्दितानि निषेवते ॥
स्थिते स्थितांस्तथा प्राज्ञान्भाषमाणान्विनिन्दति ॥ 6 ॥
3.50.m:
Atheism alone is declared to be the ruin of a man in this world, O best of brahmins; / therefore, the state of atheism must be avoided with exertion by those who desire happiness.
3.248
Haṃsa said:
There is nothing in the world that brings ruin greater than egoism; / through egoism, rulers of the earth have gone to their deaths by the hundreds.
Likewise, brahmins have perished by the thousands when filled with egoism; / egoistic people do not know who is venerable and who is not, nor what is to be done and what is not to be done.
Likewise, the egoistic person does not attain knowledge in the world; / and when his affairs are ruined, he does not consult the wise.
Filled with arrogance, he does not listen to others, [thinking himself] discerning; / other than a fall, there is no medicine here proclaimed for arrogance.
Even when death is near at hand, [caused] by those superior in strength, / by warriors, or likewise by elders, [thinking himself] discerning,
He indulges in blameworthy deeds that become the cause of death; / and he reviles wise men who stand firm [in virtue] as they speak.

3.50.s:
ahaṃkṛtānāṃ narake pradiṣṭā gatirdhruvaṃ lokavininditānām ..
prājñena tasmātparivarjanīyo darpo vināśaikakaraḥ sadaiva ..7..
3.249
haṃsa uvāca ..
dattaṃ yacchaucahīnena na tadgṛhṇanti devatāḥ ..
bubhutsavaśca dharmajñāḥ śucikāmāśca devatāḥ .. 1 ..
yakṣaiśca rākṣasaiścaiva piśācaiśca niśācaraiḥ ..
ḍākinībhiśca dharmajñāḥ śaucahīno'bhibhūyate .. 2 ..
śaucahīnamathābhyeti svayaṃ nindati kaṃ dvijāḥ ..
vyādhihīno hyaśaucaśca sarvairevābhibhūyate .. 3 ..

śaucahīnasya ripavo yānti vṛddhiṃ parāṃ dvijāḥ .. 4 ..

etāni yasya śaucāni sa śuciḥ parikīrtitaḥ .. 5 ..

tataścāpyadhikaṃ śaucamahiṃsā parikīrtitā .. 6 ..
3.50.d:
अहंकृतानां नरके प्रदिष्टा गतिर्ध्रुवं लोकविनिन्दितानाम् ॥
प्राज्ञेन तस्मात्परिवर्जनीयो दर्पो विनाशैककरः सदैव ॥7॥
3.249
हंस उवाच ॥
दत्तं यच्छौचहीनेन न तद्गृह्णन्ति देवताः ॥
बुभुत्सवश्च धर्मज्ञाः शुचिकामाश्च देवताः ॥ 1 ॥
यक्षैश्च राक्षसैश्चैव पिशाचैश्च निशाचरैः ॥
डाकिनीभिश्च धर्मज्ञाः शौचहीनोऽभिभूयते ॥ 2 ॥
शौचहीनमथाभ्येति स्वयं निन्दति कं द्विजाः ॥
व्याधिहीनो ह्यशौचश्च सर्वैरेवाभिभूयते ॥ 3 ॥
वर्धते च तथानर्थाः समर्थाश्च व्रजन्ति च ॥
शौचहीनस्य रिपवो यान्ति वृद्धिं परां द्विजाः ॥ 4 ॥
स्त्रीशौचमर्थशौचं च वाक्छौचमपि च द्विजाः ॥
एतानि यस्य शौचानि स शुचिः परिकीर्तितः ॥ 5 ॥
योर्थे शुचिः स हि शुचिर्न मृद्वारिशुचिः शुचिः ॥
ततश्चाप्यधिकं शौचमहिंसा परिकीर्तिता ॥ 6 ॥
3.50.m:
The destination prescribed for egoistic men, reviled by the world, is surely in hell; / therefore, arrogance, which brings only ruin, must always be avoided by the wise man.
3.249
Haṃsa said:
The deities do not accept what is given by one devoid of purity; / for the deities wish to know [the heart], O knowers of dharma, and desire purity.
By yakṣas, by rākṣasas, and by piśācas, night-wanderers, / and by ḍākinīs, O knowers of dharma, one devoid of purity is overcome.
Who does he blame when misfortune comes of its own accord to one devoid of purity, O twice-born? / Even if free from disease, one who is ritually impure is overcome by all.
Misfortunes increase, and capable [enemies] advance; / the enemies of one devoid of purity attain supreme growth, O twice-born.
Purity regarding women, purity regarding wealth, and also purity of speech, O twice-born— / he in whom these purities exist is proclaimed pure.
He who is pure in wealth is indeed pure, not he who is purified with earth and water; / and non-violence is proclaimed to be a purity even higher than that.

3.50.s:
śaucena hīnā narakaṃ vrajanti śaucena hīnā vibhajantyanarthān ..
śaucena hīnāśca bhavanti nindyāstasmādaśaucaṃ parivarjanīyam .. 7 ..
3.250
haṃsa uvāca ..
ācārahīnāḥ puruṣā bhavantyalpāyuṣo dvijāḥ ..

yakṣaiḥ piśācairgandharvaistathā cānyairniśācaraiḥ ..
ḍākinībhiḥ surāṇāṃ ca tathā pārṣagaṇāḥ pṛthaka ..2 ..

pitaraśca mahābhāga ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ .. 3 ..

3.50.d:
शौचेन हीना नरकं व्रजन्ति शौचेन हीना विभजन्त्यनर्थान् ॥
शौचेन हीनाश्च भवन्ति निन्द्यास्तस्मादशौचं परिवर्जनीयम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.250
हंस उवाच ॥
आचारहीनाः पुरुषा भवन्त्यल्पायुषो द्विजाः ॥
आचारहीनश्च तथा राक्षसैरभिभूयते ॥ 1 ॥
यक्षैः पिशाचैर्गन्धर्वैस्तथा चान्यैर्निशाचरैः ॥
डाकिनीभिः सुराणां च तथा पार्षगणाः पृथक ॥2 ॥
दत्तमाचारहीनेन न प्रतीच्छन्ति देवताः ॥
पितरश्च महाभाग ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः ॥ 3 ॥
सर्वलक्षणयुक्तोऽपि नरस्त्वाचारवर्जितः ॥
न प्राप्नोति तथा विद्यां न च किञ्चिदभीप्सितम् ॥
आचारहीनः पुरुषो नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 4 ॥
आचारहीनं न पुनन्ति वेदा यद्यप्यधीताः सह षड्भिरङ्गैः ॥
आचारहीनेन तु धर्मकार्यं कृतं हि सर्वं भवतीह मिथ्या ॥ 5 ॥
3.50.m:
Those devoid of purity go to hell; those devoid of purity share in misfortunes; / those devoid of purity become blameworthy; therefore, ritual impurity must be avoided.
3.250
Haṃsa said:
Men devoid of proper conduct become short-lived, O twice-born; / and one devoid of proper conduct is likewise overcome by rākṣasas,
By yakṣas, piśācas, gandharvas, and by other night-wanderers, / by ḍākinīs, and severally by the attendant retinues of the gods.
The deities do not accept what is given by one devoid of proper conduct, / nor do the ancestors, O fortunate one, nor the sages whose wealth is austerity.
Even a man endowed with all auspicious marks, if devoid of proper conduct, / does not attain knowledge, nor anything he desires; / a man devoid of proper conduct arrives in hell.
The Vedas do not purify one devoid of proper conduct, even if studied together with the six limbs; / for every act of dharma performed by one devoid of proper conduct becomes futile here.
